chapters.title: Chapter 2001: Ten Void Sealing Art!
paragraphs: The Unholy Trinity Body had already proved its value many times.
Without it, Max doubted his body could safely hold so many bloodlines, legacies, laws, flames, domains, and divine powers at the same time.

His Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, Voidwalker bloodline, Dimensional Keeper Legacy, Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, Devouring Flames, Primordial Flames, Dimension of Soul, Dimension of Light, and five Divine Veins should have clashed with one another long ago.
Yet somehow, his body had endured everything.
The Chaos Tree, however, remained more mysterious.
It gathered laws.
It grew branches from powers.
It produced fruits.
But Max felt there had to be something deeper behind it.
As he stared at the massive tree, a thought suddenly entered his mind.
"Since the Chaos Tree is filled with laws, maybe its true purpose will only appear when I enter the Divine Lord Realm in the future."
The more he thought about it, the more reasonable it seemed.
The Law Manifestation Realm allowed laws to appear outside the body and influence reality. The Divine Lord Realm, however, was a far higher stage.

Perhaps only when Max’s control over laws reached that level would the Chaos Tree reveal its true nature. Perhaps the tree was not only meant to produce Chaos Fruits. Perhaps it was meant to become the foundation of something much larger.
A law world.
A divine domain.
Or perhaps even something connected to the true path of the Unholy Trinity Body.
Max could not be sure.
For now, all he could do was make the best use of what he already had.
He looked at the towering Chaos Tree for a long moment before slowly exhaling.
"I hope my guess is right."
The Chaos Tree swayed gently in the silent dimension, its enormous branches moving as if answering him, but no clear response came.
Max did not mind.
One day, he would understand what it truly was.
For now, he still had one day before the meeting with the devils, and he intended to use every moment of that time to understand his new strength.
With that thought, Max stopped looking at the Chaos Tree and shifted his attention to something else.
"It is time to fully digest the Primordial Bloodline and the Voidwalker Bloodline," Max muttered.
He had awakened both bloodlines only recently, and because one event had followed another without pause, he had not gotten enough time to properly understand their true potential.

The Voidwalker inheritance had entered his body in the inheritance chamber of the Voidwalker Clan, and the Primordial Bloodline ability had awakened inside the training facility of the Primordial Race.
Both powers were now part of him, but possessing a power and mastering it were two completely different things.
Now that he had entered the Dimension of Time, he finally had enough space and time to examine them properly.
"First, the Voidwalker Bloodline," Max muttered.
The moment he said those words, blue glowing rings appeared around both of his hands.
There were five rings around each hand, making a total of ten.

The rings floated around his wrists to his shoulders with quiet precision. They were not ordinary rings made of metal or energy. Each one looked like a condensed circle of folded space, with a deep blue glow flowing along its edge. Within the center of each ring, Max could faintly see layers of darkness rotating inward, as if each ring contained a tiny sealed void.

The Voidwalker Clan, one of the original Five Sacred Clans, specialized in sealing. Their bloodline was not built for simple movement through space alone. It was also designed to lock, isolate, separate, imprison, and suppress.
Among the many arts stored inside the Voidwalker inheritance, the strongest technique was the Ten Void Sealing Art.
Ten Void Sealing Art.
According to the inheritance, a member of the Voidwalker Clan could form ten void rings and use them to seal almost anything.

A weapon, an attack, a person, a law, a domain, a space, and even a path could be sealed if the user had enough strength and understanding. However, the rings were not limited to sealing alone. Sealing was their greatest specialty, but it was not their only function.
Max willed the rings to move.

The ten void rings slipped away from his hands and floated in the air around him. They moved silently, circling his body like obedient stars. Their motion was smooth and natural, as if they were not separate tools but extensions of his bloodline.
Max then took out Dragonheart and tossed it into the air.
At the same time, he controlled one of the void rings.
The ring flew toward Dragonheart.

The moment it came close to the sword, the ring expanded slightly and released a blue transparent sphere. The sphere wrapped around Dragonheart in an instant, and the sword was sealed inside it before becoming suspended in the air.
It did not fall. It did not tremble. It simply floated there, locked inside the blue sphere as if it had been removed from normal space.
Max’s eyes lit up slightly.
"This is interesting."
He could feel that his connection to Dragonheart had been cut off.

It was not a permanent severing, but it was a true isolation. The sword was still in front of him, yet for that brief moment, it felt as though it existed in a different layer of space. If someone else’s weapon, attack, or treasure were trapped inside such a seal during battle, that person’s control over it would likely be disturbed or even completely broken.
Max waved his hand, and the seal loosened.
Dragonheart returned to him.
Then Max looked at the remaining void rings.
"Now, let us test the other uses."
One of the void rings floated back to his right wrist and settled there.
Max stretched his right hand through the ring.
Then he calmed his breathing and directed the power of his black flames into it.
The blue ring trembled.
Slowly, its glow changed.

The bright blue color darkened until the entire void ring became pitch black. Wisps of black flame appeared along its edges, but they did not spread outward. Instead, they were pulled inward again and again by the spatial compression of the ring.
The black flames, which were usually wild and devouring, became increasingly concentrated until their aura grew far denser than before.
Max looked at the ring with sharp interest.
The void ring was not only holding the flames.
It was compressing them.

chapters.title: Chapter 2002: True Use of the Ten Rings!
paragraphs: After a few moments, Max clenched his fist and slammed it into the ground.
Boom!
A violent wave of black flames erupted from his fist and spread outward.

The flames were far more concentrated than before. Their devouring power became sharper, heavier, and more explosive. The impact caused the Dimension of Time to tremble faintly, and for a moment, the surrounding space rippled from the force of the release.
Max looked at his fist in surprise.
"This is good."
The second use of the void rings was compression.

He could incorporate different elements or powers into the rings, and the rings would compress those powers to an extreme degree. Once released, the result would be far stronger than simply attacking directly with the same energy.
For someone like Max, who controlled many elements, bloodline powers, divine abilities, and pseudo cosmic paths, this function was terrifyingly useful.
He could use the void rings as amplifiers.
He could use them as seals.
He could use them as storage points for attacks.
He could even prepare different powers in different rings and release them during battle with almost no delay.
Max’s eyes became brighter.
Then he willed the black flames to disperse and began guiding the power of the seven-colored lightning into the void ring on his wrist.
The ring trembled more violently this time.

The seven-colored lightning came from Divine King Punishment, one of Max’s strongest powers. It carried judgment, destruction, punishment, and heavenly authority. The moment it entered the void ring, lightning flickered wildly in every direction, as if it refused to be restrained.
However, the void ring did not break.
It continued compressing the lightning.
Blue turned into seven colors.

The ring around Max’s wrist became a radiant circle of lightning, with arcs of seven-colored thunder snapping from its edges. The aura inside the ring grew more and more violent, and even Max felt a dangerous pressure forming around his hand.
"This is..."
Max stared at the ring in shock.
"This is deadly."
He could clearly feel that the compressed seven-colored lightning stored inside the void ring was far more violent than the black flames had been.

The black flames were terrifying because they devoured and corroded, but this lightning was different. It did not only destroy. It judged. It punished. It descended like a sentence from a divine law that allowed no resistance.
If he released the lightning from the void ring, the devastation would far exceed the previous black flame attack.
In terms of raw explosive destruction, the black flames could not compare to this compressed Divine King Punishment lightning.
Max looked down at the white floor of the Dimension of Time.
"This is dangerous," he muttered. "But I do not think my Dimension of Time is so easy to damage."
With that, he clenched his fist again.
Then he slammed it into the ground.
Boom!
A surge of seven-colored lightning exploded outward in all directions.

The force was far more terrifying than Max expected. The concentrated lightning struck the white floor, spread across the ground like a divine punishment net, and released a violent roar that shook the Dimension of Time.
For a moment, the clean white tiles beneath him turned black, as if they had been scorched by a power too fierce to be endured.
Then, only a few breaths later, the black marks faded.
The tiles returned to their original white color.
Max exhaled slowly.
"If this had been the real world, that attack would have destroyed everything around me."
There was excitement in his eyes.

The Ten Void Sealing Art was even more useful than he had first imagined. With this art, he could increase the strength of his existing attacks without needing to create entirely new techniques from scratch.
More importantly, the void rings gave him flexibility. He could store, compress, release, seal, and combine different powers depending on the situation.
However, in Max’s opinion, this was still not the most important use of the void rings.
He raised his hand.
All ten void rings began glowing as they floated around him.
A moment later, one void ring released the aura of his Emotion Severing Path. The space inside the ring became pale and sharp, as if an invisible blade had formed there.

Another void ring released seven-colored lightning in every direction, carrying the overwhelming aura of Divine King Punishment. A third void ring became darker and hotter as it carried the force of the Devouring Flames Domain.
These were his three pseudo cosmic paths.
Emotion Severing Path.
Divine King Punishment.
Devouring Flames Domain.
Max watched the rings carefully.
Then a smile slowly appeared on his face.
"So it is true."
The smile grew slightly wider.
"The void rings can carry pseudo cosmic paths and even cosmic paths."
When he first received the Voidwalker Bloodline inheritance, Max had been shocked to see this recorded inside the Ten Void Sealing Art.

According to the inheritance, the highest use of the void rings was not merely sealing objects or compressing elemental power. Their true value lay in their ability to temporarily carry a user’s cosmic path.

A true master of the Voidwalker Clan could place a cosmic path into a void ring, move it independently, use it to seal an enemy’s law, release it as an attack, or combine multiple rings to form a terrifying cosmic path formation.
At that time, Max had been skeptical.
A cosmic path was not like ordinary energy.

Even a pseudo cosmic path was the result of extreme comprehension, personal will, and the transformation of law into something far more profound. Carrying such a thing inside a ring sounded almost impossible.
But now, three of his void rings were carrying the aura of his three pseudo cosmic paths.
Only after seeing it with his own eyes did Max understand the true potential of the Ten Void Sealing Art.
His eyes became deep.

If one void ring could carry Emotion Severing Path, another could carry Divine King Punishment, and another could carry Devouring Flames Domain, then what would happen if he used all ten rings together in battle?
What if he placed black flames in one, Primordial Flames in another, seven-colored lightning in another, dimensional force in another, and a pseudo cosmic path in each of the remaining rings?
What if he formed a sealing formation with all ten?
What if he trapped an enemy inside that formation and released all the compressed powers at once?
Max’s smile became dangerous.
The Ten Void Sealing Art was not merely a defensive sealing art.
In his hands, it could become his greatest killing art.

chapters.title: Chapter 2003: Practice
paragraphs: Max continued practicing the Ten Void Sealing Art for hundreds of hours inside the Dimension of Time.

At first, the ten void rings moved around him like powerful but unfamiliar tools. They obeyed his will, but the response wasn’t perfect. Sometimes a ring lagged half a breath behind what he wanted. Sometimes the energy compressed inside a ring became unstable. Sometimes the sealing sphere formed too loose, and other times it locked so tight that even Max had to put in extra effort just to release it.
But with time, that awkwardness faded away.
One hour became ten. Ten hours became a hundred. After hundreds of hours of repeated practice, Max finally pushed the Ten Void Sealing Art to its current limit.

Now the ten void rings no longer felt like separate constructs built from his bloodline. They felt like part of his own body. With a single thought, he could summon them around his wrists, shoulders, feet, or even behind him in a rotating formation. With another thought, he could scatter them across a battlefield, hide them inside space, or attach them to an enemy’s attack before sealing it away entirely.

The more he practiced, the more Max understood why the Voidwalker Clan had once stood among the Five Sacred Clans. Their sealing arts weren’t simple restraints. They controlled distance. They controlled separation. They decided whether something stayed connected to the world or got cut off from it completely. That kind of power was terrifying.

After mastering the Ten Void Sealing Art as far as he currently could, Max also discovered that awakening the Voidwalker Bloodline had given him a lot of passive benefits beyond just the ability to form void rings or use inheritance arts. His entire body had changed in a subtle but powerful way.

Seals were now far less effective against him. Not just his body, but his blood, soul, limbs, senses, and energy circulation had all become extremely hard to seal. Ordinary sealing formations could no longer lock down his movement easily. Restraining techniques built on space, law chains, bloodline pressure, or energy isolation would lose most of their bite against him too. Unless whoever used the seal belonged to the Voidwalker Clan or carried a sealing path far above his own level, most seals would struggle to actually hold him.
Even the sealing power inside the Legacy Arena of the Four Sacred Clans wouldn’t be nearly as dangerous to him anymore.

That realization made Max’s eyes deepen. The Voidwalker Clan had been known for sealing since the age of the Five Sacred Clans. It made sense that their bloodline didn’t only let them seal others. A clan specialized in sealing would naturally build up resistance to seals too. Their bodies, bloodlines, and souls had evolved to understand exactly how seals worked, and that understanding made them extremely hard to imprison.

In a way, this passive effect might turn out even more useful than some of his direct attacks. After all, Max had plenty of enemies. Some would try to kill him. Some would try to capture him. Some would try to seal him away. Now, at least that last option had gotten a lot harder for them.
Once he finished going through the Voidwalker Bloodline, Max shifted his attention to the Primordial Bloodline.

Compared to the Voidwalker Bloodline, the Primordial Bloodline felt mysterious in a different way. It wasn’t as direct as the ten void rings. It didn’t hand him a complete inheritance art with obvious use cases. It felt broader, deeper, and far more fundamental, almost like it existed beneath all his other laws rather than sitting beside them.

Max sat cross-legged and activated the Primordial Bloodline. A deep golden aura spread through his body. The eye between his brows opened slowly, and the ancient symbols inside it rotated like a circle of dawn. The moment the eye opened, the laws around Max became clearer. Flame, lightning, space, light, darkness, ice, wind, soul, and every other law he’d touched seemed to draw closer to him.
Still, Max frowned slightly.

"Aside from feeling closer to all these different laws, I don’t notice much else changing," he muttered. "Even when I activate the Primordial Bloodline, it mostly just feels like my Pseudo Cosmic Paths and elemental attacks get ten times stronger. Other than that, it doesn’t feel as extraordinary as I expected."

That thought left him a bit confused. The Primordial Race was the strongest race in the Divine Realm, and probably the strongest in the entire universe. Their bloodline was the origin of human strength, and among every tier of Primordial Bloodline out there, Max carried the highest one, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.

A bloodline at that level shouldn’t be simple. Yet to Max, its effects still felt strangely hidden. It strengthened him a lot, sure. It brought him closer to the laws and multiplied the power of his paths and elements. It also let him awaken Primordial Flames. But compared to how mysterious the Primordials were supposed to be, Max felt like he’d only scratched the surface.
"I’ll need to ask Sarvion or one of the Primordials about this later," Max muttered.

He was sure there was more to the Primordial Bloodline than what he currently grasped. Maybe the problem wasn’t the bloodline. Maybe it was him. He’d only received the bloodline recently and hadn’t gotten a proper explanation of how Primordials actually used it. He was treating it like just another power stacked onto his body, but maybe the Primordial Bloodline needed to be understood as a foundation that transformed all his other powers rather than as a separate ability on its own.
Either way, thinking about it without guidance wouldn’t give him answers right away. So Max stopped dwelling on it and started practicing with the Primordial Flames instead.

The golden flame appeared above his palm the moment the eye between his brows opened. It burned quietly, pure and ancient, without the wild hunger of his black flames. Max controlled it carefully at first, shaping it into threads, blades, spheres, waves, and thin layers that wrapped his fists. The more he practiced, the more he understood its nature.

Now, at least that last option had gotten a lot harder for them.
Once he finished going through the Voidwalker Bloodline, Max shifted his attention to the Primordial Bloodline.
Compared to the Voidwalker Bloodline, the Primordial Bloodline felt mysterious in a different way.
It wasn’t as direct as the ten void rings.
It didn’t hand him a complete inheritance art with obvious use cases.
It felt broader, deeper, and far more fundamental, almost like it existed beneath all his other laws rather than sitting beside them.
Max sat cross-legged and activated the Primordial Bloodline.
A deep golden aura spread through his body.
The eye between his brows opened slowly, and the ancient symbols inside it rotated like a circle of dawn.
The moment the eye opened, the laws around Max became clearer.
Flame, lightning, space, light, darkness, ice, wind, soul, and every other law he’d touched seemed to draw closer to him.
Still, Max frowned slightly.
"Aside from feeling closer to all these different laws, I don’t notice much else changing," he muttered.
"Even when I activate the Primordial Bloodline, it mostly just feels like my Pseudo Cosmic Paths and elemental attacks get ten times stronger.
Other than that, it doesn’t feel as extraordinary as I expected."
That thought left him a bit confused.
The Primordial Race was the strongest race in the Divine Realm, and probably the strongest in the entire universe.
Their bloodline was the origin of human strength, and among every tier of Primordial Bloodline out there, Max carried the highest one, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.
A bloodline at that level shouldn’t be simple.
Yet to Max, its effects still felt strangely hidden.
It strengthened him a lot, sure.
It brought him closer to the laws and multiplied the power of his paths and elements.
It also let him awaken Primordial Flames.
But compared to how mysterious the Primordials were supposed to be, Max felt like he’d only scratched the surface.
"I’ll need to ask Sarvion or one of the Primordials about this later," Max muttered.
He was sure there was more to the Primordial Bloodline than what he currently grasped.
Maybe the problem wasn’t the bloodline.
Maybe it was him.
He’d only received the bloodline recently and hadn’t gotten a proper explanation of how Primordials actually used it.

He was treating it like just another power stacked onto his body, but maybe the Primordial Bloodline needed to be understood as a foundation that transformed all his other powers rather than as a separate ability on its own.
Either way, thinking about it without guidance wouldn’t give him answers right away.
So Max stopped dwelling on it and started practicing with the Primordial Flames instead.
The golden flame appeared above his palm the moment the eye between his brows opened.
It burned quietly, pure and ancient, without the wild hunger of his black flames.
Max controlled it carefully at first, shaping it into threads, blades, spheres, waves, and thin layers that wrapped his fists.
The more he practiced, the more he understood its nature.

chapters.title: Chapter 2004: More Pseudo Cosmic Paths!
paragraphs: Primordial Flames didn’t simply burn. They refined, purified and returned things to a more original state.

When Max used black flames, the result was violent and direct. The black flames devoured energy, corroded defenses, consumed vitality, and turned everything they touched into fuel. But the Primordial Flames worked differently.
They burned through impurities. They weakened corruption. They refined unstable energy. They even sharpened Max’s own understanding of law when he used them with restraint.
For enemies, that purity could turn terrifying. A defense built on unstable laws might get refined until it collapsed. A devil’s corrupted power might get purified until its foundation cracked.
A bloodline curse might burn away from the inside. Even a strong body could be attacked not by destroying it outright, but by burning away the hidden flaws holding its strength together.

After long practice, Max’s grasp of the Primordial Flames deepened rapidly. Eventually, he created another Pseudo Cosmic Path from them. The moment the new path took shape, the golden flame above his palm turned sharper and more profound. It no longer felt like just a bloodline ability. It became a road, a direction, a law that Max himself had started to comprehend.
Primordial Flame Path. It was still only a Pseudo Cosmic Path, but its potential ran deep.
Once that was done, Max didn’t stop. He still had time. Over the next few years inside the Dimension of Time, he focused on building Pseudo Cosmic Paths for his Ice Element and Light Element.

Before, he hadn’t been able to do this because his mastery over these two elements hadn’t gone deep enough. He could use ice and light, but using an element and walking it toward a Pseudo Cosmic Path were two completely different things. Forming a Pseudo Cosmic Path meant understanding the deeper nature, law structure, battle application, and conceptual direction of that power. Max’s mastery hadn’t reached that level before.

Now, with the Primordial Bloodline, everything had changed. The moment he focused on ice, he felt like he’d been close to it for years. He could feel the stillness inside cold, the way motion slowed down, the freezing of energy, and how ice could preserve, imprison, and destroy all at once. The element no longer felt like something he had to force himself to use. It felt natural.

The same thing happened with light. When Max studied the Light Element, he could sense its speed, purity, warmth, illumination, and judgment. It wasn’t the same as the Heavenly Luminance Divine Bloodline, but the two resonated with each other. His Primordial Bloodline made that resonance clearer, letting him understand the Light Element not just as a force of brightness, but as a law that revealed, purified, accelerated, and pierced.
Because of that, Max successfully built Pseudo Cosmic Paths for both ice and light.
"I see," Max muttered once he’d finished. "The Primordial Bloodline massively boosts my mastery over elements."
His eyes turned thoughtful. "Even for elements where I haven’t unlocked a dimension yet, I still feel a lot closer to them."

This gave him a clearer picture of the Primordial Bloodline. Maybe its greatest strength wasn’t some single obvious ability. Maybe its real value sat in comprehension itself. It pulled him closer to the laws, made elements feel natural, strengthened his Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and let him understand powers that should have taken years of study.
To other cultivators, forming a Pseudo Cosmic Path was an enormous challenge. To Max, the Primordial Bloodline made the whole process smoother, faster, and more instinctive.
That was terrifying in its own way.

After finishing the Pseudo Cosmic Paths for Primordial Flames, Ice, and Light, Max still had a few hours left. He spent the rest of the time practicing his sword arts and thinking through the Emotion Severing Path.

Dragonheart appeared in his hand, and Max moved through the Saint Order Sword Art again and again. Each swing came out calm, precise, and controlled. He wasn’t chasing his strongest attack. Instead, he focused on feeling the edge hidden inside emotion, the line between attachment and detachment, the moment when killing intent became unnecessary because the blade itself had already cut through the heart’s disturbance.

Among all his Pseudo Cosmic Paths, the Emotion Severing Path felt closest to becoming a true Cosmic Path. Divine King Punishment was powerful, but it still needed more comprehension. The Devouring Flames Domain was terrifying, but its path leaned too heavily on destruction and hunger. The Primordial Flame Path had great potential, but it had only just come together. Ice and Light were also brand new.

Emotion Severing Path was different. It had followed Max through several dangerous battles. It had sharpened his will, changed his attacks, and let him cut through things ordinary force couldn’t touch. Every time he used it, he felt like he was standing closer to the boundary between a Pseudo Cosmic Path and a true one.
"I feel like out of all my Pseudo Cosmic Paths, Emotion Severing is closest to becoming the real thing," Max muttered.
His gaze settled into calm. "It’s only a matter of time."

With that, he kept practicing. Dragonheart moved through the air in smooth arcs, and the Saint Order Sword Art carried the invisible sharpness of the Emotion Severing Path with every strike. The Dimension of Time stayed silent around him, but with each swing, the space ahead of him seemed to lose something intangible.
Anger. Fear. Desire. Attachment.

For those final hours, Max forgot about the devils, the Primordials, the Five Sacred Clans, the sacred legacy, and even the warning about Anover. He focused only on his sword. He focused only on the path. And slowly, the edge of Emotion Severing grew sharper.
On the day of the meeting with the devils, the entire Divine Realm seemed to hold its breath.
It wasn’t that the countless worlds, planets, forces, clans, empires, and ancient forces of the Divine Realm had actually stopped moving.

Cities kept running. Merchants kept traveling. Cultivators kept training. Starships still crossed the void, and formation gates still opened from one region to another. Yet beneath all that ordinary movement, a strange tension had spread across the realm like an invisible storm.

chapters.title: Chapter 2005: Stage Was Set!
paragraphs: People with ordinary status didn’t know the full truth, but even they could sense that something had changed. The sky above many major worlds felt heavier. The elders of powerful forces had suddenly withdrawn from public view. Ancient formations that hadn’t lit up in countless years began glowing quietly in hidden places.

Patrols around important star realms increased. The great families put their celebrations on hold. The forces called their wandering disciples back home. Even a few old monsters who’d been in seclusion for thousands of years opened their eyes after getting secret messages from their forces.
The Divine Realm was vast, but news traveled fast among those standing near its peak.
Devils had entered their universe. That single fact alone was enough to leave countless ancient powers on edge.

The meeting took place inside the grand council domain of the Primordial Race. This wasn’t just some hall. It was an enormous sacred meeting ground built inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain, surrounded by floating mountains, golden law rivers, and countless ancient symbols drifting slowly across the sky like living stars.

At the center stood a vast circular platform made of bronze-gold stone, and above it hovered a rotating star map showing the layout of the Divine Realm, the Mortal Realm beneath it, and the distant boundary where the Wall of Eternity stood.
The aura in the meeting place felt so heavy that even space itself seemed more solid than usual.

The Primordials sat in the highest seats. The four Primarchs sat at the front, their expressions calm, though the pressure surrounding them made it clear none of them were taking this meeting lightly. Behind them stood other powerful Primordial experts, each one carrying an ancient aura that made them look like living pillars of the universe itself.
Beyond the Primordial Race, many of the strongest first-rate forces in the Divine Realm had shown up too.

The War God Palace stood on one side, their experts dressed in battle robes and ancient armor. Their leader’s aura came off fierce and straightforward, like a weapon sharpened through countless wars. Even standing quietly, the warriors behind him carried a frightening battle intent, like they were ready to march into war the second an order came down.

Beside them stood the representatives of the Sword God Palace. Compared to the War God Palace, their group looked far quieter, but the sharpness surrounding them felt even more suffocating. Their robes moved gently without any wind, and sword intent flowed around them like an invisible river. Several of their elders looked calm on the surface, but Max could feel that each of them was like a sheathed divine sword waiting to be drawn.

The Nine Star Court had also arrived. Their experts wore dark blue robes marked with star patterns, and nine radiant stars floated behind their leading elder like a small constellation. Their presence felt mysterious and profound, carrying traces of destiny, star law, and heavenly calculation.

The Stellar Templar stood not far off, their armor shining with silver light. Unlike the War God Palace, they carried a colder, more disciplined presence. They looked like witches of a sacred order, every movement measured and every gaze filled with solemn vigilance.

The Lunarian Kingdom had sent its royal delegation as well. Their people wore moon-white robes and silver crowns, and their leader carried an elegant, unreadable aura. A faint moon shadow hovered above their group, casting a gentle glow that somehow made the surrounding space feel colder and quieter.

The Grand Void Sanctum stood in a section where space itself seemed to bend. Their experts stayed half-hidden inside layers of darkness and folded void. Some looked clear for a moment and blurred the next, as if they weren’t fully standing in the same space as everyone else.

Ascension Hall had come too. Their representatives looked solemn and dignified, with ancient scrolls, law tablets, and golden seals floating behind them. They were known for managing many of the Divine Realm’s great ascension records and ancient trials, and their presence here alone showed how serious the situation had gotten.
Then there were the Four Sacred Clans.

Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest had all come with their leaders, elders, and selected descendants. Their expressions were also solemn. Even though a lot had happened in the Four Sacred Clans due to Max and Freya, they still chose to attend the meeting. They knew not to let their personal matters change what matters the most.
Their four sacred ancestors were present too, standing above their respective clans with solemn faces. Every so often, their gazes drifted toward Max.
They weren’t the only ones watching him.
Beside the Primordials stood the ten new geniuses who’d received the Primordial Bloodline. Max stood among them with a calm expression.

Revona stood quietly not far from him, her posture relaxed, her eyes deep and unreadable. Damian’s face stayed cold as he looked over the gathered first-rate forces. Ervin looked thoughtful, like he was trying to work out the meaning behind every arrangement in the meeting ground.

Morgana glanced around with a faint sneer, though even she kept her mouth shut in a place like this. Kaiden stood beside Revona, his expression steady. Orion looked far less carefree than usual, while Rosaline, Rakan, Aurelian, and the rest all carried different shades of seriousness.

They’d only been given one week. One week to awaken their Primordial Bloodline abilities. One week to digest the truth about the devils. One week to prepare for a meeting involving forces standing at the very peak of the Divine Realm.

For Max, that week had stretched much longer thanks to the Dimension of Time, but even he could feel that today’s atmosphere was different from any battle or trial he’d faced before. This wasn’t an arena where strength alone decided everything. This was a meeting where words could decide whether the Divine Realm slid into war, compromise, delay, or disaster.

His gaze swept across the gathered forces. War God Palace. Sword God Palace. Nine Star Court. Stellar Templar. Lunarian Kingdom. Grand Void Sanctum. Ascension Hall. Four Sacred Clans. Primordial Race. Each of these forces could shake countless worlds with a single command. Yet today, all of them had gathered in one place because a small group of devils had shown up in their universe.
That alone said everything about how terrifying the devil race really was.

chapters.title: Chapter 2006: Arrival of the Devils!
paragraphs: The wait for the Devil Race didn’t last long.

Only a few minutes had passed since the major forces of the Divine Realm gathered inside the grand council domain of the Primordial Race, yet the atmosphere already felt heavy enough to crush weaker cultivators.

The four Primarchs stood at the center of the meeting ground, surrounded by the leaders of the strongest first-rate forces, the Four Sacred Clans, and the newly awakened Primordial geniuses. No one spoke casually.
Even those who hated waiting understood that this meeting would decide whether the Divine Realm gained time to prepare or took another step toward a universe-shaking war.
Then the sky changed.

The golden clouds above the council domain slowly parted. A dark crack appeared between them. Black mist poured out of that crack, and the pure primordial light in the air dimmed, as if a stain had spread across the heavens.
The temperature dropped sharply. The laws around the meeting ground twisted for a moment, and a cruel pressure came down from above.
The devils had arrived.

There were only around ten of them, but their presence alone tensed up the entire council domain. Each devil stood tall and powerful, covered in ancient tattoos that resembled Infernal Demon Tattoos, only deeper and more vicious.

Their horns glowed with dark crimson light, and the markings across their bodies seemed to pulse like living symbols. They hovered above the meeting ground as if they hadn’t stepped into enemy territory, but had come to inspect a place that would soon belong to them.
At their front stood Varok.

He looked young, handsome, and cruel. His skin was pale with a faint gray tone, his eyes were dark red, and the tattoos running from his horns down to his neck and hands made him look both elegant and savage.

He was the son of Devil Emperor Abaddon, but his expression carried none of the caution an envoy should have. He looked down at the gathered forces of the Divine Realm with a faint smile, as if the Primordials, sacred clans, palace masters, kingdom rulers, and ancient leaders below weren’t worth being nervous about.
"You’ve put together quite the grand welcome for me," Varok said.
His voice spread through the sky.
The four Primarchs rose from their seats at the same time and appeared in the air in front of the devils.
Arvantos stood among them, his expression calm and unreadable. Beside him stood the other three Primarchs, and their presence alone made the pressure in the sky much heavier.

The first was Primarch Eryndor, a tall man with bronze-gold skin, long dark hair, and eyes that burned like molten stars. His aura felt thick, ancient, and overwhelming, like a living mountain built from the first bones of the universe.
Among the four Primarchs, he gave off the most direct physical pressure, and every breath he took made space tremble faintly.

The second was Primarch Lysandra, a woman dressed in flowing silver-gold robes. Her hair was pale as moonlight, and countless tiny law runes moved around her like fireflies. Her aura came off calm, but it carried terrifying depth, as if she could see through energy, soul, bloodline, and fate with a single glance.

The third was Primarch Veyrion, a cold-faced man whose eyes seemed to hold a rotating starfield. His body didn’t release much pressure openly, but the space around him bent naturally, making him feel distant even while standing right there.
Compared to Eryndor’s overwhelming force and Lysandra’s profound mystery, Veyrion felt like someone who could make entire star realms disappear without changing his expression.

Arvantos stood slightly ahead of them. He’d already spoken with Max and the others before, but now, facing Varok and the Devil Race, his aura felt completely different. He no longer looked like an elder teaching younger geniuses. He looked like one of the pillars holding up the universe.
Behind the four Primarchs, the leaders of the top first-rate forces rose into the air too.

The War God Palace Master, Garron Aresvale, stood with both arms crossed, his body wrapped in dark battle armor that looked forged from the bones of ancient battlefields. His eyes were sharp and wild, and even before he said a word, his battle intent made it clear he’d rather crush the devils than negotiate with them.

Beside him stood the Sword God Palace Master, Celian Voss, a calm man in white sword robes. He carried no visible sword, yet the air around him was filled with sword intent so sharp that even the darkness released by the devils seemed to split apart before it could touch him.

The Nine Star Court was represented by High Lord Astren Vale, an old man with nine small stars rotating behind him. His eyes were deep and calculating, and his fingers moved slowly, as if he were measuring hidden changes in fate.

The Stellar Templar stood behind Grand Marshal Seraphis Kael, whose silver armor shone with cold starlight. His presence felt disciplined and solemn, carrying the air of someone who’d commanded countless wars without ever letting emotion cloud his judgment.

The Lunarian Kingdom’s delegation was led by Queen Selene Lunaris, a beautiful woman with moon-white hair and a silver crown. She stood beneath a faint lunar shadow, her expression gentle, though her eyes stayed clear and distant, like a cold moon watching worlds rise and fall.

The Grand Void Sanctum’s master, Lord Vael Noxis, appeared half-hidden inside folded darkness. His figure blurred at the edges, and sometimes he looked close while his aura felt thousands of miles away.
Ascension Hall was led by Hall Master Orin Caldus, a dignified man with ancient scrolls and golden law tablets floating behind him. His expression stayed grave, and his eyes never left Varok.

The Four Sacred Clans had also sent their leaders and ancestors. Valerius burned with sacred solar light. Ashbourne carried blood-iron battle force. Ravenhart stood in shadowed silence. Evercrest controlled the surrounding space through hidden roots and sealed domains.
Even though the recent matter involving the Voidwalker Clan hadn’t been settled, none of them dared show any internal conflict in front of the devils.

Below them, Max and the other nine geniuses stood near the Primordial side. They weren’t seated among the leaders, but their position let them hear every word clearly. The meeting hadn’t been kept from them.
Arvantos had said it was time they learned the truth, and clearly that also meant they were allowed to listen to the negotiations that would shape the direction of the coming storm.

Max looked up at Varok in silence. He’d already heard that Varok carried the Pearl of Abyss. Because of that, the Primordials couldn’t simply kill or seal him without risking consequences no one could predict. Still, watching the young devil stand above the council domain with such arrogance made Max’s eyes turn colder.

sentences.text: The wait for the Devil Race didn’t last long.

Only a few minutes had passed since the major forces of the Divine Realm gathered inside the grand council domain of the Primordial Race, yet the atmosphere already felt heavy enough to crush weaker cultivators.
The four Primarchs stood at the center of the meeting ground, surrounded by the leaders of the strongest first-rate forces, the Four Sacred Clans, and the newly awakened Primordial geniuses.
No one spoke casually.
Even those who hated waiting understood that this meeting would decide whether the Divine Realm gained time to prepare or took another step toward a universe-shaking war.
Then the sky changed.
The golden clouds above the council domain slowly parted.
A dark crack appeared between them.
Black mist poured out of that crack, and the pure primordial light in the air dimmed, as if a stain had spread across the heavens.
The temperature dropped sharply.
The laws around the meeting ground twisted for a moment, and a cruel pressure came down from above.
The devils had arrived.
There were only around ten of them, but their presence alone tensed up the entire council domain.
Each devil stood tall and powerful, covered in ancient tattoos that resembled Infernal Demon Tattoos, only deeper and more vicious.
Their horns glowed with dark crimson light, and the markings across their bodies seemed to pulse like living symbols.
They hovered above the meeting ground as if they hadn’t stepped into enemy territory, but had come to inspect a place that would soon belong to them.
At their front stood Varok.
He looked young, handsome, and cruel.
His skin was pale with a faint gray tone, his eyes were dark red, and the tattoos running from his horns down to his neck and hands made him look both elegant and savage.
He was the son of Devil Emperor Abaddon, but his expression carried none of the caution an envoy should have.

He looked down at the gathered forces of the Divine Realm with a faint smile, as if the Primordials, sacred clans, palace masters, kingdom rulers, and ancient leaders below weren’t worth being nervous about.
"You’ve put together quite the grand welcome for me," Varok said.
His voice spread through the sky.
The four Primarchs rose from their seats at the same time and appeared in the air in front of the devils.
Arvantos stood among them, his expression calm and unreadable.
Beside him stood the other three Primarchs, and their presence alone made the pressure in the sky much heavier.
The first was Primarch Eryndor, a tall man with bronze-gold skin, long dark hair, and eyes that burned like molten stars.
His aura felt thick, ancient, and overwhelming, like a living mountain built from the first bones of the universe.
Among the four Primarchs, he gave off the most direct physical pressure, and every breath he took made space tremble faintly.
The second was Primarch Lysandra, a woman dressed in flowing silver-gold robes.
Her hair was pale as moonlight, and countless tiny law runes moved around her like fireflies.
Her aura came off calm, but it carried terrifying depth, as if she could see through energy, soul, bloodline, and fate with a single glance.
The third was Primarch Veyrion, a cold-faced man whose eyes seemed to hold a rotating starfield.
His body didn’t release much pressure openly, but the space around him bent naturally, making him feel distant even while standing right there.
Compared to Eryndor’s overwhelming force and Lysandra’s profound mystery, Veyrion felt like someone who could make entire star realms disappear without changing his expression.
Arvantos stood slightly ahead of them.
He’d already spoken with Max and the others before, but now, facing Varok and the Devil Race, his aura felt completely different.
He no longer looked like an elder teaching younger geniuses.
He looked like one of the pillars holding up the universe.
Behind the four Primarchs, the leaders of the top first-rate forces rose into the air too.
The War God Palace Master, Garron Aresvale, stood with both arms crossed, his body wrapped in dark battle armor that looked forged from the bones of ancient battlefields.
His eyes were sharp and wild, and even before he said a word, his battle intent made it clear he’d rather crush the devils than negotiate with them.
Beside him stood the Sword God Palace Master, Celian Voss, a calm man in white sword robes.
He carried no visible sword, yet the air around him was filled with sword intent so sharp that even the darkness released by the devils seemed to split apart before it could touch him.
The Nine Star Court was represented by High Lord Astren Vale, an old man with nine small stars rotating behind him.
His eyes were deep and calculating, and his fingers moved slowly, as if he were measuring hidden changes in fate.
The Stellar Templar stood behind Grand Marshal Seraphis Kael, whose silver armor shone with cold starlight.
His presence felt disciplined and solemn, carrying the air of someone who’d commanded countless wars without ever letting emotion cloud his judgment.
The Lunarian Kingdom’s delegation was led by Queen Selene Lunaris, a beautiful woman with moon-white hair and a silver crown.
She stood beneath a faint lunar shadow, her expression gentle, though her eyes stayed clear and distant, like a cold moon watching worlds rise and fall.
The Grand Void Sanctum’s master, Lord Vael Noxis, appeared half-hidden inside folded darkness.
His figure blurred at the edges, and sometimes he looked close while his aura felt thousands of miles away.
Ascension Hall was led by Hall Master Orin Caldus, a dignified man with ancient scrolls and golden law tablets floating behind him.
His expression stayed grave, and his eyes never left Varok.
The Four Sacred Clans had also sent their leaders and ancestors.
Valerius burned with sacred solar light.
Ashbourne carried blood-iron battle force.
Ravenhart stood in shadowed silence.
Evercrest controlled the surrounding space through hidden roots and sealed domains.
Even though the recent matter involving the Voidwalker Clan hadn’t been settled, none of them dared show any internal conflict in front of the devils.
Below them, Max and the other nine geniuses stood near the Primordial side.
They weren’t seated among the leaders, but their position let them hear every word clearly.

Arvantos had said it was time they learned the truth, and clearly that also meant they were allowed to listen to the negotiations that would shape the direction of the coming storm.

Because of that, the Primordials couldn’t simply kill or seal him without risking consequences no one could predict.

chapters.title: Chapter 2007: Terms and Conditions!
paragraphs: Varok looked at the four Primarchs, then at the leaders standing behind them. A sneer crossed his face.
"I didn’t expect this meeting to bring in so many insects," he said. "But since you’ve dragged out so many ants to watch, I won’t complain."
The expressions of many leaders turned cold at once.

The War God Palace Master gave a low laugh, and the sound carried real violence in it. The Sword God Palace Master’s eyes narrowed slightly. Several elders of the Four Sacred Clans let out faint killing intent, but the four Primarchs stayed calm.

Varok spread his hands. "Since you’ve gathered everyone, let’s begin." His smile faded, and his voice sharpened. "I don’t enjoy wasting time. Have you decided whether you’ll accept my conditions, or would you rather have war instead?"
The council domain fell silent.

Varok continued before anyone could answer. "My condition is simple. I’ll establish a force of my own in the Divine Realm. This force will be independent. No Primordial, sacred clan, or any force in the Divine Realm will suppress it, monitor it openly, restrict its normal movement, or interfere with its affairs without cause."

His gaze moved across the leaders one by one. "My people will be allowed to enter the Divine Realm, trade, cultivate, recruit, and build our foundation here. As long as we don’t start slaughtering your people, you won’t move against us. In exchange, I won’t push for immediate war."
A cold silence followed. Even though everyone had already heard the general condition from Arvantos, hearing Varok say it so openly still made the air feel suffocating.
Letting devils establish a force inside the Divine Realm wasn’t a small concession. It was like letting poison into the bloodstream and hoping it wouldn’t spread.
Arvantos looked at Varok calmly. "We’re willing to accept a modified version of your condition."
Varok’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Modified?"

Primarch Eryndor stepped forward, his voice deep enough to shake the sky. "You may establish a force in the Divine Realm, but it won’t be free from consequences. If any devil gets caught harming the human race, forcibly corrupting cultivators, slaughtering innocent people, devouring worlds, damaging star realms, or using devil power to secretly control the forces of the Divine Realm, all terms will be broken."

Primarch Lysandra continued in a calm but cold voice. "If that happens, every protection granted to your people will disappear. Any devil involved will be killed. Any devil force connected to the crime will be destroyed. If your newly established faction shelters the offender, the entire faction will be wiped out."
Varok’s expression darkened. "You dare threaten to kill devils after agreeing to negotiate?"
Before the Primarchs could respond, Garron Aresvale, the War God Palace Master, laughed with open contempt.
"Seems like you’ve misunderstood something, devil brat."
Varok turned slowly toward him.

Garron’s sneer deepened. "This is the Divine Realm, not your devil universe. You’re not standing in your father’s court, and the people here aren’t your subjects. If any devil gets caught doing something suspicious, we’ll kill them without mercy. If you want to call that a threat, go ahead and call it a threat."
The devils behind Varok let their killing intent loose all at once.
Garron’s battle aura exploded in response, turning the air around him into a roaring battlefield.
"Try it," he said coldly.
The atmosphere nearly broke.
Then Arvantos raised one hand. The pressure from both sides stopped before it could fully erupt.
Varok’s face had gone much darker. He stared at Garron for a long moment, then looked back at the four Primarchs.
"You expect me to accept a condition where any random force can accuse my people and kill them?"

Primarch Veyrion spoke for the first time. His voice was quiet, but it reached everyone clearly. "No. We’ll set up a judgment system. If a devil gets accused, the matter will be investigated by representatives from the Primordial Race and at least three top first-rate forces. But if a devil gets caught in the act, the nearest force has full authority to kill them immediately."
Varok’s eyes flashed with cold light.
Lysandra added, "There’s another condition."
Varok looked at her. "Go on."
"The devils are prohibited from entering the Mortal Realm."
The moment she said it, Max’s eyes sharpened slightly, and the other geniuses grew more serious too.
The Mortal Realm was far weaker than the Divine Realm. If devils gained access to it, the fallout would be disastrous. Countless worlds wouldn’t be able to resist even a small group of devils.

Lysandra’s voice stayed calm. "Any attempt to open a passage toward the Mortal Realm, contact forces there, spread devil power there, establish hidden shrines there, or carry out suspicious activity connected to it will count as a violation of the agreement. If a violation happens, the devils involved will be killed."
Arvantos added, "And if your force is connected to it, your force will be destroyed."
Varok’s expression turned colder. "You people have a lot of rules for a side that claims it doesn’t want war."
Celian Voss, the Sword God Palace Master, spoke softly. "Rules are the only reason this meeting hasn’t already turned into slaughter."
The air turned colder again.

High Lord Astren Vale of the Nine Star Court then said, "There’s another matter. If our geniuses run into devils outside the universe in future battlefields, trials, ruins, or neutral spaces, your people must not target them with killing intent, assassination attempts, soul corruption, or bloodline curses."
Varok looked at him with a faint sneer. "You want me to control every devil beyond this universe?"
Astren’s eyes stayed calm. "You’re the one asking to establish a force here. If you want privileges inside our Divine Realm, you should restrain your race elsewhere too."

Varok laughed coldly. "I can control the devils who fall under my banner in this universe. I can’t control every devil in the devil universe, and I can’t control those acting outside my authority. If your geniuses run into devils beyond this universe, their survival will depend on their own strength."
Damian’s face turned cold hearing that.
Orion clenched his fists.
Morgana sneered softly. "So they want safety here but won’t offer any out there."
Revona stayed silent, but her eyes had turned sharper.

Max watched Varok carefully. He understood exactly what Varok’s words meant. The devils wanted their people protected inside the Divine Realm, but they refused to guarantee the safety of Divine Realm geniuses outside the universe.
That wasn’t surprising. This negotiation wasn’t about fairness. It was about leverage.
Grand Marshal Seraphis Kael of the Stellar Templar said coldly, "Then your people in the Divine Realm won’t get absolute protection either. If they stir up hatred, they’ll face the consequences."

Queen Selene Lunaris added in a gentle but firm voice, "Your force can exist, but it can’t recruit any people of the Divine Realm. If any people of the Divine Realm were to join your force, they will be declared a traitor and be killed immediately"

Lord Vael Noxis of the Grand Void Sanctum spoke from within the folded darkness. "Your force will also be forbidden from building secret spatial passages without registering them. Any hidden passage we find will be destroyed immediately."

Hall Master Orin Caldus of Ascension Hall said, "Your members will be recorded. Their identities, cultivation, aura signatures, and movements between major regions have to be registered. Call it a restriction if you want, but without it, there’s no agreement."
Varok’s face grew darker with every added condition. The devils behind him looked furious, but none of them moved.

They clearly understood that despite their arrogance, they stood deep inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain, surrounded by the strongest forces of the Divine Realm. If not for Varok’s identity and the Pearl of Abyss, they wouldn’t have dared stand here so boldly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2008: Max’s Exposing the Hole in the Agreement!
paragraphs: Varok’s voice turned icy. "You want to accept my condition while tying my hands and feet."
Arvantos replied calmly, "You want to enter our Divine Realm while expecting us to trust the Devil Race. Neither side gets everything it wants."
Varok stared at him. Arvantos stared back. For a long moment, the entire council domain hung frozen between war and compromise.
Neither side was willing to fully back down. Varok refused to drop his demand to establish a devil force in the Divine Realm.

The Primordials and the leaders of the Divine Realm refused to accept any agreement that handed the devils unrestricted freedom. Both sides knew the flaws in the other’s position, and both sides knew starting a war right now would be dangerous.

The devils had too few people inside the universe to win a direct war at this point. The Divine Realm couldn’t kill Varok casually because of Abaddon and the Pearl of Abyss. That balance forced both sides to keep talking.
The argument dragged on for a long time. Conditions got added, rejected, altered, and narrowed down.
The devils demanded independence. The Divine Realm demanded restrictions. The devils demanded freedom of movement. The Divine Realm demanded registration.

The devils demanded no suppression. The Divine Realm demanded the right to retaliate if harm was done. The devils refused to take responsibility for devils beyond the universe. The Divine Realm refused to offer them complete protection inside it.

In the end, both sides compromised. The devils would be allowed to establish a force in the Divine Realm, but only within a designated star region chosen by the Primordials and approved by the major forces.

Their members would be registered. Their movements would be monitored in limited ways. They’d be forbidden from entering the Mortal Realm, building secret passages, committing slaughter, spreading forced corruption, enslaving cultivators, or interfering with existing forces through hidden means.
If they broke these conditions, the Divine Realm would have the right to kill the offenders. If the violation was severe enough, the whole agreement would be considered broken.
Varok’s expression stayed dark after the terms were settled, but a faint smile still crept onto his lips.
Max noticed it. So did Revona. So did several of the older leaders. No matter how many restrictions had been piled on them, the devils had still won something important.
They’d gained a foothold. For the first time since the ancient war, the Devil Race would be allowed to build a force inside the Divine Realm, inside another universe.
Even watched, even restricted, even surrounded by conditions from the Divine Realm’s leaders, the result stayed the same. The devils had entered their universe. And now they’d be allowed to stay.
Varok looked down at the council domain and smiled faintly. "Good. Let this be the start of a more peaceful relationship between our races."
No one believed him.
The meeting had avoided immediate war. But deep down, everyone knew this wasn’t peace. It was only the first move of something far more dangerous.
Just as Varok’s faint smile appeared, Max stepped forward from among the ten geniuses. The movement wasn’t big, but in that suffocating council domain, it pulled countless gazes toward him at once.

The leaders of the Divine Realm looked over. The Four Sacred Clans narrowed their eyes. The devils behind Varok stared at him with cold amusement, while the other nine geniuses showed different reactions.
Orion’s eyes widened slightly, Damian turned serious, Ervin frowned like he’d guessed something coming, and Revona’s gaze sharpened with rare interest.
Max stopped beneath the floating star map and looked up at Varok.
"Your agreement has a flaw," he said.
The council domain went silent.
Varok slowly lowered his gaze, his dark red eyes fixing on Max. A faint sneer crossed his face. "And who are you supposed to be?"
Max didn’t flinch. "Someone who can see the hole in your words."

Several devils immediately let their killing intent loose. The pressure came down toward Max like a black tide, but before the Primarchs or any of the leaders could react, Max’s middle eye opened between his brows. A pure golden flame appeared inside it.
Primordial Flames.

The black killing intent closing in on him burned away silently before it ever touched his body. It didn’t scatter. It got refined into nothing with a calm purity that made several devils’ expressions shift.
Even Varok’s eyes narrowed.
The four Primarchs glanced at Max at the same time. Arvantos’s expression stayed calm, but a faint light passed through his eyes.

Max looked directly at Varok and continued, "You said the devils under your banner in this universe will follow the agreement, but you also said you can’t control devils beyond this universe. That means any devil can act outside your so-called authority, attack our geniuses in neutral spaces, corrupt our people beyond the Wall of Eternity, and then claim they were never your responsibility."
Varok’s smile faded slightly.
Max’s voice turned colder. "That’s not a loophole. That’s a prepared escape route."

The expressions of many leaders shifted. High Lord Astren Vale of the Nine Star Court looked at Max with a trace of approval. Grand Marshal Seraphis Kael crossed his arms, his cold eyes fixed on Varok. The Sword God Palace Master, Celian Voss, gave a faint nod, while Garron Aresvale of the War God Palace laughed under his breath.
Varok stared at Max and sneered. "You talk boldly for someone standing behind his elders."
Max smiled faintly. "You talk boldly for someone hiding behind his father’s name and a Primal Treasure."
The sky turned cold. The devils behind Varok nearly erupted on the spot.
Varok’s face went completely dark. "Human, do you want to die?"

Max immediately took a defensive stance. This time, the aura around him changed. Ten blue void rings appeared around his body, rotating from his wrists to his shoulders, each carrying a different kind of pressure.

One held a pale invisible sharpness that made emotions tremble. One flickered with seven-colored lightning. One burned with black devouring flames. One released the pure golden heat of Primordial Flames. The remaining rings carried folded space, light, ice, soul force, dragon aura, and deep Voidwalker sealing power.
Max couldn’t be sure when a devil would sneak attack him and so even though he was standing with leaders of the Divine Realm, he was still cautious.
For the first time, the devils looked at Max seriously.
Varok’s gaze locked onto the void rings. "What are you?"
Max answered calmly, "The person who’ll kill your people if they cross the line."

The movement wasn’t big, but in that suffocating council domain, it pulled countless gazes toward him at once.
The leaders of the Divine Realm looked over.
The Four Sacred Clans narrowed their eyes.
The devils behind Varok stared at him with cold amusement, while the other nine geniuses showed different reactions.
Orion’s eyes widened slightly, Damian turned serious, Ervin frowned like he’d guessed something coming, and Revona’s gaze sharpened with rare interest.
Max stopped beneath the floating star map and looked up at Varok.
"Your agreement has a flaw," he said.
The council domain went silent.
Varok slowly lowered his gaze, his dark red eyes fixing on Max.
A faint sneer crossed his face.
"And who are you supposed to be?"
Max didn’t flinch.
"Someone who can see the hole in your words."
Several devils immediately let their killing intent loose.
The pressure came down toward Max like a black tide, but before the Primarchs or any of the leaders could react, Max’s middle eye opened between his brows.
A pure golden flame appeared inside it.
Primordial Flames.
The black killing intent closing in on him burned away silently before it ever touched his body.
It didn’t scatter.
It got refined into nothing with a calm purity that made several devils’ expressions shift.
Even Varok’s eyes narrowed.
The four Primarchs glanced at Max at the same time.
Arvantos’s expression stayed calm, but a faint light passed through his eyes.
Max looked directly at Varok and continued, "You said the devils under your banner in this universe will follow the agreement, but you also said you can’t control devils beyond this universe.

That means any devil can act outside your so-called authority, attack our geniuses in neutral spaces, corrupt our people beyond the Wall of Eternity, and then claim they were never your responsibility."
Varok’s smile faded slightly.
Max’s voice turned colder.
"That’s not a loophole.
That’s a prepared escape route."
The expressions of many leaders shifted.
High Lord Astren Vale of the Nine Star Court looked at Max with a trace of approval.
Grand Marshal Seraphis Kael crossed his arms, his cold eyes fixed on Varok.
The Sword God Palace Master, Celian Voss, gave a faint nod, while Garron Aresvale of the War God Palace laughed under his breath.
Varok stared at Max and sneered.
"You talk boldly for someone standing behind his elders."
Max smiled faintly.
"You talk boldly for someone hiding behind his father’s name and a Primal Treasure."
The sky turned cold.
The devils behind Varok nearly erupted on the spot.
Varok’s face went completely dark.
"Human, do you want to die?"
Max immediately took a defensive stance.
This time, the aura around him changed.
Ten blue void rings appeared around his body, rotating from his wrists to his shoulders, each carrying a different kind of pressure.
One held a pale invisible sharpness that made emotions tremble.
One flickered with seven-colored lightning.
One burned with black devouring flames.
One released the pure golden heat of Primordial Flames.
The remaining rings carried folded space, light, ice, soul force, dragon aura, and deep Voidwalker sealing power.
Max couldn’t be sure when a devil would sneak attack him and so even though he was standing with leaders of the Divine Realm, he was still cautious.
For the first time, the devils looked at Max seriously.
Varok’s gaze locked onto the void rings.
"What are you?"
Max answered calmly, "The person who’ll kill your people if they cross the line."

chapters.title: Chapter 2009: Max’s One Condition!
paragraphs: The council domain went deadly silent.

The four sacred ancestors looked at Max with complicated expressions. They’d seen him fight. They’d seen him awaken the fifth end. They’d seen him break through to the Law Manifestation Realm and shake the Five Sacred Clan domain.
But now, standing in front of Varok and speaking on behalf of the Divine Realm’s younger generation, Max no longer looked like a reckless genius who’d stumbled into ancient secrets.
He looked like someone stepping into his role.
Arvantos watched him for a moment, then spoke. "Continue."
That single word shocked a lot of people. A Primarch had just given Max permission to speak at this meeting.
Varok’s eyes turned colder.

Max looked around at the gathered leaders, then turned back to Varok. "The Divine Realm should add another condition. Any devil force established here must accept a blood-oath boundary. If a devil outside this universe harms a recognized genius, envoy, or protected representative of our universe under orders from Varok, Abaddon, or any devil faction connected to the force established here, the agreement will be considered broken."
Varok sneered. "And how will you prove orders were given?"
Max replied, "Through soul traces, bloodline residue, contract marks, memory inspection, fate calculation, and testimony from neutral forces if the incident happens beyond the Wall of Eternity."
The Nine Star Court’s High Lord Astren Vale smiled faintly. "That’s doable."
The Ravenhart ancestor narrowed her eyes. "Difficult, but doable."

Lord Vael Noxis of the Grand Void Sanctum said from within the folded darkness, "If the devil force established here leaves a registered authority mark on its members, connection traces can be tracked."
Hall Master Orin Caldus of Ascension Hall nodded. "Ascension Hall can record the recognized geniuses and envoys. Anyone under official protection will have their status sealed into the agreement."
Varok’s face darkened further.
Max continued, "There’s another condition too."
Arvantos looked at him with interest.
Varok’s voice turned icy. "You’re adding a lot of conditions for someone still at the Law Manifestation Realm."

Max ignored the jab. "The Divine Realm should form an enforcement team made up of the ten new Primordial geniuses and representatives from the top first-rate forces. If devils break the agreement in places where elders can’t act openly, this team will have the right to investigate, suppress, and kill the offenders."

The ten geniuses reacted at once. Orion’s eyes widened before a grin slowly spread across his face. Damian’s expression sharpened. Ervin looked surprised, then thoughtful. Morgana’s lips curled with interest.
Kaiden glanced at Revona, while Revona looked at Max like she was seeing him in a new light. Rosaline, Rakan, and Aurelian all turned serious.
The War God Palace Master laughed loudly. "Good. Very good. Since the devils want to plant a force in our Divine Realm, our younger generation should have a blade pointed at their throats too."
Queen Selene Lunaris spoke gently. "It would also stop the devils from blaming every conflict on overbearing elders."
Celian Voss said calmly, "If their younger devils can move freely around the Divine Realm, our young geniuses should be able to respond in kind."
Varok’s eyes burned with anger. "You want to build a hunting group for my people and call it enforcement?"
Max looked at him calmly. "You want to build a devil force in our universe and call it peace."
For a moment, no one spoke. Then Garron Aresvale laughed again, his battle intent shaking the air. "I like this kid."
Arvantos looked toward the other three Primarchs.
Eryndor nodded. "The proposal has merit."
Lysandra’s eyes moved across the devils. "It also gives the younger generation real experience before the greater war arrives."
Veyrion said quietly, "And it puts pressure on the devil force without forcing immediate conflict."

Arvantos turned back to Varok. "This condition will be added. The ten new Primordial geniuses along with the geniuses from the Four Sacred Clan will form the core of a special enforcement group. They won’t attack devils without reason, but if your people violate the agreement, they’ll have the authority to act."
Varok’s expression turned ugly. The devils behind him glared at Max with undisguised killing intent.

Max didn’t look away. He knew this move would make him a target, but he didn’t care. The devils had already entered their universe. If they were allowed to move around freely while everyone politely waited for disaster to strike, the Divine Realm would only be giving them time to spread their roots.
Someone needed to watch them. Someone needed to act without getting held back by the older generation’s hesitation. And if there was one thing Max was good at, it was turning danger into growth.
Varok stared at him for a long time. Then his lips slowly curved again, though this time the smile carried real malice.
"Fine," he said. "Add your little enforcement group."
His gaze stayed locked on Max. "But remember this, human. Once you take on a role like that, you’re no longer just a genius standing behind the Primordials. You become part of the game."
Max smiled faintly. "I was already part of it the moment your people entered our universe."
Varok’s eyes flashed.

Arvantos raised his hand, and the newly added terms sealed themselves into the agreement through a massive golden law scroll that appeared above the council domain. One by one, the conditions lit up across its surface.

The devil force would be restricted to a designated star region. Their members would be registered. They were forbidden from entering the Mortal Realm. They couldn’t build hidden passages. They couldn’t enslave, corrupt, or slaughter people of the Divine Realm. They couldn’t secretly control local forces.
Any violation would allow retaliation. Any confirmed connection to attacks on official geniuses or envoys beyond the universe would also count as a breach.
And finally, the special enforcement group would be formed, with Max and the other nine new Primordial geniuses at its core.
The moment that final condition appeared, many gazes turned toward Max. The leaders of the Divine Realm now saw him differently.

The Four Sacred Clans looked at him with even more complicated emotions. The other geniuses realized their own role had shifted from future hope to active blade. And the devils committed his face to memory.
Varok finally looked away from Max and placed his palm against the golden law scroll. The Pearl of Abyss flickered faintly beneath his sleeve, letting out a dark pulse.
Arvantos placed his palm against the scroll too.
The agreement was sealed.
The devils had won the right to build a force inside the Divine Realm. But because of Max, they hadn’t gotten a free path to spread without consequences.
Then one of the devils standing beside Varok suddenly leaned in and whispered something into his ear.
"I see," Varok sneered as he looked at Max again. "No wonder you’re so confident talking to me. Turns out you’re the strongest young genius in this universe."
He added, "But has the Primordial Universe fallen so far that its strongest genius is only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm? I haven’t heard anything this funny in a while."
