chapters.title: Chapter 2010: Provocation for a battle?!
paragraphs: Varok’s gaze moved across the young geniuses standing near the Primordial side.
His dark red eyes lingered on Damian, Ervin, Revona, Morgana, Kaiden, Orion, Rosaline, Rakan, Aurelian, and the rest. Most of them had already stepped into the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm.

Their auras were young, fierce, and unstable in places from their recent Primordial Bloodline awakenings, but their realms were undeniable. They weren’t ordinary geniuses anymore. They’d turned into young monsters carrying the future of the Divine Realm on their shoulders.
Then Varok’s gaze finally landed back on Max. A faint sneer slowly crossed his face.

"I’ll admit, the other young geniuses of your universe aren’t bad," Varok said, his voice carrying across the council domain. "All of them sit at the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm. At the very least, they look like people your universe might reasonably pin some hope on."
His smile turned colder.
"But him?"
Varok’s eyes fixed on Max with open mockery.
"How can the so-called strongest young genius of your universe only be at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm? Is this some kind of joke?"
The moment those words fell, the atmosphere shifted. Several of the Divine Realm’s leaders frowned. The young geniuses turned cold too.

Orion’s grin disappeared. Damian’s eyes sharpened with faint killing intent. Ervin’s expression turned serious, while Morgana’s lips curled in displeasure. Even Revona, who’d stayed calm through most of the meeting, looked at Varok with a colder gaze.
They all knew Max’s realm sat lower than theirs. But none of them thought he was weak. He had defeated every single one of them at one entirely lower realm than them.
Max had only recently stepped into the Law Manifestation Realm, but you couldn’t judge his foundation by realm alone.
Before Max could say anything, a cold voice came from the War God Palace side.
Saint Reiner, who’d been sitting silently among the senior figures of the War God Palace, finally spoke.
"You talk too much for someone hiding behind a few devils."
Many eyes turned toward him.

Saint Reiner rose slowly from his seat. He was an old man with long silver hair, a weathered face, and eyes that looked like they’d witnessed countless battlefields. His body wasn’t large, but the moment he stood, an ancient and terrifying war intent spread through the council domain.
It wasn’t the sharp, reckless aura of a young warrior. It was the heavy pressure of someone who’d survived endless wars and personally walked through mountains of corpses.
The armor covering his body was dark gold and crimson, marked with countless scars. Every mark carried the weight of a battle that had once shaken the heavens.

In the War God Palace, the title of Saint wasn’t handed to ordinary geniuses or promising juniors. It was a position reserved for beings who stood at the same level as the palace master, or possessed strength that could surpass that seat.
Saint Reiner was one of the oldest and most powerful figures in the War God Palace, a legendary presence who’d once fought beside Garron Aresvale and had even guided him during his early years.

To Max, Saint Reiner was more than just an ancient powerhouse. He was also a teacher to him. Max had personally inherited everything Saint Reiner knew about the Seven Divine Veins, so in a way, Max counted as his student.
Now Saint Reiner looked at Varok with undisguised contempt.

"You’re looking down on a Primordial at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm," Saint Reiner said, his voice calm but heavy, "yet he’s more than enough to handle a few devils at the same realm."
His words instantly drew attention from both sides.

The War God Palace Master, Garron Aresvale, didn’t stop him. Instead, he leaned back with a fierce smile. He clearly understood what Saint Reiner was doing. The old saint wasn’t speaking out of arrogance. He was deliberately pushing the devils to reveal how far they were willing to go.
The War God Palace had never been the kind of force that stayed quiet when insulted. If the devils wanted to test the Divine Realm’s courage, the War God Palace would never be the first to back down.
Varok looked at Saint Reiner. For a moment, he said nothing. Then a cunning light flashed through his eyes. The mockery on his face deepened, but it no longer looked like simple arrogance.
"Oh?"
Varok’s gaze shifted from Saint Reiner to Max and back again.
"So you actually believe this Primordial trash at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm can handle devils at the same realm?"
The word trash made the air turn colder at once.
Max’s expression didn’t change, though he had a feeling something interesting was about to happen.

Saint Reiner’s eyes narrowed. He’d immediately caught Varok’s trap. The devil was trying to twist his words and drag Max into the center of the confrontation. Saint Reiner hadn’t meant to push Max into a reckless fight. He’d only wanted to remind the devils that the Divine Realm wasn’t short on powerful warriors.
But Varok had seized the opening.
Varok smiled. "Then how about this."
His voice grew louder, spreading across the entire council domain.

"I’ll send one devil from my side at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm. Let him fight this Primordial." He looked at Saint Reiner with a provocative smile. "You said he’s more than enough to handle a few Law Manifestation Realm devils. Then surely a single devil at the 5th level won’t be too much, right?"

Saint Reiner’s expression darkened. His gaze shifted to Max. For the first time, a trace of concern crossed his ancient eyes. He knew Max’s strength better than most people here, but he also knew how dangerous it was to fight a devil from a higher realm.
Max had only recently entered the Law Manifestation Realm, and even if his combat power outstripped his cultivation, the gap between the 1st and 5th levels was still huge.

The moment Varok mentioned the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm, plenty of people caught his intent. He wasn’t just trying to humiliate Max. He was trying to use Max’s lower realm as a weapon against the Divine Realm’s confidence.

If Max refused, Varok would mock him as an overhyped reputation manufactured by the Primordials and the top forces. If Max accepted and lost, the devils would use the win to crush the momentum of the Divine Realm’s younger generation before the agreement had even fully settled.
The timing was malicious. The method was crude, but it worked.
Varok turned toward the four Primarchs. "What do you say? Since your side seems so confident, surely you wouldn’t object to a simple exchange between juniors."
The entire council domain went silent. The leaders of the top first-rate forces looked toward the four Primarchs.
Arvantos’s expression stayed calm. Eryndor’s molten-star eyes glowed faintly. Lysandra looked at Max as if she were measuring something inside him. Veyrion’s starfield-like gaze stayed unreadable.
For a moment, none of them spoke. Then Arvantos said, "We have no objection."
Varok’s smile widened slightly.
Eryndor added in a deep voice, "A fight between juniors won’t affect the agreement."
Lysandra’s eyes stayed on Max. "Nor will it decide the future of the Divine Realm."
Veyrion spoke quietly. "But if both sides agree, there’s no reason to stop it."
The four Primarchs had all given their answer. They didn’t object.

For a moment, none of them spoke.
Then Arvantos said, "We have no objection."
Varok’s smile widened slightly.
Eryndor added in a deep voice, "A fight between juniors won’t affect the agreement."
Lysandra’s eyes stayed on Max.
"Nor will it decide the future of the Divine Realm."
Veyrion spoke quietly.
"But if both sides agree, there’s no reason to stop it."
The four Primarchs had all given their answer.
They didn’t object.

chapters.title: Chapter 2011: A Life and Death battle!
paragraphs: That decision stirred up the atmosphere again. Some leaders looked thoughtful. Some frowned. Some looked worried, while others looked interested. The War God Palace Master’s smile widened, since he’d always preferred direct clashes over endless talk. The Sword God Palace Master stayed calm, but the sword intent around him sharpened slightly.
The Four Sacred Clans watched Max with complicated expressions. After everything that had happened in their domain, they knew well enough that Max’s realm couldn’t be measured normally.
On top of that, they’d personally watched Max beat one of their own geniuses at the 10th level of the Law Manifestation Realm, let alone a devil sitting at the 5th.

Saint Reiner, though, stayed silent, his eyes fixed on Max. He’d spoken to provoke the devils, but Varok had instantly turned his words into a challenge aimed straight at Max. Saint Reiner knew Max wouldn’t back down just because his opponent held a higher realm. He also knew Max’s pride wasn’t the kind that could be easily reined in.
Still, if the fight turned too dangerous, Saint Reiner was ready to step in. No agreement between the Divine Realm and the Devil Race mattered more than Max’s life.
Max still hadn’t said anything.
Varok looked down at him, his expression now dripping with open provocation.
"So, Primordial?" His voice slowed down, turning mocking. "Are you ready to fight a devil at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm?"

The devils behind Varok grinned coldly. One of them stepped forward. He stood taller than Varok, his massive body covered in dark crimson tattoos. His horns curved backward like blades, and black fire flickered around his shoulders.

His aura clearly sat at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm, but the pressure he gave off ran far stronger than an ordinary cultivator at that level. His body carried the brutal strength of the Devil Race, and his eyes gleamed with bloodthirsty excitement.
He looked at Max like he’d already found his prey.
"A Primordial at the 1st level?" the devil said with a deep laugh. "Young master, you’re honoring him too much by sending me."
Varok chuckled. "Don’t underestimate him too much. Apparently he’s the strongest young genius of this universe."
The devil’s laughter grew louder.
Several Divine Realm geniuses showed their anger openly.
Orion clenched his fists. "This bastard."
Damian’s face turned colder. "He’s trying to use Max to humiliate all of us."
Ervin sneered lightly. "Let him try. Now that Max has reached the Law Manifestation Realm, I have a feeling he’s gotten even harder to gauge right now. We’re about to see a good show."
Only Revona looked at Max with a solemn expression. Nobody knew exactly what was going through her mind.
Max stood at the center of the temporary battlefield with Dragonheart in hand.

Across from him, Raghor, the devil chosen by Varok, grinned with savage confidence. His massive body was covered in dark crimson devil tattoos, and black flames flickered around his shoulders like a cloak of living malice.

He sat at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm, four minor realms above Max, and as a member of the Devil Race, his true combat power naturally outpaced ordinary cultivators at the same level.
To most people, this should have been a hard fight. To Varok, it should have been a humiliation set up for the Divine Realm.
But Max looked calm. Too calm.
Raghor noticed that calm, and his grin slowly turned cruel. "Still looking confident, huh. Good. I hate killing prey that trembles too early."
Max looked at him without much feeling.
"I’ll accept this fight," Max said slowly. "But it has to be a life-and-death battle. Otherwise, I’m not interested in entertaining a bunch of stupid devils."
The moment those words fell, the council domain went silent.
Varok was stunned for a brief moment. Then his eyes narrowed. He couldn’t tell whether the Primordial boy in front of him was a peerless genius or a complete idiot.

A 1st level Law Manifestation Realm cultivator was actually asking for a life-and-death battle against a devil at the 5th level of the same realm. Even among the Devil Race, that kind of arrogance would be considered absurd unless someone had absolute confidence behind it.

The leaders of the top first-rate forces were surprised too. They already knew Max wasn’t simple. They’d heard about his performance, his breakthrough, and the shocking events inside the Five Sacred Clan domain. Some had personally felt the strange pressure hidden in his body.
Even so, asking for a life-and-death battle under these circumstances still went beyond what they’d expected.
Saint Reiner’s eyes turned colder. He didn’t stop Max, but the war intent around him sharpened faintly.
Max didn’t look back. His gaze stayed on Varok. "So, what’ll it be, Varok?"
Varok stared at him for a second. Then he laughed.
"Hahaha!"
His laughter spread through the council domain, dripping with contempt and amusement.
"I’ve seen arrogant fools before, but I’ve never seen an idiot quite like you. Since you’re so eager to die, I suppose I have no reason to refuse."
He turned to Raghor. "Go ahead and kill him."
Raghor’s grin widened. "My pleasure, young master."

The massive devil rolled his shoulders as he looked at Max with utter disdain. The devil tattoos across his body began to glow, and dark energy surged around him like smoke rising off a battlefield soaked in blood.
"Dying in front of all these Primordials and leaders of your universe must be pretty embarrassing, don’t you think?" Raghor said with a deep laugh.

His devil aura erupted. The battlefield beneath his feet trembled, and the black flames around him roared higher. His law manifestation started forming behind him, taking shape as a vast devil furnace filled with charred bones, screaming shadows, and burning crimson chains.
The pressure it released turned several weaker descendants of the Divine Realm pale.
Max smiled faintly at the sight.
"What morons you devils are...."

Before Raghor’s expression could even change, a blue void ring flashed out from Max’s body. It moved too fast. The ring didn’t travel like a normal attack. It folded through space, appeared in front of Raghor almost instantly, and wrapped around his body before his devil aura could fully erupt.
Raghor’s eyes went wide. "What?"

The void ring expanded. A blue transparent sphere formed around him in an instant. The devil furnace behind him froze. The black flames around his body froze. Even the crimson tattoos glowing across his skin dimmed, as if the connection between his body and the world around him had been cut off.
Raghor tried to move, but his limbs didn’t respond. He tried to circulate his devil power, but the energy inside him turned sluggish. He tried to roar, but even his voice got trapped in his throat.
He’d been sealed. Not restrained. Not slowed. Sealed. His entire body hung suspended in midair, frozen in a separate layer of space.
The expressions of the devils changed. Varok’s smile stiffened.

Before anyone could react, Max moved. His figure vanished from where he stood and reappeared directly in front of Raghor. His right hand transformed mid-motion, pale human fingers turning into terrifying dragon claws covered in black scales.

The claws carried the brutal strength of the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, the sharpness of his Law Manifestation Realm foundation, and the condensed force of a body strengthened well beyond ordinary limits.
Raghor’s eyes trembled with horror. He still couldn’t move.

chapters.title: Chapter 2012: A Sneak Attack!
paragraphs: The next instant, Max thrust his dragon claws forward.
Puchi!
His claws pierced through Raghor’s chest and came out through his back.

The battlefield fell silent. The devil’s eyes bulged. The law manifestation behind him shattered before it could fully take shape. The devil furnace collapsed into black sparks, the crimson chains dissolved into smoke, and the dark flames around his body died out like candles caught in a storm.
Raghor stared at Max in disbelief, as if he still couldn’t understand how the battle had ended before it had really begun.
Max pulled his claws out. Raghor’s body fell from the air and crashed onto the battlefield.
The blue void ring returned to Max’s side, rotating silently beside his shoulder.
The massive devil didn’t move again. He was dead.. A devil at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm had been killed in a single exchange.

For a moment, no one spoke. The leaders of the Divine Realm stared at Max with different reactions. Some looked shocked. Some looked thoughtful. Some looked pleased. Garron Aresvale of the War God Palace laughed loudly, his voice full of fierce satisfaction.

Celian Voss of the Sword God Palace looked at the void ring with a rare trace of interest. High Lord Astren Vale’s nine stars rotated faster behind him, as if his calculations had just shifted. Even the Four Sacred Clans fell into a deep silence, their gazes fixed on Max with complicated emotions.

The nine geniuses reacted too. Orion’s eyes shone with excitement. Damian’s expression grew even more serious. Ervin let out a soft breath, while Morgana smiled like she’d just watched something extremely entertaining. Revona stared at Max without a word, but her eyes carried a depth that hadn’t been there before.
Saint Reiner slowly unclenched his fist. A faint smile crossed the old saint’s face.
"Good," he muttered.
Max didn’t look at the fallen devil. He raised his head and looked at Varok.
"Are you happy now?"
His voice came out calm. There was no arrogance in it. That only made the humiliation worse.

Varok’s expression had gone completely dark. The mockery on his face was gone. The amusement was gone. Even the earlier arrogance that had filled his eyes had faded, replaced by something far colder and more dangerous. He stared at Raghor’s corpse, then slowly shifted his gaze back to Max.

A devil from his camp had been killed. And not after a long battle, but in an instant. The Divine Realm’s side hadn’t just defended its dignity. Max had crushed the trap Varok set and turned it right back on him, in front of every major force present.
But that wasn’t what truly disturbed Varok. What truly disturbed him was Max himself.
Varok’s eyes narrowed as he stared at the blue void ring floating beside Max.

’A 1st level Law Manifestation Realm cultivator sealed Raghor before he could even react. His body strength is abnormal. His bloodline aura runs layered. Dragon power, Primordial power, sealing power colder than ordinary law. This isn’t a normal genius.’
His expression stayed dark, but his thoughts raced.
’The Primordial Race has produced a rare monster.’
Varok’s gaze turned even more vicious.
’No. Not just rare. Dangerous.’

He’d seen plenty of geniuses in the Devil Universe. Some had terrifying bloodlines. Some had monstrous bodies. Some were blessed by Primal Treasures. Some could cross realms and slaughter enemies stronger than themselves.

But Max was different. His realm sat low, yet his foundation felt impossibly dense. His powers weren’t scattered like a kid collecting treasures. They were beginning to fuse into a real combat system, one that could threaten beings far above him.
If someone like Max was allowed to grow, he’d become a problem. Not just for Varok. For the entire Devil Race.

’If he reaches the Divine Lord Realm, ordinary young devils might not be able to touch him. If he reaches the Divine King Realm, he could become a real obstacle in the coming war. If he lives long enough to mature, he might turn into one of the blades that cuts straight into our invasion.’
A cold decision formed in Varok’s heart.
’He cannot be allowed to grow.’

The Pearl of Abyss shifted beneath his sleeve. It had stayed quiet until now, hidden under his aura and the pressure of the devils around him. But the moment Varok made his decision, a dark pulse flowed from the pearl into his palm.
Varok’s face stayed still. No one saw him raise his hand. No one heard him chant. The Pearl of Abyss didn’t need such obvious movements.

A thin black line appeared behind Max. It was almost invisible. It didn’t tear open space violently. It simply appeared, as if a piece of reality had quietly been erased. From that erased line, an abyssal spike emerged, silent and cold, carrying a power that didn’t belong to ordinary law.
The spike moved toward the back of Max’s head. Fast. Silent. Deadly.
Max’s eyes changed. At the last moment, a warning exploded inside his senses. His Dimensional Sovereign Body trembled. His Primordial Bloodline and Voidwalker bloodline pulsed violently.
’Danger.’

The attack was already behind him. Max didn’t try to block it. He knew instantly this wasn’t something he should take head-on. The aura carried by the abyssal spike felt too strange. It didn’t feel like a normal attack from Varok.
It felt deeper, colder, and far more ancient, like it had come from a darkness that existed before worlds were even separated.
Pearl of Abyss.
The realization flashed through Max’s mind.

Without hesitation, Max activated the entrance to the Dimension of Time. His figure blurred. The abyssal spike pierced forward, but just before it touched him, Max disappeared. The attack passed through the space where he’d stood and struck empty air.
For one breath, the council domain froze. Then the entire sky erupted.
"Varok!"
Arvantos’s voice thundered through the council domain.
The four Primarchs moved at the same time. Arvantos appeared above the battlefield, his golden primordial aura spreading across the sky like a vast divine curtain.

Eryndor stepped to his left, his bronze-gold body releasing crushing physical pressure that made the air collapse layer by layer. Lysandra appeared to his right, silver-gold runes flowing around her as she locked onto every trace of abyssal energy in the area. Veyrion appeared behind them, and the space around the battlefield folded into countless invisible barriers.
In an instant, the four Primarchs formed a defensive formation. They didn’t attack right away. They stayed wary. Not of Varok himself. Of the Pearl of Abyss.
A Primal Treasure couldn’t be treated casually. Even with their strength, they couldn’t assume suppressing Varok would come easy while he held one of the five Primal Treasures.
If the Pearl of Abyss erupted fully inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain, the consequences might go beyond even what they could predict.

The leaders of the top first-rate forces reacted too. Garron Aresvale’s battle aura exploded like a war sun. Celian Voss’s sword intent filled the sky. Astren Vale’s nine stars formed a calculation array behind him. Seraphis Kael raised one hand, and the Stellar Templar instantly locked into a battle formation.
Queen Selene Lunaris summoned a pale moon barrier. Lord Vael Noxis distorted the void near the devils. Hall Master Orin Caldus opened an ancient law scroll that released sealing light.
The Four Sacred Clans released their auras too. For a moment, the devils found themselves surrounded by the full pressure of the Divine Realm’s peak forces.
Varok stood at the center of that pressure. His face had gone pale. A thin line of dark blood slid from the corner of his mouth. The Pearl of Abyss hovered above his palm now, no longer fully hidden.
It looked like a small black pearl, smooth and bottomless, with faint rings of abyssal light rotating inside it. Looking at it felt like staring into a hole that led beneath reality itself.
Around the pearl, space didn’t crack. It sank. Light didn’t scatter. It disappeared. Laws didn’t break apart. They got swallowed into a depth that refused to reveal its limit.

This was the true terror of the Pearl of Abyss. It didn’t simply release destructive power. It opened a connection to the abyss itself. Any attack born from it could ignore many ordinary defenses, since it didn’t need to break through them the normal way.

It could erase a path through space, appear behind a target, bury itself inside their body, and drag their flesh, soul, bloodline, or laws into abyssal collapse. Used fully, it could open abyssal passages, hide traces from fate, devour surrounding energy, and blur the boundary between worlds.
It was a treasure capable of turning a single moment of carelessness into death.

But Varok wasn’t its true master. At least, not yet. His cultivation only sat at the Divine King Realm. That realm was already powerful by normal standards, but it wasn’t enough to freely control a Primal Treasure.
The Pearl of Abyss had answered him because of his bloodline, status, and preparation, but using it still came with a price. The moment the sneak attack failed, the backlash hit him.

Dark veins appeared along Varok’s wrist. The abyssal patterns crawled up his arm before slowly sinking back into his flesh. His aura turned unstable for a brief moment, and the devils behind him immediately stepped forward in alarm.
"Young master!"
Varok raised one hand, stopping them. His expression looked ugly. He’d paid the price, yet the attack had still failed. Max had escaped.
The spot where Max had stood now sat empty, but everyone knew he wasn’t dead. He’d vanished somewhere at the very last moment, dodging the Pearl of Abyss’s strike by a hair.

Seraphis Kael raised one hand, and the Stellar Templar instantly locked into a battle formation.
Queen Selene Lunaris summoned a pale moon barrier.
Lord Vael Noxis distorted the void near the devils.
Hall Master Orin Caldus opened an ancient law scroll that released sealing light.
The Four Sacred Clans released their auras too.
For a moment, the devils found themselves surrounded by the full pressure of the Divine Realm’s peak forces.
Varok stood at the center of that pressure.
His face had gone pale.
A thin line of dark blood slid from the corner of his mouth.
The Pearl of Abyss hovered above his palm now, no longer fully hidden.
It looked like a small black pearl, smooth and bottomless, with faint rings of abyssal light rotating inside it.
Looking at it felt like staring into a hole that led beneath reality itself.
Around the pearl, space didn’t crack.
It sank.
Light didn’t scatter.
It disappeared.
Laws didn’t break apart.
They got swallowed into a depth that refused to reveal its limit.
This was the true terror of the Pearl of Abyss.
It didn’t simply release destructive power.
It opened a connection to the abyss itself.
Any attack born from it could ignore many ordinary defenses, since it didn’t need to break through them the normal way.
It could erase a path through space, appear behind a target, bury itself inside their body, and drag their flesh, soul, bloodline, or laws into abyssal collapse.
Used fully, it could open abyssal passages, hide traces from fate, devour surrounding energy, and blur the boundary between worlds.
It was a treasure capable of turning a single moment of carelessness into death.
But Varok wasn’t its true master.
At least, not yet.
His cultivation only sat at the Divine King Realm.
That realm was already powerful by normal standards, but it wasn’t enough to freely control a Primal Treasure.
The Pearl of Abyss had answered him because of his bloodline, status, and preparation, but using it still came with a price.
The moment the sneak attack failed, the backlash hit him.
Dark veins appeared along Varok’s wrist.
The abyssal patterns crawled up his arm before slowly sinking back into his flesh.
His aura turned unstable for a brief moment, and the devils behind him immediately stepped forward in alarm.
"Young master!"
Varok raised one hand, stopping them.
His expression looked ugly.
He’d paid the price, yet the attack had still failed.
Max had escaped.
The spot where Max had stood now sat empty, but everyone knew he wasn’t dead.
He’d vanished somewhere at the very last moment, dodging the Pearl of Abyss’s strike by a hair.

chapters.title: Chapter 2013: End of the Meeting!
paragraphs: Lysandra’s eyes turned cold. "You used a Primal Treasure to sneak attack a junior during an agreed battle."
Eryndor’s voice carried heavy killing intent. "You truly want war."
Veyrion stared at the Pearl of Abyss. "Careful. The treasure’s still active."
Arvantos looked at Varok, and for the first time since the meeting began, his calm expression showed a trace of terrifying anger.
"Varok," he said slowly. "Explain yourself."
Varok wiped the blood from the corner of his mouth. His expression stayed dark, but his eyes still carried stubborn arrogance.
"That Primordial killed one of my people."
Garron Aresvale laughed coldly. "In a life-and-death battle you agreed to."
Celian Voss’s voice came out quiet. "And you answered by ambushing him with a Primal Treasure."

Saint Reiner’s face had gone colder than anyone else’s. His war intent had grown so dense that the space around him trembled. If not for the four Primarchs standing between both sides and the Pearl of Abyss still pulsing in Varok’s hand, he would have already crossed the battlefield.
"That was my student," Saint Reiner said. His voice came out low, but everyone heard it. "If he dies because of your sneak attack, no agreement will save you."

Varok’s eyes flickered. The pressure coming from all sides was terrifying. Even with the Pearl of Abyss, he knew he couldn’t act recklessly again. He’d already suffered backlash from one silent strike.
If he forced the pearl to erupt while surrounded by the four Primarchs and the strongest forces of the Divine Realm, the outcome might slip out of his control.
The pearl could protect him. It could threaten them. But it could also consume him if he tried to push power beyond what his realm could handle.
For the first time, Varok felt the danger of standing in another universe.
Then space trembled softly above the battlefield. A silver ripple opened. Max stepped out of it.
His expression stayed calm, but his eyes had gone much colder than before. The Dimension of Time had saved him, but the fact remained that he’d nearly been killed.

If his Dimensional Keeper Legacy had warned him even a fraction later, if his reaction had been slower, if the entrance to the Dimension of Time had failed to open in time, that abyssal spike would have gone straight through his head.
Max looked at the Pearl of Abyss in Varok’s hand. Then he looked at Varok.
"One day I’ll return that a hundredfold."
Varok didn’t answer him. For a few breaths, he just stared. Seeing Max standing there alive and unharmed after dodging the Pearl of Abyss made Varok feel even worse than before.

Raghor had been killed in front of everyone, his sneak attack had failed, and the Primordial he wanted erased had returned with the same calm expression, as if even a Primal Treasure hadn’t been enough to truly scare him.

That silence stung worse than any insult. Varok’s hatred for Max climbed to a whole new level. Before this, Max had been a troublesome genius who might become an obstacle down the road. Now, in Varok’s eyes, he’d become someone who had to die.
A young Primordial with that kind of talent, that kind of reaction speed, that kind of strange escape method, and that kind of fearless attitude couldn’t be allowed to grow freely.
If Max survived a few more centuries, he might become one of the most dangerous enemies the Devil Race would ever face inside this universe.
But Varok couldn’t make another move now. The four Primarchs were already watching him with cold eyes. The leaders of the top first-rate forces had locked their auras onto him too.
Saint Reiner’s killing intent felt especially terrifying, and Varok could tell the old saint of the War God Palace was only waiting for one excuse to act.

Even with the Pearl of Abyss in his possession, Varok knew he couldn’t keep pushing the situation. He’d already suffered backlash from using the treasure once, and if he forced it again surrounded by this many peak experts, the outcome might not stay within his control.
The Pearl of Abyss was powerful. But it wasn’t something his current cultivation could use without a cost.

Varok slowly wiped the dark blood from the corner of his mouth. His expression settled back into calm, but that calm only made the hatred hiding beneath it feel more dangerous. He looked away from Max and turned to the four Primarchs.
"We have our agreement," Varok said coldly. "Now it’s time for us to leave."
The four primarchs became silent hearing him. They knew that if the devils wanted to leave they couldn’t stop them since they possessed the Pearl of Abyss. And so they didn’t even try to stop them.
Arvantos looked at him without any warmth. "Remember the terms."
Primarch Eryndor’s voice followed like a heavy mountain pressing down from the heavens. "If your devils break them, there will be no second negotiation."
Lysandra’s silver-gold eyes stayed fixed on the Pearl of Abyss. "And if you use that treasure carelessly inside our universe again, don’t assume your father’s name will protect you."
Veyrion said nothing, but the space around the devils tightened faintly, as if reminding them their retreat was being allowed, not overlooked.

Varok’s fingers curled around the Pearl of Abyss. A dark, radiant light flashed from the pearl. For an instant, the sky above the grand council domain seemed to sink into a bottomless darkness. The devils behind Varok got swallowed by that abyssal glow one after another, their figures twisting like shadows reflected on deep water.
Varok’s gaze stayed on Max until the very last moment. The hatred in his eyes was unmistakable.
Max looked back at him calmly. Neither of them said anything.
Then the abyssal light surged. A moment later, Varok and the remaining devils vanished from the council domain.
The black mist in the sky slowly faded. The pressure left behind by the Pearl of Abyss lingered for a few breaths before the primordial light of the ancestral domain washed it away.
No one moved right away. The agreement had been made. The devils had retreated.
But everyone present understood this wasn’t the end of the conflict.
It was only the beginning.

chapters.title: Chapter 2014: A Path Beyond the Seven Divine Veins!
paragraphs: After Varok and the devils disappeared, the meeting finally came to an end.

The outcome wasn’t a surprise. In truth, everyone present had already sensed the likely result before the meeting even started. The Divine Realm wasn’t in a position to launch a full war against the Devil Race right now.

The hole in the Wall of Eternity was still small, the devils inside their universe were limited in number, and the older generation needed time to prepare. Because of all that, flat-out rejecting Varok’s demands had never been the realistic option.

What actually mattered wasn’t whether the Divine Realm would agree to his conditions. What mattered was how many restrictions they could squeeze into the agreement. That was the whole reason for the meeting.
The Devil Race had gotten permission to set up a force in the Divine Realm, but that permission came with chains attached.

They’d be watched. Their movements would get recorded. They’d be forbidden from entering the Mortal Realm. They’d face punishment if they harmed, corrupted, enslaved, or secretly controlled the people of the Divine Realm.
The devils had won a foothold, but the Divine Realm had made sure that foothold wouldn’t turn into a free path to spread unchecked.
Even so, nobody looked relaxed.
The strongest first-rate forces started leaving one after another.

The War God Palace, Sword God Palace, Ascension Hall, Nine Star Court, Grand Void Sanctum, Stellar Templar, and Lunarian Kingdom all exchanged a few brief words with the four Primarchs before preparing to head out.
Their leaders didn’t speak loudly, but the solemn look on their faces made it clear each force had already started thinking about the future.

The years ahead wouldn’t be peaceful. Defense lines needed strengthening, disciples needed warning, hidden spies needed rooting out, and every major force had to prepare for a possible war that might arrive within five hundred years, or even sooner.

The Four Sacred Clans stayed quiet too. Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest had walked into this meeting carrying their own internal conflict, but after watching the devils and seeing Varok try to use the Pearl of Abyss on Max, even they understood the Divine Realm now faced a far bigger threat.
Whatever resentment and suspicion still lingered between them and the Voidwalker Clan couldn’t be allowed to weaken the whole universe.
Max stood silently near the Primordial side, watching the great forces leave. His fight with Raghor had ended quickly, but its impact hadn’t faded.

Plenty of gazes still drifted toward him before turning away. Some carried approval. Some carried curiosity. Some carried caution. Some carried the complicated mix of emotions from people who’d just realized this 1st level Law Manifestation Realm youth couldn’t be measured by normal rules.
Just then, Saint Reiner walked toward him from the War God Palace’s side.
The old saint’s aura had softened compared to when Varok attacked. He looked calmer now, though the deep battle intent around him hadn’t fully faded.
His long silver hair moved slightly as he approached, and the scars across his dark gold and crimson armor looked even more ancient under the fading light of the council domain.
He stopped in front of Max and looked at him for a moment. Then he laughed and patted him on the shoulder.
"Haha, you did well, kid," Saint Reiner said. "Those devils really thought they could do whatever they wanted inside our universe. How stupid."
Max smiled lightly. "They were pretty stupid, yeah."

Saint Reiner’s laughter faded into a satisfied grin, but his eyes soon turned more serious. He looked Max over closely, as if examining the changes in his body with a gaze sharpened by countless years of body cultivation.
Then his expression shifted.
"I can see it," Saint Reiner said. "You’ve unlocked the fifth vein of the Seven Divine Veins."
Max’s eyes moved slightly.
Saint Reiner nodded with clear approval. "The Vein of Resilience. Good boy. With this, you’ve officially surpassed every single person in the Divine Realm who’s ever opened the Seven Divine Veins."

His words carried real pride. Saint Reiner had always been strict with Max, and he wasn’t someone who handed out praise easily. His whole path revolved around war, body cultivation, and endless tempering. Getting approval like that from him meant Max had truly achieved something extraordinary.

Saint Reiner continued, "I told you before that only the Primordials had ever managed to reach the fourth Divine Vein, and that wasn’t wrong. Among the Primordial Race, there’s one existence who opened the fourth vein with the help of a complete technique, a natural primordial body, and countless resources accumulated by the oldest force in the Divine Realm."
He paused for a moment. "Even for that person, going beyond the fourth Divine Vein was impossible."
Max listened quietly.

Saint Reiner looked at him and smiled with rare pride. "But you, Max, have done what nobody else in the Divine Realm has managed. Not the War God Palace. Not the Sword God Palace. Not the Four Sacred Clans. Not even the Primordial Race. You’ve opened the fifth Divine Vein and reached the Vein of Resilience. From this point on, when it comes to the Seven Divine Veins, you’ve officially surpassed everyone in this universe."
His hand tightened slightly on Max’s shoulder. "You did well."
Max nodded lightly, but the curiosity in his eyes didn’t fade.

After a brief silence, he asked, "In your inheritance, you mentioned that beyond the Seven Divine Veins, there’s an even higher body cultivation path. You also said the Seven Divine Veins are only the foundation needed to reach that higher path."
Saint Reiner’s smile slowly faded.
Max’s expression sharpened as he pressed on. "Can you tell me more about that?"

Saint Reiner sighed. For a moment, the old saint looked far older than before. His eyes, filled with pride just a breath ago, now carried the regret of a man who’d chased a path for countless years without ever finding its end.

"The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins is the thing that’s eluded me the most," he said slowly. "In all my research, all my battles, all my studies of ancient body cultivation methods, and all the ruins I explored, I found plenty of fragments pointing to its existence. But fragments are only fragments. I know that path exists for certain, but sadly, I don’t know much about it."

chapters.title: Chapter 2015: Library of the Primordials!
paragraphs: Max frowned slightly.

Saint Reiner continued, "When I first got my hands on the incomplete Seven Divine Veins method, it was broken beyond recognition. Most people would’ve written it off as some ancient body cultivation remnant with no real value. I spent centuries researching it, comparing it against lost techniques, studying old battle records, digging through forbidden ruins, and testing it on myself over and over. Only after all that did I manage to complete the Seven Divine Veins."

His voice grew heavier. "But while completing it, I found something strange. The Seven Divine Veins didn’t feel like the end of a body cultivation path. They felt like preparation. Each vein strengthens one part of the body’s foundation, but together, they seem built to support something far greater."

Saint Reiner looked directly at Max. "The Origin Vein strengthens the root of physical existence. The Vitality Vein strengthens recovery and life force. The Speed Vein strengthens movement and reaction. The Strength Vein strengthens raw physical force. The Resilience Vein strengthens endurance and resistance. The remaining veins, if you manage to open them, should round out the body’s balance. Once all seven exist together, I believe they form the true foundation needed to step into a higher body cultivation realm."
Max’s eyes sharpened. "What’s that higher realm called?"
Saint Reiner shook his head. "I don’t know."
Max fell silent.

Saint Reiner’s expression carried regret, but his voice stayed steady. "That’s the part I never found. I searched for names, records, techniques, and inheritance fragments, but everything beyond the Seven Divine Veins was either erased, hidden, or never properly passed down in this universe. All I can tell you is this. The Seven Divine Veins aren’t the final destination. They’re the gate."
"I see," Max said softly, his frown deepening slightly.
If even Saint Reiner didn’t have a clear answer about the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, finding clues would be extremely hard. Saint Reiner wasn’t an ordinary elder.

He was one of the greatest body cultivation experts in the Divine Realm, and he’d spent centuries studying this exact path. If even he’d only turned up fragments, the truth behind the higher body cultivation path had to be buried incredibly deep.
Saint Reiner noticed Max’s expression and smiled again. "Don’t look so discouraged."
Max looked at him.
"I don’t have the answer," Saint Reiner said. "But that doesn’t mean nobody does."
"Who does?" Max asked, curious.
"The Primordial Race," Saint Reiner replied solemnly, his gaze shifting toward the ancient halls of the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

"They’re the oldest force in the Divine Realm. Their history stretches back further than every palace, court, kingdom, sanctum, hall, and sacred clan gathered here today. If anyone in this universe has records about the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, it’d most likely be them."

Saint Reiner looked back at Max. "You’re a Primordial now. Use that. Visit the library of the Primordial Race. Search through their ancient records. Look for anything tied to body cultivation, divine veins, primordial physique, origin body, or paths beyond the seven veins. If there’s even a small clue anywhere, it should be there."
Max nodded. "I will."
Saint Reiner patted his shoulder again, this time with more weight behind it.

"Take care of yourself, kid," he said. "Things are about to get wild in our universe. The devils have gotten in, the Wall of Eternity’s been pierced, and forces that stayed silent for countless years might start moving again. You need to get stronger fast."
His old eyes sharpened once more. "And the next time I see you, I’d better see you go beyond the Seven Divine Veins."
Max’s expression turned solemn. "I’ll try my best."
Saint Reiner gave a satisfied nod. "Good."

He turned and walked back toward the War God Palace delegation, who were already waiting for him near the edge of the council domain. Garron Aresvale glanced at Max with a fierce grin before leading the warriors of the War God Palace into a glowing spatial passage.
Saint Reiner went in last. Before disappearing, he looked back one more time.
Max met his gaze from a distance. No more words passed between them.
A moment later, the spatial passage closed, and the War God Palace vanished from the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
Max stood where he was, Saint Reiner’s words still echoing in his mind.
The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins. The library of the Primordial Race.
The next day, Primarch Arvantos gathered the ten young Primordials once again.
This time, they weren’t in the grand council domain where the meeting with the devils had taken place. Instead, Arvantos brought them into a quieter hall inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

The hall was vast but not oppressive. Its walls were made of ancient bronze-gold stone, and countless faint runes flowed across them like silent rivers of light. A wide window opened on one side of the hall, showing off the magnificent scenery of the Primordial Ancestral Domain outside.

From where Max stood, he could see floating mountains drifting above golden clouds. Ancient palaces sat on distant peaks, primordial law rivers flowed through the sky, and enormous stone statues of forgotten experts watched over the domain like guardians from the earliest era of the universe.
The whole place carried a sense of age that couldn’t be found anywhere else in the Divine Realm.
Arvantos stood in front of the window with his hands behind his back. After a moment, he finally spoke.
"Now that the meeting with the devils has wrapped up, it’s time to talk about the truly important matter."
His voice stayed calm, but every word carried weight. He kept looking through the window for a few more breaths before turning toward Max and the others.

"The agreement with Varok only delayed the problem. It didn’t solve anything. The devils have gained a foothold in the Divine Realm, the Wall of Eternity has been pierced, and the Devil Race is still trying to widen the breach from the other side. If nothing changes, a true war is coming sooner or later."
The expressions of the ten geniuses turned serious.

sentences.text: Max frowned slightly.
Saint Reiner continued, "When I first got my hands on the incomplete Seven Divine Veins method, it was broken beyond recognition.
Most people would’ve written it off as some ancient body cultivation remnant with no real value.
I spent centuries researching it, comparing it against lost techniques, studying old battle records, digging through forbidden ruins, and testing it on myself over and over.
Only after all that did I manage to complete the Seven Divine Veins."
His voice grew heavier.
"But while completing it, I found something strange.
The Seven Divine Veins didn’t feel like the end of a body cultivation path.
They felt like preparation.
Each vein strengthens one part of the body’s foundation, but together, they seem built to support something far greater."
Saint Reiner looked directly at Max.
"The Origin Vein strengthens the root of physical existence.
The Vitality Vein strengthens recovery and life force.
The Speed Vein strengthens movement and reaction.
The Strength Vein strengthens raw physical force.
The Resilience Vein strengthens endurance and resistance.
The remaining veins, if you manage to open them, should round out the body’s balance.
Once all seven exist together, I believe they form the true foundation needed to step into a higher body cultivation realm."
Max’s eyes sharpened.
"What’s that higher realm called?"
Saint Reiner shook his head.
"I don’t know."
Max fell silent.
Saint Reiner’s expression carried regret, but his voice stayed steady.
"That’s the part I never found.
I searched for names, records, techniques, and inheritance fragments, but everything beyond the Seven Divine Veins was either erased, hidden, or never properly passed down in this universe.
All I can tell you is this.
The Seven Divine Veins aren’t the final destination.
They’re the gate."
"I see," Max said softly, his frown deepening slightly.
If even Saint Reiner didn’t have a clear answer about the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, finding clues would be extremely hard.
Saint Reiner wasn’t an ordinary elder.
He was one of the greatest body cultivation experts in the Divine Realm, and he’d spent centuries studying this exact path.
If even he’d only turned up fragments, the truth behind the higher body cultivation path had to be buried incredibly deep.
Saint Reiner noticed Max’s expression and smiled again.
"Don’t look so discouraged."
Max looked at him.
"I don’t have the answer," Saint Reiner said.
"But that doesn’t mean nobody does."
"Who does?" Max asked, curious.
"The Primordial Race," Saint Reiner replied solemnly, his gaze shifting toward the ancient halls of the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
"They’re the oldest force in the Divine Realm.
Their history stretches back further than every palace, court, kingdom, sanctum, hall, and sacred clan gathered here today.
If anyone in this universe has records about the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, it’d most likely be them."
Saint Reiner looked back at Max.
"You’re a Primordial now.
Use that.
Visit the library of the Primordial Race.
Search through their ancient records.
Look for anything tied to body cultivation, divine veins, primordial physique, origin body, or paths beyond the seven veins.
If there’s even a small clue anywhere, it should be there."
Max nodded.
"I will."
Saint Reiner patted his shoulder again, this time with more weight behind it.
"Take care of yourself, kid," he said.
"Things are about to get wild in our universe.
The devils have gotten in, the Wall of Eternity’s been pierced, and forces that stayed silent for countless years might start moving again.
You need to get stronger fast."
His old eyes sharpened once more.
"And the next time I see you, I’d better see you go beyond the Seven Divine Veins."
Max’s expression turned solemn.
"I’ll try my best."
Saint Reiner gave a satisfied nod.
"Good."
He turned and walked back toward the War God Palace delegation, who were already waiting for him near the edge of the council domain.
Garron Aresvale glanced at Max with a fierce grin before leading the warriors of the War God Palace into a glowing spatial passage.
Saint Reiner went in last.
Before disappearing, he looked back one more time.
Max met his gaze from a distance.
No more words passed between them.
A moment later, the spatial passage closed, and the War God Palace vanished from the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
Max stood where he was, Saint Reiner’s words still echoing in his mind.
The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins.
The library of the Primordial Race.

chapters.title: Chapter 2016: Three Ways!
paragraphs: Arvantos’s gaze swept across them. "You’re all talented. Each of you stood at the peak of the Cosmic Ascension Conference, and each of you now carries a Primordial Bloodline. Some of you have already awakened bloodline abilities. Some have already stepped into the Divine Lord Realm. Some of you have inheritances, physiques, talents, and backgrounds ordinary cultivators could never dream of."
His eyes paused on Max for a brief moment before moving on.
"But talent alone isn’t enough."
The hall grew even quieter.

Arvantos went on, "Given the current situation, normal growth in the Divine Realm won’t be enough for any of you. If you cultivate naturally, even with your talent, most of you would need thousands of years, maybe longer, to reach the Holy King Realm or Divine Master Realm. Only after reaching those stages would you truly have the strength to influence the war between universes."
Orion frowned. "Thousands of years?"

Arvantos nodded. "That’s already a generous estimate. You need to understand that the higher the cultivation realm, the slower progress gets. In the early stages, a genius can break through several minor realms in a short stretch of time. But once you pass the Divine Lord Realm, Divine King Realm, Holy Lord Realm, Holy King Realm, and Divine Master Realm, every step demands far more than just energy. You need comprehension, foundation, law refinement, bloodline stability, soul strength, and opportunities that suit your path."

His voice deepened. "Plenty of geniuses who once shook the Divine Realm turned ordinary after reaching the higher realms because they lacked one of those things. Some had talent but no opportunity. Some had opportunity but no foundation. Some had foundation but lacked the courage to risk their lives. Some simply hit the limit of what their bloodline and comprehension could support."

Max listened silently. He understood this better than most. His own growth had been fast, but it had never come easy. Every major jump in strength had come from terrifying inheritances, dangerous trials, hidden dimensions, cosmic paths, bloodlines, and battles where death had never sat far away.
Arvantos continued, "But we don’t have thousands of years." His gaze sharpened. "I want all of you to reach that level of strength within five hundred years."
The ten geniuses fell silent. Even Damian’s cold expression shifted slightly.
Five hundred years. Reaching the Holy King Realm or even the Divine Master Realm in five hundred years was an outrageous goal.
For ordinary cultivators, even imagining something like that would sound laughable. But Arvantos wasn’t speaking like it was a joke. He spoke like it was the bare minimum.

"You’re the future hope of this universe," Arvantos said. "Old people like me will lead the war if it comes. The Primarchs, the ancient experts, the masters of the first-rate forces, and the hidden protectors of the Divine Realm will stand at the front. But wars between universes aren’t won by old strength alone. The older generation can defend. We can delay. We can hold the line. But the younger generation is the one that creates variables."

His eyes swept across them again. "A young genius who rises fast enough can break the balance. A cultivator who reaches a realm earlier than expected can change a battlefield. A monster who survives where others die can become a blade no enemy saw coming. That’s why the devils are dangerous, and that’s exactly why all of you matter."
Max’s gaze deepened slightly.
Arvantos continued, "If you stay protected inside the Divine Realm and grow slowly, you might become powerful one day, but that day might come too late. So we need to pick a faster path."
Orion’s eyes lit up slightly. "What path?"
Arvantos smiled faintly. "There are only three real ways for all of you to get stronger quickly."
The moment he said it, the attention of the ten geniuses sharpened even further.
Orion immediately asked, "What three ways?"
Arvantos looked at him with a faint smile. "The first and easiest way is the Primordial Race."
The answer surprised no one, but everyone listened closely.

Arvantos said, "If you want, I can summon great experts from our race to personally guide each of you. We can give you cultivation grounds, bloodline pools, law towers, ancient scriptures, combat instructors, soul tempering formations, divine medicines, and resources even many first-rate forces can’t easily offer. With the foundation you already have, I can guarantee every one of you will at least reach the Holy Lord Realm within the five hundred years we have."

That statement shook a few of the geniuses’ hearts. Holy Lord Realm within five hundred years. A promise like that would drive countless cultivators mad with envy. For most forces, producing even one Holy Lord could change their entire status. Yet Arvantos was talking about the Primordial Race forcibly nurturing ten of them within five centuries. That alone showed just how terrifying the resources and background of the oldest race in the Divine Realm really were.
But Arvantos’s expression soon turned more serious.
"That said, I don’t recommend this path unless there’s no other choice."
Damian’s eyes narrowed. "Why?"

"Because a path built purely on protection and resources is fast, but it isn’t sharp," Arvantos replied. "You’d grow stronger, sure, but your strength would come from cultivating under controlled pressure. Your foundations might look impressive, but they’d miss the tempering that comes from real danger. You’d learn techniques, improve your realms, refine your bloodlines, and strengthen your laws, but you wouldn’t go through the kind of desperate situations that force a genius to truly transform."

His voice carried a note of warning. "The Primordial Race can raise your cultivation. But if we raise you too safely, we might also make you rusty. Worse, your foundations might turn unstable because too many resources got poured into you too fast. On the surface, you’d become Holy Lords. In reality, you might end up weaker than enemies who reached the same realm through blood, battle, and life-or-death opportunities."
Morgana smiled faintly. "So it’s the comfortable path."
"Yes," Arvantos said. "And comfort is dangerous for people like you."
Damian looked at Arvantos. "Then what are the other two methods?"

His tone made it clear he had no interest in sitting inside the Primordial Race for five hundred years. Most of the others seemed to feel the same way. They were geniuses who’d fought their way to the peak of the Cosmic Ascension Conference. None of them wanted to be raised like treasures inside a protected cage.

chapters.title: Chapter 2017: Godslayer’s Pilgrimage!
paragraphs: Arvantos smiled slightly. "Have any of you heard of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage?"

The ten geniuses looked at each other. No one answered. Even Revona, who seemed to know plenty of secrets, showed a trace of confusion. Orion blinked. Ervin frowned in thought. Damian stayed quiet, but his expression made it obvious the term was new to him.
Max finally asked, "What is that?"
Arvantos’s smile faded, and his expression turned solemn.
"The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage is the highest-level opportunity available to the younger generation across all five universes."
Those words instantly changed the atmosphere in the hall.

Arvantos continued, "If the Cosmic Ascension Conference gathers the strongest geniuses of the Divine Realm from our universe, then the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage gathers the strongest geniuses from all five universes. The Primordial Universe, the Devil Universe, the Spirit Universe, the Angel Universe, and the Dragon Universe all send their most terrifying young monsters there."

The expressions of the ten geniuses shifted. All five universes. That meant they wouldn’t only be facing geniuses from the Divine Realm. They’d be facing devils born in the Devil Universe, spirits naturally close to law and life essence, angels wielding terrifying holy power and divine order, and dragons whose bodies and bloodlines ranked among the strongest in existence.

Arvantos said, "Don’t underestimate what that means. In our universe, all of you count as peak geniuses. But in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, you’ll run into beings who carry the destiny of their own universes. Some were born from royal bloodlines. Some have been trained by supreme races since childhood. Some are descendants of old monsters who fought in the last universal war. Some hold treasures, physiques, eyes, souls, and laws even I wouldn’t casually dismiss."
Orion’s excitement turned more serious. Damian’s eyes sharpened. Max stayed calm, but his interest had clearly been stirred.

Arvantos looked at them and continued, "The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t sit inside any of the five universes. It exists in a strange region beyond the Wall of Eternity, beyond the reach of the five universes, in a place where their borders overlap without fully merging. Some call it the Forgotten Crossing. Some call it the Grave Road. Some call it the Battlefield Beneath the Gods. But its true name, at least in the oldest records, is the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Why’s it called that?"
Arvantos stayed silent for a moment. Then he said, "Because according to ancient records, gods once fell there."
The hall went deathly quiet.

Arvantos continued slowly, "Not Divine Masters. Not peak experts who got worshiped as gods by weaker worlds. I’m talking about beings closer to the true meaning of that word. Whether they were real True Gods, failed True Gods, or existences who’d touched the threshold above the Divine God Realm, no one can say for certain. Too much time has passed, and too many records have been lost. But what we do know is that countless divine remnants, broken weapons, blood-stained laws, shattered thrones, and sealed inheritances got left behind there."

His voice grew deeper. "Every cycle, the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage opens up for the younger generation of the five universes. No single race controls it. And because of that, it became a battleground for geniuses from all five universes."
Ervin asked quietly, "What kind of opportunities exist there?"
Arvantos glanced at him. "Almost every kind you can imagine, and plenty you can’t."

He raised one hand, and faint images appeared in the air in front of them. Max saw a vast road made of broken stars. He saw ruined temples floating inside storms of law. He saw a battlefield where enormous bones stretched across space like mountain ranges. He saw a river of golden blood flowing against time. He saw a shattered throne surrounded by countless weapon fragments. He saw a dark valley where laws moved like living beasts.

Arvantos said, "There are inheritance grounds left behind by fallen supreme beings. There are law pools capable of pushing a cultivator’s comprehension forward by centuries. There are body tempering zones where flesh gets crushed, rebuilt, and transformed. There are soul-forging ruins where one mistake can erase the mind, but success can strengthen the soul beyond ordinary limits. There are bloodline altars that can purify, evolve, or mutate bloodlines. There are ancient weapons that choose their own owners. There are battlefields where killing enemies earns divine marks, and those marks can be traded for opportunities that don’t exist anywhere in the Divine Realm."
Several geniuses drew in a soft breath.

Arvantos continued, "There are also trials tied to the five universes. Some test the body. Some test the soul. Some test law comprehension. Some test killing power. Some test will. Some test whether a cultivator can survive betrayal, illusion, despair, and temptation. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t raise gentle flowers. It sharpens blades."
Max’s eyes deepened. That kind of place sounded dangerous. But it was also exactly the kind of place where he could grow the fastest.

Arvantos looked at them solemnly. "Any opportunity you find there will be countless times stronger than anything you’d normally find in the Divine Realm. That’s why there’s never a shortage of geniuses willing to go in. Every race sends its monsters. Every universe sends its future pillars. Some go there to rise. Some go there to kill rivals before they mature. Some go there to seize inheritances that could shift the balance of their race."
Max’s eyes narrowed at that. ’This place probably isn’t simple.’

Arvantos looked at the ten of them and spoke again. "The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t stay open all the time. It follows cycles that none of the five universes fully control. The next opening is coming up soon. If you choose this path, you’ll be sent there."
Orion couldn’t hold back any longer. "And the third path?"
Arvantos turned toward him. "The third path is tied to the Seven Monarchs."
The moment those words left his mouth, the atmosphere in the hall shifted again.
Damian’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Monarchs?"

His reaction wasn’t small. Even someone as cold and composed as Damian couldn’t stay indifferent hearing that title. The others grew more attentive too. Some looked surprised, some looked doubtful, and some seemed like they’d only heard the name in passing without ever really believing it was real.
"Are they actually real?" Damian asked in a low voice. "I thought the Seven Monarchs were just legends, some wild rumor passed around the Divine Realm."
Before Arvantos could answer, Revona smiled faintly. "Oh, they’re very real," she said.
Everyone turned toward her. Revona’s expression stayed calm, but there was a strange depth in her eyes, as if that title had stirred up memories buried far beyond this life.
"In fact," she continued, "I even fought one of the Monarchs in one of my past lives."
The hall fell silent again.
Max looked at Revona for a moment, then turned back to Arvantos with a slight frown. "Monarchs?"
This time, he was genuinely confused. It was the first time he’d heard of them.

Judging by Damian’s reaction, though, they clearly weren’t ordinary figures. If someone like Damian had only ever treated them as legends, then these so-called Monarchs had to be existences hidden so deeply that even top geniuses of the Divine Realm didn’t know the full truth.

The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t raise gentle flowers.
It sharpens blades."
Max’s eyes deepened.
That kind of place sounded dangerous.
But it was also exactly the kind of place where he could grow the fastest.
Arvantos looked at them solemnly.
"Any opportunity you find there will be countless times stronger than anything you’d normally find in the Divine Realm.
That’s why there’s never a shortage of geniuses willing to go in.
Every race sends its monsters.
Every universe sends its future pillars.
Some go there to rise.
Some go there to kill rivals before they mature.
Some go there to seize inheritances that could shift the balance of their race."
Max’s eyes narrowed at that. ’This place probably isn’t simple.’
Arvantos looked at the ten of them and spoke again.
"The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t stay open all the time.
It follows cycles that none of the five universes fully control.
The next opening is coming up soon.
If you choose this path, you’ll be sent there."
Orion couldn’t hold back any longer.
"And the third path?"
Arvantos turned toward him.
"The third path is tied to the Seven Monarchs."
The moment those words left his mouth, the atmosphere in the hall shifted again.
Damian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"Monarchs?"
His reaction wasn’t small.
Even someone as cold and composed as Damian couldn’t stay indifferent hearing that title.
The others grew more attentive too.
Some looked surprised, some looked doubtful, and some seemed like they’d only heard the name in passing without ever really believing it was real.
"Are they actually real?" Damian asked in a low voice.
"I thought the Seven Monarchs were just legends, some wild rumor passed around the Divine Realm."
Before Arvantos could answer, Revona smiled faintly.
"Oh, they’re very real," she said.
Everyone turned toward her.
Revona’s expression stayed calm, but there was a strange depth in her eyes, as if that title had stirred up memories buried far beyond this life.
"In fact," she continued, "I even fought one of the Monarchs in one of my past lives."
The hall fell silent again.
Max looked at Revona for a moment, then turned back to Arvantos with a slight frown.
"Monarchs?"
This time, he was genuinely confused.
It was the first time he’d heard of them.
Judging by Damian’s reaction, though, they clearly weren’t ordinary figures.

If someone like Damian had only ever treated them as legends, then these so-called Monarchs had to be existences hidden so deeply that even top geniuses of the Divine Realm didn’t know the full truth.

chapters.title: Chapter 2018: Seven Monarchs!
paragraphs: Arvantos looked at Max and spoke slowly. "The Monarchs are real beings."
His voice stayed calm, but it carried a seriousness that made everyone listen without interrupting.

"The Seven Monarchs might be the strongest seven beings in our entire universe. They rarely show themselves in the Divine Realm, and even a lot of first-rate forces only know fragmented rumors about them. Some believe they’re ancient cultivators who survived the last universal war. Some believe they’re living embodiments of certain cosmic paths. Some believe they’re existences who failed to step into the True God Realm but still surpassed the limits of ordinary Divine Masters. None of those rumors are entirely right, but none of them are completely wrong either."
Max’s eyes sharpened.
Arvantos continued, "In a way, they’re the protectors of our universe."

Those words changed Max’s expression. Protectors of the universe. That title carried too much weight. The Primordial Race was already the oldest force in the Divine Realm. The four Primarchs stood among the highest beings Max had ever seen.

Yet Arvantos was saying the Seven Monarchs were the universe’s last protectors. That meant their standing didn’t sit below the Primordial Race. If anything, they occupied a place so special that even the Primordials had to acknowledge them.
Max couldn’t help but ask, "Are the Seven Monarchs stronger than Primarchs like you?"
The other geniuses looked toward Arvantos too. This was the question they all wanted answered.

Arvantos smiled lightly, but his answer wasn’t direct. "It’s hard to say who’s stronger between the four Primarchs and the Seven Monarchs." He paused for a moment before continuing. "Our powers are different. Our responsibilities are different. Our battlefields are different. The four Primarchs stand openly at the front of the Primordial Race, and we carry the weight of leading the oldest force in the Divine Realm. We guard the structure of this universe through authority, armies, ancient formations, and the foundation left behind by our ancestors."
His gaze moved past the window, toward the distant sky of the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

"The Seven Monarchs work differently. They don’t rule forces in the ordinary sense. They don’t attend conferences. They don’t fight over territory. They don’t get involved in the disputes of forces, clans, kingdoms, or palaces unless the matter touches the survival of the universe itself. Most of the time, they exist outside the visible order of the Divine Realm."
His voice deepened. "But when the universe reaches its final line of defense, they’re the ones who show up."
The hall went extremely quiet.

Arvantos looked back at them. "That’s why they’re called Monarchs. Not because they sit on thrones ruling over people, but because each of them has mastered a path so completely that ordinary cultivators can’t even imagine the height they’ve reached. One Monarch might suppress a forbidden region alone. Another might guard a wound in the Wall of Eternity. Another might sleep inside a dead star realm, waiting for an ancient seal to break. Another might be watching the movements of the Angel Race, the Dragon Race, or the devils right now."
Max listened with growing interest. He’d already seen plenty of powerful beings, but the way Arvantos talked about the Seven Monarchs made them feel different.
The Primarchs were mighty pillars. The Monarchs sounded like hidden blades buried somewhere in the darkness beyond the known world.
Arvantos continued, "The third path for all of you is to receive tutelage from one of the Seven Monarchs."
The expressions of the ten geniuses shifted again. Even Revona’s smile faded slightly.

Arvantos said, "If the first path is safe cultivation under the Primordial Race, and the second path is the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the third path means being personally guided by one of the beings closest to the peak of our universe. That doesn’t mean all of you would get accepted. The Monarchs don’t teach casually. They don’t care about your background, your reputation, or the rankings you earned in the Cosmic Ascension Conference."
His gaze swept across them. "If a Monarch doesn’t find you suitable, even I can’t force them to take you in."
Orion frowned. "Then how are we even supposed to choose that path?"
"You won’t choose them first," Arvantos replied. "They’ll choose you."
That answer made the hall feel heavier.

Arvantos explained further, "Each Monarch follows a different path. Some specialize in body cultivation. Some specialize in soul. Some specialize in space, fate, sword, battle, life, death, and other terrifying directions. If your foundation resonates with one of them, you might get summoned. If not, you’ll have to choose between the Primordial Race’s protected training and the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."

Max’s heart stirred slightly. Body cultivation. The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins immediately jumped into his mind. Saint Reiner had told him that if any force held records about the higher path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, it would be the Primordial Race.
But now Arvantos had mentioned that among the Seven Monarchs, there might be someone who specialized in body cultivation.
Maybe that wasn’t a coincidence. Maybe Saint Reiner’s clue and Arvantos’s third path pointed toward the same place.

Arvantos seemed to notice the shift in Max’s expression but didn’t comment on it. Instead, he continued, "Still, don’t think this third path is easier than the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Getting taught by a Monarch isn’t the same as being protected by a teacher. Their methods run extreme a lot of the time. Some might throw you into danger worse than anything you’d face in the Divine Realm. Some might test your will until your soul nearly breaks. Some might force you to confront your own path in a way that leaves no room to retreat."

His expression turned stern. "A Monarch won’t waste time comforting you. If they accept you, it means they believe you have a real chance to carry part of the universe’s future. If you fail, they won’t lower the standard just for you."

No one spoke. The three paths now felt far heavier than before. The first path offered safety, resources, and steady growth, but risked dulling their edge. The second path offered terrifying opportunities in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, but also dropped them among monsters from all five universes, where death could show up at any moment.
The third path offered guidance from the universe’s hidden protectors, but acceptance wasn’t guaranteed, and the training might turn out even harsher than stepping onto an ancient battlefield.
Arvantos looked at them calmly. "You all have one day to decide."

His voice spread through the hall. "The next opening of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage is in one week. During that time, the Monarchs will also be told about your existence. If any of them show interest, you’ll know before the pilgrimage begins."
He paused briefly. "Decide how you want your path to unfold."

The ten geniuses stayed silent. Each of them carried different ambitions, different foundations, different fears, and different reasons for wanting strength. But after hearing Arvantos’s words, they all understood one thing clearly.
From this moment on, their choices would no longer affect only themselves.
Arvantos looked at them one last time. Then his figure faded from the hall and vanished without a sound.

The hall grew quiet. Outside the wide window, the Primordial Ancestral Domain remained majestic and ancient, but in Max’s eyes, even that sacred scenery now seemed to carry the weight of an approaching storm.
