chapters.title: Chapter 2019: Talking Among Themselves!
paragraphs: Only the ten geniuses remained inside the hall after Arvantos disappeared.

For a while, no one spoke. The words Arvantos had left behind still hung in the air. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the Seven Monarchs, the Devil Race, the Wall of Eternity, and the coming war all pressed down on them like invisible mountains.

Before this, every one of them had counted as a peak genius of the Divine Realm. Each carried their own pride, their own background, their own ambitions, and their own path to the top. But now the stage had suddenly expanded far beyond the Divine Realm itself.
They were no longer only competing with each other. They’d have to face monsters from all five universes.
Orion was the first to break the silence. He looked around at everyone with a smile, though the excitement in his eyes ran more serious than usual. "So, which path is everyone picking?"
Kaiden answered without much hesitation. "I’m willing to train under one of the Monarchs if I get chosen. Otherwise, I’ll go to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
His tone came out firm. He’d clearly already made up his mind.
Damian nodded from the side. "Same."
He looked toward Ervin. "What about you?"

Ervin shrugged lightly, but his thoughtful expression showed he wasn’t treating this casually. "I don’t know much about the Seven Monarchs, so I can’t say whether I want to be chosen by them or not. But the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage tempts me a lot."
Damian nodded again. He was clearly interested in that place too. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage sounded dangerous, but for geniuses like them, danger and opportunity often meant the same thing.
A place where the strongest young monsters from all five universes gathered was exactly the kind of battlefield that could either kill them or push them far past their current limits.
Revona looked at them calmly and said, "Training under the Seven Monarchs isn’t something we can control."
Everyone turned toward her.

She continued, "The Monarchs are extremely arrogant people. I can tell you that much. They don’t care about reputation, background, bloodline, or how many people sing your praises in the Divine Realm. Their choices are strange, and their standards are even stranger. If even one of us gets chosen by them, that would already count as a huge stroke of luck."
Max looked at her. "You seem to know a lot about them."
Revona nodded slightly. "I know them better than anyone else here."
There was no arrogance in how she said it. She stated it like a plain fact.

"I remember fighting one of the Monarchs in one of my past lives," she said. "I haven’t fully unlocked the memories from that lifetime, but I remember enough to say they’re not ordinary powerful beings. Their strength, their personalities, and even the way they look at the world all sit apart from normal experts."
A faint trace of memory crossed her eyes.
"They’re the kind of people who won’t look twice at you unless something about you catches their interest."
Max thought for a moment, then asked, "Does any of the Seven Monarchs cultivate the body?"
Revona looked at him and shook her head. "Not that I remember."
Max’s gaze shifted slightly.

Revona added, "But I can’t say for sure. My memories from that lifetime are incomplete. There might be a Monarch who walks the body cultivation path, or one who understands it even if it’s not their main focus. I only remember fragments, so I can’t give you a definite answer."
"I understand," Max said with a nod.

His thoughts drifted back to Saint Reiner’s words. The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins. If one of the Seven Monarchs really had knowledge about that path, getting chosen by them would be extremely valuable to him.
But like Revona had said, the Monarchs wouldn’t take on disciples or students just because someone wanted to learn from them. They’d choose based on their own mysterious standards.

Max quietly weighed his options. If one of the Seven Monarchs picked him, he could train under them for a while before heading to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. If none of them showed interest, he’d go straight to the pilgrimage.
Either way, he had no intention of sitting inside the Primordial Race for five hundred years growing under protection. That kind of path might raise his cultivation quickly, but it didn’t suit him.
He’d gotten stronger through danger, battle, inheritance, risk, and the constant pressure of enemies. A protected path would only dull the edge he’d built up.

The group kept discussing their choices for a little longer. Orion clearly leaned toward the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Damian also seemed set on going there if no Monarch picked him. Ervin stayed curious about the unknown opportunities beyond the Wall of Eternity.
Morgana looked entertained by the idea of meeting geniuses from the Devil, Spirit, Angel, and Dragon Universes. Revona stayed calm, but Max could tell she’d already made her decision internally.

After the discussion wound down, the ten geniuses gradually went their separate ways. Some headed back to their assigned rooms. Some went to ask the Primordial attendants questions. Some left to prepare their cultivation, weapons, or mental state for whatever came next.
Max didn’t head back to his room right away. There were still things he needed to sort out.

He walked through the ancient corridors of the Primordial Ancestral Domain, following an aura he’d sensed earlier. Compared to the council domain and the training chambers, this part of the ancestral domain felt quieter.

Golden mist drifted between the pillars, and ancient symbols flowed across the walls like slow-moving streams. The deeper Max walked, the more he felt the Primordial Bloodline inside his body respond to the surroundings.
After a while, he found Sarvion standing beside a stone terrace. The terrace overlooked a vast primordial valley below.

In the distance, law rivers flowed through the sky, and floating mountains drifted silently above the clouds. Sarvion stood with his hands behind his back, his expression calm, as if he’d already known Max would show up.
"You have questions," Sarvion said without turning around.
Max wasn’t surprised. He walked forward and stopped beside him. "I do."
Sarvion glanced at him. "Ask."

chapters.title: Chapter 2020: Slow Awakening of Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline!
paragraphs: Max didn’t waste time. "It’s about my Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline."
Sarvion’s eyes moved slightly, but he stayed silent.

Max continued, "I know it’s supposed to be the highest level of Primordial Bloodline. I can feel it bringing me closer to the laws, strengthening my elemental control, boosting the power of my Pseudo Cosmic Paths, and letting me use the ability I awakened through it. But somehow it still feels weaker than I expected."
He frowned slightly.

"I don’t mean it’s weak. It’s not. But given how powerful the Primordial Race is supposed to be, and given that Tier 4 is the highest bloodline level, I feel like I’m only touching the surface. Other geniuses with lower-tier bloodlines seem to have awakened their abilities more fully, while mine still feels incomplete."
Sarvion listened quietly. Then he smiled faintly.
"That’s because it is incomplete."
Max’s eyes sharpened. "What do you mean?"

Sarvion turned to face him fully. "The others awakened low-tier Primordial Bloodlines. Their bloodlines carry real power, but the potential locked inside them is limited compared to yours. Because of that, the training facility could push their bloodline abilities to fully awaken in a short time."
He paused briefly.
"Your case runs differently."
Max stayed silent, listening carefully.

Sarvion continued, "You carry the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline. That’s the highest level of Primordial Bloodline our race knows of. It stands on the same level as the bloodline the four Primarchs carry. In terms of potential, your bloodline isn’t something that can fully awaken in a few days, a few months, or even a few years."
Max’s expression shifted slightly.
Sarvion looked off into the distance.

"The Primordial Bloodline isn’t just a source of strength. It’s a foundation tied to law, body, soul, origin, and the deeper structure of existence itself. A low-tier bloodline might awaken one or two abilities and settle into a stable state quickly. A higher-tier bloodline holds far more layers. Each layer carries more power, more law resonance, and more transformation."
His voice turned more serious.
"A Tier 4 bloodline sits in a different category. Its potential runs too vast. If its full power woke up inside your body all at once, your body would most likely get destroyed."
Max’s eyes narrowed. "Destroyed?"

Sarvion nodded. "Exploded into nothing, burned from the inside, torn apart by law pressure, or crushed by origin force. The exact result would depend on how the awakening happened, but none of those outcomes would feel good."

Max fell silent. He’d already gone through bloodline combustion during the forced awakening inside the training chamber. Even with his powerful physique, his Dimensional Sovereign Body, his Divine Veins, and all his other foundations, that process had still hurt badly.
If what he’d awakened so far was only a small slice of his Tier 4 bloodline, he could only imagine how terrifying the full awakening would feel.

Sarvion continued, "That’s why your awakening feels slow. It’s not because your bloodline is weak. It’s because it’s too strong to awaken carelessly. As your cultivation realm climbs, as your body grows stronger, as your soul stabilizes, and as your comprehension of the laws deepens, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline will awaken bit by bit."
He looked at Max calmly.

"Each stage will reveal more of its strength. The Primordial Flames are only one manifestation. Your closeness to the laws is another. The boost to your Pseudo Cosmic Paths is another. There will be more changes down the road, but your body has to grow strong enough to handle them first."
Max nodded slowly. Now it made sense. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline wasn’t weaker than he’d expected. He’d just expected it to behave like an ordinary bloodline ability.

The lower-tier bloodlines of the others had awakened faster because they carried less hidden depth. His bloodline stayed asleep in layers because its full potential was too much for his current body to hold.
"That makes sense," Max said.

Sarvion smiled lightly. "Good that you asked. A lot of young geniuses get this wrong. They feel let down when a supreme bloodline doesn’t immediately hand them overwhelming abilities. They don’t realize the strongest bloodlines are often the slowest to fully awaken. The deeper the bloodline, the more careful the awakening has to be."

Max looked thoughtful. That explanation matched his current path too. His body already stood stronger than most cultivators at his realm, but even so, the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline still had to awaken slowly.
That meant he needed to strengthen his body even further if he wanted to draw out its full potential.
That led him to his next question.
"Sarvion," Max said, "does the Primordial Race have any cultivation arts or techniques tied to the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins?"
Sarvion’s expression shifted slightly. This time, he didn’t answer right away. He looked at Max with a bit more seriousness. "You’ve opened the Seven Divine Veins?"
"Five of them," Max replied. "Origin, Vitality, Speed, Strength, and Resilience."
Sarvion’s eyes narrowed faintly. For the first time, Max saw real surprise cross his face.
"The fifth vein," Sarvion said softly. "So Saint Reiner’s inheritance actually reached that level in your hands."

Max nodded. "He told me the Seven Divine Veins are only a foundation for a higher body cultivation path, but he doesn’t know much about what’s beyond them. He said the Primordial Race might have records."
Sarvion stayed quiet for a few breaths. Then he said, "The Primordial Race does hold a complete Seven Divine Veins cultivation art."
Max’s eyes sharpened.

Sarvion continued, "It’s one of the ancient body cultivation methods preserved in our records. Very few people cultivate it, because opening the veins demands an absurd foundation, extreme pain tolerance, rare resources, and a body capable of surviving repeated transformation. Even among Primordials, very few have ever gotten far with it."
He looked at Max again.
"As for a technique beyond the Seven Divine Veins, I’m not sure."
Max frowned slightly.

Sarvion said, "I know there are records mentioning higher body cultivation paths. I also know some ancient Primordial experts believed the Seven Divine Veins weren’t the end. But whether we actually hold a complete technique beyond them, I can’t say. Information at that level would be stored somewhere I don’t usually access casually."
"Where?" Max asked.

chapters.title: Chapter 2021: Codex Library!
paragraphs: "The Codex Library," Sarvion replied.
That name made Max’s eyes shift slightly.

Sarvion continued, "The Codex Library is one of the oldest record halls of the Primordial Race. It holds ancient techniques, lost histories, war records, bloodline studies, cosmic path theories, forbidden cultivation methods, and fragments recovered from ruins older than many of the current forces in the Divine Realm. If there’s information about a body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, it’ll most likely be there."

He paused before adding, "But the Codex Library isn’t a place that just hands you answers. Some records stay sealed. Some require authority. Some respond only to bloodline level. Some only open if your path resonates with them. Since you carry the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, you should get access to a lot of areas, but how much you actually find will come down to you."
Max nodded with understanding. "Then I’ll go there."

Sarvion smiled faintly. "That would be wise. Before you choose between the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage and the Seven Monarchs, you should understand your own foundation as much as you can. Your body, your bloodline, and your path are all unusual. If you find even a small clue about what comes after the Seven Divine Veins, it might change how you prepare for the future."

Max looked toward the distant law rivers flowing across the sky. The path ahead had grown clearer, but also much bigger. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline hadn’t fully awakened. The Seven Divine Veins weren’t the end.
The Codex Library might hold the next clue. And in one week, the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage would open.
Max turned back to Sarvion and gave a slight nod. "Thank you."
Sarvion looked at Max calmly. "Don’t thank me yet."
Max raised his brows slightly.
Sarvion turned away from the stone terrace and started walking toward the inner halls of the Primordial Ancestral Domain. "Let me take you to the Codex Library."
Max followed without hesitation.

The two of them left the terrace behind and moved through a long corridor filled with quiet golden mist. Compared to the paths Max had walked before, this route felt even older. No attendants, no guards, no young Primordials moving around.
The walls on both sides were made of dark bronze stone, and countless ancient symbols were carved into them so deeply they looked less like inscriptions and more like wounds left by time.

As Max walked, he felt the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline inside him responding again. It wasn’t a powerful reaction, but it stayed constant. The bloodline pulsed once every few steps, almost like it recognized the direction they were heading.

The deeper they went, the more Max sensed that this part of the Primordial Ancestral Domain wasn’t built for display. It wasn’t meant to impress outsiders. It was a place where the Primordial Race kept things they didn’t casually show to others.
Sarvion didn’t talk much while leading the way. Max stayed quiet too.

After a while, they arrived at an ancient door that looked far smaller than Max expected. Compared to the enormous gate of the training facility, this door looked almost ordinary. It stood only twice the height of a normal person and was made of dull gray stone.
No golden dragons carved into it, no towering statues, no grand formation circles spreading across the floor. Only a single symbol sat engraved at its center.
It showed the image of an open book, with a rotating star inside it.

Max looked at the symbol for a moment. The longer he stared, the stranger it became. At first it looked like a simple carving. Then he realized the star inside the book was actually moving. Its light stayed faint, but it seemed to hold countless words flowing within it.
Sarvion stopped in front of the door. "This is the entrance to the Codex Library," he said.
Max glanced at the small stone door and frowned slightly. "This is the library?"
Sarvion smiled faintly. "Only the entrance."

He raised his hand and placed his palm against the open-book symbol. The symbol lit up. A soft golden light spread across the dull gray stone, and the door slowly opened without a sound. Beyond it, there was no corridor, no chamber, and no visible library hall.
There was only darkness. Not empty darkness, but a deep, layered darkness filled with countless faint lights, like stars hidden behind mist.
Sarvion stepped forward. Max followed him through the doorway.
The moment he crossed the threshold, the world changed. The corridor disappeared. The stone door disappeared. Even the sense of standing inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain disappeared.

Max found himself inside an enormous pocket dimension. His eyes widened slightly. The Codex Library wasn’t a building. It was a separate space, a vast, silent, impossible space built to preserve the knowledge of the Primordial Race.
There was no floor beneath him in any ordinary sense. Instead, he stood on a wide transparent path made of condensed light.

Beneath that path stretched an endless dark void filled with floating books, jade slips, crystal tablets, ancient scrolls, sealed boxes, stone slabs, research files, law fragments, inheritance orbs, memory crystals, and strange objects Max couldn’t immediately identify.

Above him, the same sight stretched endlessly upward. Everywhere he looked, knowledge floated in the air. Some books drifted slowly with their pages open, glowing words rising from them like mist. Some scrolls sat wrapped in chains of light.

Some jade slips rotated inside small transparent cubes. Some crystal tablets released faint images of ancient battles, body cultivation diagrams, bloodline structures, formation patterns, and cosmic path theories.
Some inheritance orbs gave off such heavy pressure that Max knew they held terrifying techniques or memories left behind by ancient experts.

At first glance, the whole place looked chaotic. It seemed like countless books, records, inheritances, and research files had been tossed into the air by some careless giant and left to drift wherever they landed.

There were shelves, but the shelves didn’t stand on the ground. They floated in layers across the pocket dimension. Some stood vertical. Some lay horizontal. Some turned slowly like wheels. Some spiraled around invisible pillars. Some arranged themselves in rings that rotated around larger inheritance crystals.

chapters.title: Chapter 2022: A Strange Library Indeed!
paragraphs: It looked scattered. It looked disordered. It looked impossible to search.

But after Max stared for a few moments, his eyes slowly narrowed. That wasn’t the case. The Codex Library only looked chaotic on the surface. In truth, everything had its place. Every book, scroll, tablet, crystal, and inheritance object seemed to float according to a hidden order.

Their positions weren’t based on something as simple as size, shape, age, or type. Instead, deeper connections seemed to decide where they sat. Records related to bloodline resonance floated near body cultivation studies.

Ancient war reports drifted close to cosmic path theories. Sealing inheritances gathered around spatial research files. Some law diagrams sat beside battle records, as if the library itself understood which techniques had been born from which wars.
Max felt like he was looking at a living mind made of knowledge. The arrangement was strange, but not random. It only looked messy to someone who couldn’t see the logic behind it.
"This place," Max muttered.
Sarvion glanced at him. "Strange, isn’t it?"
Max nodded. "It looks like everything’s scattered everywhere, but that’s not really true. Every record here feels like it’s exactly where it should be."
Sarvion smiled slightly. "Good observation."
He looked out across the vast pocket dimension, his expression carrying a rare trace of reverence.

"The Codex Library is one of the oldest treasures of the Primordial Race. It doesn’t just store books. It stores knowledge, inheritance, memory, research, history, failures, warnings, and even incomplete ideas left behind by experts who died before finishing their paths."
His voice softened slightly.

"Some of the records here were written by Primarchs. Some were left behind by ancient elders who no longer carry names in the outside world. Some got recovered from ruined star realms after the last war. Some came from forbidden zones. Some are fragments taken from enemies. Some aren’t even written in our language, but the library keeps them anyway because their meaning might turn useful one day."
Max looked around silently. He could feel it. This place was more than a library. It was the memory of the Primordial Race.

Sarvion continued, "The order here isn’t something ordinary people can grasp at first glance. The Codex Library arranges knowledge based on resonance, origin, usage, danger, compatibility, and hidden relationships between different paths. That’s why it looks scattered. A body cultivation record might float beside a bloodline study because the person who created it discovered a certain bloodline could endure a certain body refinement method. A war record might sit near a sealing art because that sealing art got created to counter an enemy from that war. A failed technique might sit beside a successful inheritance because one explains the weakness of the other."

Max’s eyes deepened as he listened. That explained why the library felt so strange. Its structure wasn’t built for convenience. It was built for understanding. A normal library placed records where they were easy to find. The Codex Library placed records where their meanings connected.
Sarvion raised his hand. A small golden light appeared above his palm.

"The Codex Library will respond to your authority, bloodline, and intent. Since you carry the Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline, plenty of areas won’t reject you. That doesn’t mean every record will open for you, though. Some inheritances need specific compatibility. Some need contribution. Some stay sealed because they’re dangerous. Some can’t be read unless your soul can withstand what’s inside them."
Max looked at a distant black scroll wrapped in nine layers of golden chains. Even from far away, he could feel a faint pressure coming off it.

Sarvion followed his gaze and said, "For example, that scroll holds a failed attempt to create an artificial cosmic path from devil corruption and primordial origin. The expert who wrote it died before finishing the theory. Three people tried studying it afterward. Two lost control of their laws, and one ended up half-corrupted before getting sealed. It stays here because even a failed path can teach future generations what not to do."
Max pulled his gaze away. "I understand."
Sarvion nodded. "Good. Curiosity helps here, but carelessness gets dangerous."

He pointed deeper into the pocket dimension. "Records related to the Seven Divine Veins are stored across several layers. The complete Seven Divine Veins cultivation art shouldn’t be hard for you to access with your bloodline authority. But if you’re looking for something beyond the Seven Divine Veins, the library might not show it to you directly."
Max frowned slightly. "Why not?"

"Because the Codex Library responds to intent, but it also responds to readiness," Sarvion replied. "If a record about that path truly exists, it might only appear once your body, bloodline, and comprehension grow strong enough to reach it. You’ve opened five Divine Veins, so you might be close, but close doesn’t always mean enough."

Max looked out into the endless sea of floating knowledge. Books drifted like stars. Scrolls turned like sleeping dragons. Inheritance crystals pulsed in the distance like ancient hearts. Somewhere in this impossible place, there might be a clue to the path beyond the Seven Divine Veins.
His eyes settled into calm focus. "Then I’ll search until I find something."
Sarvion looked at him for a moment. Then he smiled faintly. "That’s the right attitude."

He raised his hand again, and a thin thread of golden light flew out from his palm. The light entered the vast library, passing through floating shelves, spinning scrolls, and rings of ancient tablets.
A few breaths later, several records responded from a distance. They glowed softly before drifting toward Max and Sarvion.
Books. Jade slips. Stone tablets. A crystal file holding anatomical diagrams. A sealed inheritance orb with seven faint lights rotating inside it.
One by one, they stopped in front of Max.

Sarvion said, "Start with these. They’re the records most directly connected to the Seven Divine Veins. Read them carefully. Don’t only look for the final answer. Sometimes the path beyond a technique hides in why the technique got created in the first place."
Max nodded and reached toward the first ancient book. The moment his fingers touched its cover, the five Divine Veins inside his body pulsed at the same time.
Origin. Vitality. Speed. Strength. Resilience.
The book trembled faintly, as if it recognized him.
"This book must hold the original complete Seven Divine Veins," Max muttered as he opened it and started reading.
Even though he already carried the complete version Saint Reiner had created, Max couldn’t help but wonder about the original, full version of the Seven Divine Veins.

Two lost control of their laws, and one ended up half-corrupted before getting sealed.
It stays here because even a failed path can teach future generations what not to do."
Max pulled his gaze away.
"I understand."
Sarvion nodded.
"Good.
Curiosity helps here, but carelessness gets dangerous."
He pointed deeper into the pocket dimension.
"Records related to the Seven Divine Veins are stored across several layers.
The complete Seven Divine Veins cultivation art shouldn’t be hard for you to access with your bloodline authority.
But if you’re looking for something beyond the Seven Divine Veins, the library might not show it to you directly."
Max frowned slightly.
"Why not?"
"Because the Codex Library responds to intent, but it also responds to readiness," Sarvion replied.
"If a record about that path truly exists, it might only appear once your body, bloodline, and comprehension grow strong enough to reach it.
You’ve opened five Divine Veins, so you might be close, but close doesn’t always mean enough."
Max looked out into the endless sea of floating knowledge.
Books drifted like stars.
Scrolls turned like sleeping dragons.
Inheritance crystals pulsed in the distance like ancient hearts.
Somewhere in this impossible place, there might be a clue to the path beyond the Seven Divine Veins.
His eyes settled into calm focus.
"Then I’ll search until I find something."
Sarvion looked at him for a moment.
Then he smiled faintly.
"That’s the right attitude."
He raised his hand again, and a thin thread of golden light flew out from his palm.
The light entered the vast library, passing through floating shelves, spinning scrolls, and rings of ancient tablets.
A few breaths later, several records responded from a distance.
They glowed softly before drifting toward Max and Sarvion.
Books.
Jade slips.
Stone tablets.
A crystal file holding anatomical diagrams.
A sealed inheritance orb with seven faint lights rotating inside it.
One by one, they stopped in front of Max.
Sarvion said, "Start with these.
They’re the records most directly connected to the Seven Divine Veins.
Read them carefully.
Don’t only look for the final answer.
Sometimes the path beyond a technique hides in why the technique got created in the first place."
Max nodded and reached toward the first ancient book.
The moment his fingers touched its cover, the five Divine Veins inside his body pulsed at the same time.
Origin.
Vitality.
Speed.
Strength.
Resilience.
The book trembled faintly, as if it recognized him.
"This book must hold the original complete Seven Divine Veins," Max muttered as he opened it and started reading.
Even though he already carried the complete version Saint Reiner had created, Max couldn’t help but wonder about the original, full version of the Seven Divine Veins.

chapters.title: Chapter 2023: A Reaction!
paragraphs: As Max read through the original complete Seven Divine Veins technique, his expression slowly grew more thoughtful.
The technique was far more complex than the one Saint Reiner had created. At their core, both methods led to the same result. Both aimed to open the Seven Divine Veins inside the body.

Both strengthened the physical foundation through Origin, Vitality, Speed, Strength, Resilience, and the two remaining veins Max had yet to unlock. Both treated the body not as a simple vessel for energy, but as a divine structure that could be refined, expanded, and pushed past ordinary limits.
But the gap between them was enormous.

Saint Reiner’s version came out clean, direct, and terrifyingly practical. It explained the process clearly. It focused on what needed doing, what resources were required, what dangers would come up, and how the body should endure each transformation.

It was the kind of technique built by someone who’d spent centuries studying an incomplete path, cutting away unnecessary confusion, fixing flaws through countless attempts, and rebuilding the method so someone else could actually cultivate it.
The original complete Seven Divine Veins technique read completely differently. It felt like a divine scripture.

Every sentence seemed to carry several layers of meaning. Every diagram held hidden changes. Even the descriptions of the veins weren’t simple instructions, but profound explanations of how the physical body connected to law, origin, soul, vitality, and the deeper structure of existence.
Some parts sounded less like a cultivation method and more like the thoughts of an ancient being who’d already reached a height where ordinary language could no longer properly describe the body.

Max could follow it, but even he had to slow down to read it. If a normal body cultivator tried studying this technique, they’d probably spend years puzzling over a single Chapter and still miss its true meaning.
That didn’t mean Saint Reiner’s version had flaws. Actually, Max felt the opposite.
Saint Reiner’s version stood out precisely because it had taken something impossibly profound and turned it into a method someone could actually cultivate directly.
The original technique had likely come from an existence at the peak of body cultivation, maybe someone so powerful that opening the Seven Divine Veins was just a natural step on their path.
Saint Reiner, on the other hand, had used research, battle experience, ancient fragments, and centuries of study to rebuild the technique from an incomplete inheritance.

One was a scripture written from the height of a god-like expert. The other was a path carved open by a mortal genius who refused to quit. Both held value. Both carried real power. They were simply different.
After a long while, Max closed the ancient book in his hand.
"But there’s still no mention of a body cultivation technique beyond the Seven Divine Veins," he muttered.
His brows furrowed slightly. He’d read the complete technique carefully from start to finish. He hadn’t skipped a single diagram, note, warning, or hidden annotation.
The text confirmed the Seven Divine Veins as an extraordinary body cultivation path, and it went deeper than Saint Reiner’s version in plenty of areas.

But it never clearly said what came after all seven veins opened. There were hints. There were vague phrases. There were lines talking about preparing the body for a higher transformation. But there was no name, no complete method, and no direct answer.
Max placed the book back into the air, and it slowly floated away, drifting back to its strange assigned spot inside the Codex Library.

He started searching more broadly. The Codex Library stretched out beyond imagination. Books, scrolls, jade slips, crystal tablets, stone slabs, research files, inheritance orbs, sealed diagrams, and fragments of ancient records floated through the pocket dimension in countless layers.
Some drifted past him like quiet birds. Some turned slowly in the distance like planets circling invisible suns. Some stayed wrapped in chains of light, refusing to open even as Max approached.

Max moved through the transparent pathways, scanning everything around him. He searched for records tied to body cultivation. He searched for anything related to divine veins, immortal physiques, primordial bodies, origin bones, bloodline vessels, law-forged flesh, and ancient body transformation.
Whenever a book or jade slip responded to his intent, he pulled it over and read through it.

Some records described rare body tempering methods. Some explained how Primordials strengthened their physiques through bloodline resonance. Some were research notes on why certain body cultivation paths collapsed after reaching the Divine King Realm. Some held battle reports about ancient experts whose bodies were strong enough to resist cosmic path attacks.
Valuable knowledge sat everywhere. Yet none of it gave him the answer he wanted.
Hours passed. Max didn’t grow impatient. He understood a place like the Codex Library wouldn’t simply hand him what he wanted just because he asked. Sarvion had already warned him.

Some knowledge here responded to authority. Some responded to bloodline. Some responded to readiness. Some stayed hidden not because no one could find them, but because finding them required the right person at the right moment.

Max kept moving deeper. The scenery around him grew stranger the farther he went. The floating shelves looked older. The light grew dimmer. The books and tablets here weren’t cleanly preserved anymore.

Plenty were damaged, cracked, burned, or incomplete. Some pages floated without covers. Some scrolls were torn in half. Some stone tablets had missing corners. Some jade slips looked so old their surfaces had lost their original color.
This part of the Codex Library felt different. It didn’t feel like a section for complete inheritances. It felt like a graveyard of forgotten knowledge.

Max slowed his pace. His five Divine Veins pulsed faintly inside his body. Origin. Vitality. Speed. Strength. Resilience. The reaction started weak, so faint that Max almost brushed it off. But after a few more steps, the pulse came again, slightly stronger than before.
Max stopped. His eyes narrowed.

The Codex Library stayed silent around him. Books floated through the air in their strange order. Ancient scrolls drifted in slow circles. Faded jade slips turned gently in the darkness. Everything looked scattered, yet everything still carried that hidden arrangement that made this place feel almost alive.
Then Max noticed something. At the far corner of this forgotten layer, near a spot where the light barely reached, a single withered page floated alone.

It looked insignificant. The page was old, yellowed, and torn at the edges. It had no cover, no protective seal, no glowing inscription, and no powerful aura. Next to the inheritance orbs, golden scrolls, and crystal tablets around it, the page looked like a useless remnant that should have turned to dust long ago.
But it kept drifting in place. It didn’t move with the other records. It floated in a small, quiet circle at the very edge of the library space, as if waiting for someone to notice it.
Max’s eyes fixed on it. The five Divine Veins inside his body trembled again. This time, the reaction came through clear.

Max moved toward the withered page. The closer he got, the stronger the response grew. His Origin Vein pulsed deep inside his body. His Vitality Vein stirred with warm life force. His Speed Vein sent a faint current through his limbs. His Strength Vein tightened his muscles slightly. His Resilience Vein turned firm, as if bracing his body for some unknown pressure.
Max reached out. The withered page drifted toward him on its own. The moment his fingers touched it, all five Divine Veins trembled at once.
Max’s expression changed. The reaction wasn’t violent, but it ran deep. It felt like the five veins had recognized something far above them, something they were connected to but hadn’t yet reached.
The sensation wasn’t like finding a technique of the same level. It felt like standing before a gate that had always existed beyond the Seven Divine Veins, hidden behind mist until this exact moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 2024: Eternal Body!
paragraphs: Max slowly lowered his gaze to the page. Very few words remained written on it. Most of the text had faded away, leaving only broken marks and incomplete lines. But at the very top of the withered page, one name stayed clear.
Eternal Body.

The moment Max read those two words, his five Divine Veins shook again. This time, the tremor spread through his entire body. His blood slowed for an instant. His bones seemed to grow heavier. His flesh tightened, and his soul felt like it had just heard an ancient echo from a path buried beyond time.
Even his Dimensional Sovereign Body reacted faintly, not with rejection, but with a strange silence, as if it too were paying attention to the name written on the page.
Eternal Body.

Max stared at those words. Now he was certain. Whatever this page mentioned tied directly into the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins. The complete Seven Divine Veins technique hadn’t given him the answer. Saint Reiner hadn’t known the answer.

Even Sarvion had only told him to search the Codex Library and see what turned up. Yet here, in a forgotten corner of this pocket dimension, a withered page had responded to the five Divine Veins inside him.
That couldn’t be a coincidence.
Max held the page carefully. The old paper felt fragile, but it didn’t crumble. Instead, a faint warmth spread from it into his palm, then flowed toward the five Divine Veins in his body.
His eyes deepened.
"So this is it," Max muttered softly.
The path beyond the Seven Divine Veins. Or at least, the first clue to it.
He looked once more at the name written at the top of the page. Eternal Body. A faint excitement rose in his heart, but he quickly pushed it down. He knew this was only a fragment.

The page didn’t hold a complete technique. Most of its contents were missing, and even the remaining lines were barely readable. But for Max, a name alone was already enough to prove Saint Reiner had been right.
The Seven Divine Veins weren’t the end. They were only the foundation.

Max held the withered page carefully and left the Codex Library. The moment he stepped out of the pocket dimension, the endless sea of floating books, scrolls, jade slips, inheritance orbs, research files, and ancient fragments disappeared behind him.

The strange silence of that impossible library faded, and the familiar aura of the Primordial Ancestral Domain returned. The dull gray stone door closed behind him without a sound, and the symbol of the open book with a rotating star slowly dimmed until it looked like an ordinary carving again.
Sarvion was still waiting outside. He stood quietly in the corridor with his hands behind his back, as though he hadn’t moved at all since Max went in.
The golden mist around him flowed gently, and the ancient symbols on the walls flickered with soft light, but Sarvion’s expression stayed calm and unreadable.
When Max walked out, Sarvion turned his gaze toward him. "How was it?" he asked.

Max didn’t answer right away. He looked down at the withered page in his hand. Compared to the countless grand records inside the Codex Library, this page looked almost pitiful. It was old, fragile, yellowed by time, and torn along the edges.
Most of the writing had faded away, leaving only broken marks and incomplete traces. Yet the name at the top of the page still carried a strange weight Max couldn’t ignore.
Eternal Body.
Those two words had made all five Divine Veins inside him tremble. That alone proved this paper wasn’t ordinary.
After a brief silence, Max held out the page and handed it to Sarvion.
"I found something," he said. "Can you tell me where this paper came from?"

Sarvion took the withered page. At first he only looked at it casually, but the moment his eyes landed on the name at the top, his expression shifted slightly. It wasn’t shock, but a clear trace of seriousness crossed his gaze now.
He didn’t explain right away. Instead, he held the page in the air between them and released a thin stream of primordial energy into it.
"Let me check the records," Sarvion said.

The page floated by itself. A moment later, purple screens appeared around it. They weren’t ordinary formation projections. Each screen was made of condensed information runes, with lines of ancient text moving across them rapidly.
Some showed dates. Some showed names. Some showed storage locations. Some showed records of who had touched, studied, sealed, or transferred the page in the past.
The screens circled the withered paper like a group of searching eyes, scanning its origin from every possible trace left behind.
Max watched silently. The Codex Library was strange enough on its own, but now he realized even a single damaged page inside it carried its own recorded history.

The Primordial Race had preserved not just techniques and inheritances, but also the paths those things had traveled to end up in their possession. Every fragment had a source, every relic had a trail, and every broken record still counted as part of a much larger chain of knowledge.
Several breaths passed. The purple screens kept shifting. Then Sarvion’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"I found it."
Max’s gaze sharpened.
Sarvion looked away from the floating screens and turned to him. "This paper got brought back by a Primordial who entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage for tempering."
Max’s expression shifted. "Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."

He repeated the name softly. For a moment, he looked at the withered page again. He wasn’t disappointed. If anything, this answer only made his resolve firmer. He’d entered the Codex Library searching for clues about the body cultivation path beyond the Seven Divine Veins, and he’d only found a single broken page.

That page didn’t contain a complete technique. It didn’t tell him how to cultivate the Eternal Body. It didn’t explain what came after opening all seven Divine Veins. It only gave him a name and a direction.
But sometimes a direction was enough.

The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. That was where this page had turned up. That meant the clue he needed didn’t sit fully within the Primordial Race, nor did it stay hidden in some ordinary ancient record of the Divine Realm.

It came from that mysterious place beyond the Wall of Eternity, the place where geniuses from all five universes gathered, the place where gods were said to have fallen, the place packed with opportunities, inheritances, dangers, and ancient remnants beyond anything found in the Divine Realm.

Max slowly closed his fingers around the page again after Sarvion handed it back. His eyes deepened. He’d already planned to enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage before this. Even without this clue, that place gave him the best path to grow stronger quickly.
The Divine Realm wasn’t enough for him anymore. Training safely under the Primordial Race didn’t suit him. If no Monarch chose him, the pilgrimage would naturally become his next stop.

But now his reason for going ran deeper. He wasn’t just entering to compete with the geniuses of the five universes anymore. He wasn’t just entering to grab opportunities and prepare for the coming war. He was going to search for the Eternal Body. He was going to search for the path beyond the Seven Divine Veins.

chapters.title: Chapter 2025: Back to Four Sacred Clans!
paragraphs: Sarvion watched him quietly and seemed to catch what he was thinking.

"The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage isn’t a place where answers come easy," Sarvion said. "If this page came from there, the complete inheritance might be hidden in some dangerous region, sealed inside an ancient ruin, held by another race, or scattered across different trials. It’s also possible only this fragment survives."
Max looked at him. "But it’s still a clue."
Sarvion nodded. "Yes. And for someone walking a lost path, a clue is sometimes worth more than a complete technique that doesn’t even belong to them."

Max stared at the withered page for a long moment. The five Divine Veins inside his body sat quiet now, but he could still remember how they’d trembled when he first read the name Eternal Body. That reaction couldn’t be false.
After a while, Max carefully folded the page and stored it away. His decision was clear now. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was no longer just one of his options. It was the place he had to go.
"Sarvion," Max said calmly, "I’ve decided."
Sarvion looked at him.
Max’s eyes stayed steady. "I’m going to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
Sarvion didn’t look surprised. Instead, he gave a faint smile. "I figured you would."
After talking with Sarvion a little longer, Max parted ways with him and headed straight back to the room assigned to him inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
For now, nothing urgent remained for him to do. Arvantos had already laid out the three possible paths. Sarvion had explained the truth behind his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline.

The Codex Library had handed him a clue about the Eternal Body, and that clue pointed straight to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Unless one of the Seven Monarchs chose him, Max’s next destination was already set.
He only had to wait. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage would open in roughly six days. For most people, six days wasn’t much. For Max, six days gave him more than enough time to make real progress.

The moment he entered his room, Max activated the isolation formation and stepped into the Dimension of Time. The quiet space of his personal dimension unfolded around him, and the shift in time flow immediately gave him what the outside world couldn’t.

He didn’t waste a single moment. He started training with his Pseudo Cosmic Paths, refining his control over the Emotion Severing Path, Divine King Punishment, the Devouring Flames Domain, the Primordial Flame Path, the Ice Path, and the Light Path.

Time flowed differently inside the dimension. Max moved from one path to another with complete focus. He practiced the Ten Void Sealing Art until the ten void rings responded with even greater precision.

He compressed Primordial Flames in one ring and black flames in another, then compared how both powers behaved under the pressure of void sealing. He used Dragonheart to test how the Emotion Severing Path flowed through his sword strikes.
He refined his use of Divine King Punishment, making sure the seven-colored lightning didn’t just explode outward with brute force, but came down with judgment and purpose.
Three days passed like that.
On the fourth day, Arvantos summoned all ten geniuses again. They gathered in the same quiet hall inside the Primordial Ancestral Domain.

This time, the atmosphere felt different from before. Everyone already knew the Seven Monarchs would make their decision before the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage opened, and even though most of them stayed quiet, their eyes showed real anticipation.
Arvantos stood at the front of the hall with a solemn expression.
"The Seven Monarchs have made their decision," he said.
The ten geniuses immediately went serious.
Arvantos looked at each of them before continuing, "They’ve chosen three among you."
The hall went silent.
"Orion. Kaiden. Morgana."
Those three names changed the expressions of everyone else.
Orion blinked, then pointed at himself. "Me?"
Kaiden’s expression stayed steady, but his eyes clearly moved. Morgana raised her brows slightly, then smiled with interest, like she’d just heard something amusing and dangerous at the same time.
The others looked surprised too.

Max glanced toward the three of them thoughtfully. He hadn’t expected the Monarchs to pick Orion, Kaiden, and Morgana out of everyone here, but after thinking back on what Revona had said, it didn’t seem too strange.
The Seven Monarchs didn’t choose by normal standards. Their eyes worked differently from ordinary experts, and what caught their interest might not be obvious to anyone else.
Revona smiled faintly from the side. "Told you their choices were strange."
Orion recovered quickly and grinned. "Strange or not, I’ll take it."
Damian folded his arms and looked at him. "Try not to die under your Monarch’s training."
Orion’s grin stiffened slightly. "That was unnecessary."
Morgana chuckled softly. "No, I think that was very necessary."
Kaiden stayed calm, but his gaze had turned resolute. Whichever Monarch had chosen him, this was an opportunity countless geniuses in the Divine Realm would never get. He wasn’t going to waste it.
Soon, a Primordial expert entered the hall to take the three away. Before leaving, Orion looked back at Max and the others with a wide smile. "Don’t fall too far behind while I’m gone."
Damian snorted. "Worry about yourself."

Morgana gave everyone a casual wave, while Kaiden nodded once before following the Primordial expert out of the hall. A spatial passage opened in front of them, and the three chosen geniuses disappeared into it.
Only seven remained. Arvantos turned toward Max, Damian, Ervin, Revona, Rosaline, Rakan, Aurelian, and the others who hadn’t been chosen.
"As for the rest of you," he said solemnly, "I take it you’re planning to enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."

The seven geniuses nodded. None of them hesitated. The first path, staying with the Primordial Race and cultivating safely, didn’t suit them. The Monarch path was no longer in their hands. That left the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the dangerous battlefield where the strongest young geniuses of all five universes would gather.
Arvantos looked at their faces and spoke in a heavier voice. "In that case, you have one day to visit your loved ones and settle your personal matters."
The hall grew quieter.

"There’s no telling what you’ll run into in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. You might encounter geniuses from the Devil Race, Angel Race, Dragon Race, and Spirit Race. You might enter ruins that have killed people far stronger than you. You might find opportunities that change your whole future, but you might also run into dangers that don’t give you a second chance."
His gaze swept across them. "The chance of death is very high."
No one looked away.

Arvantos continued, "Use this one day well. Meet the people you want to meet. Say what you need to say. Prepare your weapons, steady your minds, and make sure you walk into that place without regret."
The seven geniuses nodded solemnly.
After saying this, Arvantos dismissed them and vanished from the hall.

Max and the others talked for a short while afterward. Nobody said much. The mood had turned heavier. Everyone had families, teachers, friends, clans, or people they wanted to see before heading off to a place where even their own survival wasn’t guaranteed.
One by one, they went their separate ways.

Max also left the Primordial Ancestral Domain and headed back to the Five Sacred Clan domain. This time, his arrival looked completely different. No one threatened him. No one blocked his path. No elder questioned his identity or tried to push him around with authority.

Instead, the guards and descendants of the Four Sacred Clans treated him with obvious restraint and respect. Some even lowered their heads as he passed. Their expressions stayed complicated, but none of them dared show open hostility.

chapters.title: Chapter 2026: Freya’s Concern!
paragraphs: Max almost laughed. ’They flip their attitude pretty easily.’
Of course, he understood why. The truth about the Voidwalker Clan had already come out, and the devil crisis had pulled the whole Divine Realm’s attention elsewhere.

More importantly, Max’s strength and standing had shifted in everyone’s eyes. He’d awakened the Voidwalker inheritance, gotten a Primordial Bloodline, killed a devil at the 5th level of the Law Manifestation Realm in front of every major force, and survived a sneak attack from the Pearl of Abyss.
At this point, treating him like some ordinary outsider would just be foolish.
Max ignored the stares around him and headed straight for the Voidwalker Clan’s area. There he found Freya.
The moment he told her about his plans, her expression shifted several times.

"Godslayer’s Pilgrimage," Freya said softly. Her face turned serious, but after a while, she nodded. "That place actually suits you right now. There are plenty of opportunities there, and if you can survive them, your strength will grow way faster than it would inside the Divine Realm."

Max looked at her, a little surprised. The way Freya talked sounded too familiar. It didn’t sound like she’d just heard rumors about the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. It sounded like she knew the place from personal experience.
"Have you been to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage?" Max asked.
Freya nodded. "Yes."
Max’s eyes moved.
Freya smiled faintly. "What do you think I’ve been doing since I ascended to the Divine Realm all these years?"
She walked to the window and looked out at the distant Voidwalker grounds.
"The moment I entered the Divine Realm and got my original strength back to its peak, I entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. That’s actually one of the reasons I couldn’t come find you sooner."
Her voice carried a trace of regret, but it quickly turned serious again.

"And I’ll tell you this, Max, that place is insane. Geniuses from all five first races fight there over resources, inheritances, trials, ancient marks, and opportunities you won’t find anywhere else. The Devil Race, Spirit Race, Angel Race, Dragon Race, and our own universe all send their monsters there. Some of them are arrogant beyond belief. Some are terrifyingly strong. Some look harmless until they kill people without warning. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage really opened my eyes to how wide the world beyond our universe actually is."
Max listened quietly.
Freya turned back to him and smiled lightly. Then she stepped closer and patted his head.
"But I know you’ll do just fine there."
Max immediately pulled her hand off his head. "I’m not a kid anymore, Big Sis."
"Is that so?" Freya asked with a mischievous smile.
Max narrowed his eyes slightly. "What’s with that look?"
Freya’s smile widened. "Where are Alice and Lenavira?"
Max froze for a moment.

Freya looked at him with the expression of someone who already knew everything. "I know you’ve been keeping them with you, but you should let them out now. You don’t know what you’ll run into in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. That place is way too dangerous, and dragging them along would only put them at unnecessary risk. The safest place for them right now is right here, inside the Voidwalker Clan."
Max didn’t answer right away.
Freya’s expression softened a little. "Back in Acaris, I treated Alice badly. I know that. I want to make it up to her properly."

Then she added with a faint smile, "And I want to get to know Lenavira better too. After all, these two girls are going to be my brother’s future wives. As your elder sister, I should at least understand them, right?"
Max’s face turned slightly red. "Big Sis."

Freya ignored his embarrassment and kept going. "With me here, I can guide them. The Voidwalker Clan has resources, inheritances, training grounds, and protection they can’t find anywhere else. By the time you get back, they should be able to reach at least the Law Manifestation Realm, maybe even higher if their progress goes well."

Max grew thoughtful. Freya’s teasing annoyed him, but the first part of what she said made sense. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage wasn’t a normal training ground. It was a place where the most dangerous geniuses of five universes gathered.
Alice and Lenavira were talented, but bringing them there right now wouldn’t help them. It would only expose them to dangers far beyond their current level.
Leaving them inside the Voidwalker Clan was the best choice.
After a moment, Max waved his hand. Space rippled beside him. Alice and Lenavira appeared out of nowhere.
Alice blinked in confusion and looked around. "Max?"
Her eyes moved across the unfamiliar surroundings. "Where is this place?"
Lenavira also looked around with wonder. The aura here felt far stronger than what she was used to, and even the space itself felt different. "Is this the Four Sacred Clans you told us about?"

Before Max could answer, Alice’s gaze landed on Freya. Her expression darkened immediately. She hadn’t forgotten what Freya had done to her back in Acaris. Even with the situation changed, even knowing Freya was Max’s sister, that memory wasn’t something she could just erase.
Freya noticed Alice’s expression and didn’t look away. For once, her smile turned gentler and quieter.
Max spoke before the atmosphere could get too stiff. "Alice, Lenavira, this is indeed the Four Sacred Clans. More specifically, we’re inside the Voidwalker Clan."
Both women turned toward him.
Max then explained everything briefly. He told them about the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the danger of that place, the geniuses from all five universes, and why he couldn’t bring them along this time.
He didn’t downplay how serious this was. Alice and Lenavira needed to understand this wasn’t some ordinary journey or a short training trip.
"This place will be safer for both of you," Max said. "Big Sis will help guide you, and the Voidwalker Clan has enough resources to support your cultivation."
Alice frowned. "You’re leaving us here because it’s that dangerous?"
Max nodded. "Yes."
Lenavira’s expression turned worried. "Then what about you?"
Max smiled faintly. "I’ll be fine."
Neither of them looked convinced.
Max added, "But don’t worry about the others inside the Dimension of Genesis."

He walked toward a section of the wall and placed his palm against it. A faint silver light spread from his hand. Using Dimensional Anchor, Max created an anchor point connecting directly to the Dimension of Genesis.

The wall trembled slightly, and a circular portal slowly formed on its surface. The portal shimmered with layered spatial light, and beyond it, a faint trace of the Dimension of Genesis could be felt.
Alice and Lenavira looked at the portal in surprise.

"This portal connects to the Dimension of Genesis," Max explained. "You can go in and out through it. I’ve separated the Dimension of Genesis from myself and fixed it to this anchor for now, so even if something happens to me out there, the people inside won’t be affected."
The moment he said that, the worry in Alice and Lenavira’s eyes deepened. They might not fully grasp the scale of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, but they understood Max.

He’d never done something like this before. He’d never separated one of his dimensions from himself as a precaution. He’d never spoken like there was a real chance something might happen to him. The fact that he’d made these preparations told them more than his words ever could.
This journey was dangerous. Far more dangerous than anything he’d faced before.
Alice looked at him quietly. Lenavira lowered her gaze slightly. The room grew tense.
Seeing the heavy mood, Freya let out a small sigh and stepped toward the door.
"You three should talk," she said. "I’ll wait outside."
With that, she left the room and closed the door behind her, giving Max, Alice, and Lenavira the space they needed.

chapters.title: Chapter 2027: To Alice and Lenavira!
paragraphs: No sooner had Freya left the room than Alice turned toward Max.
Her eyes were full of worry.
"Do you really have to go if it’s this dangerous?"

A heavy silence filled the room. The question sounded simple, but it carried a lot of weight. Alice wasn’t asking because she didn’t understand his ambition. She was asking because she understood him too well. Max had always walked toward danger whenever danger promised strength, and even though that strength had protected them plenty of times, it had also put him on a path where every step seemed sharper than the one before.
Lenavira stood beside Alice without a word, but her expression carried the same fear.
Max looked at both of them. For a moment, he didn’t answer. Then he took a deep breath and nodded lightly. "I have to."
Alice’s fingers tightened slightly.

Max continued in a quiet voice, "The situation’s already changed. The devils have gotten into our universe, the Wall of Eternity’s been pierced, and nobody knows how long this current peace will hold. If I stay here and cultivate normally, I might get strong someday, but that day might come too late."
He looked at Alice first, then at Lenavira.
"I need strength. Not just for myself, but for both of you, for Big Sis, for the people inside the Dimension of Genesis, and for everything I want to protect."
His voice dropped lower.

"And you both know about my parents. My mother and father are still trapped. I haven’t forgotten what happened to them. I haven’t forgotten who destroyed my childhood. If I want to rescue them, if I want revenge, if I want to stand in front of the people who took everything from me and make them answer for it, then I can’t afford to grow slowly."

Alice bit her lower lip. She wanted to tell him not to go. She wanted to tell him that revenge, strength, destiny, even the fate of the universe, didn’t matter more than his own life. But looking into his eyes, she knew those words wouldn’t stop him. Max wasn’t leaving because he wanted to abandon them. He was leaving because he believed this was the only way he could one day come back without fear.

Lenavira finally spoke. "You always risk your life for strength," she said quietly. "More strength, greater strength, then even more strength after that. When are you going to stop doing this and just live normally? When are you going to start caring about yourself? When are you going to look after yourself the way you look after everyone else?"

Max’s heart tightened slightly. He didn’t know how to answer right away, because Lenavira wasn’t wrong. He’d thrown himself into danger again and again. He’d challenged enemies stronger than himself, accepted trials that could’ve killed him, hidden pain beneath calm smiles, and kept moving forward even as every new step brought a stronger enemy. He understood their fear. He understood why they were tired of watching him leave for places where death waited.

But he couldn’t stop. Not yet. Not while his parents stayed imprisoned. Not while the devils threatened the universe. Not while people like Varok looked at their home as a place to invade, corrupt, and control. Not while Max still lacked the power to fully decide his own fate.

He stepped closer and pulled both Alice and Lenavira into his arms. They didn’t resist. Alice leaned against his chest, her hands gripping his clothes tightly. Lenavira closed her eyes for a moment and rested her forehead against his shoulder. For a while, none of them spoke. The silence between them wasn’t empty anymore. It was filled with fear, affection, helplessness, and a warmth none of them wanted to let go of.
"I promise you both," Max said softly. "It won’t be long before I leave all this fighting behind and live peacefully with you. That’s what I’m working so hard for."
His arms tightened around them.

"I don’t want endless war. I don’t want to spend my life chasing enemies from one battlefield to the next. I want to reunite with my family. I want to protect the people beside me. I want a life where I don’t have to worry about someone taking everything away from me again."
Alice’s eyes turned slightly red. "Then come back," she whispered. "Don’t just promise us a future and disappear before we get there."
Max lowered his gaze to her. "I’ll come back."
Lenavira looked at him with trembling eyes. "You always say that so calmly."
Max smiled faintly, but his voice stayed serious. "Because I mean it."

The room went quiet again. This time, the silence felt softer. Alice slowly raised her hand and touched his face, as if trying to memorize him before he left. Lenavira moved closer too, her earlier worry slowly giving way to something warmer and more tender. Max looked at the two women in his arms, and for the first time that day, thoughts of the devils, the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the Eternal Body, and the coming war faded from his mind.
For this moment, there was only them. Alice. Lenavira. The people he wanted to come back to. The people who made all his desperate effort feel like it meant something.

Max gently lowered his head and kissed Alice first. She didn’t pull away. Then Lenavira moved closer, and Max turned to her too, holding both of them with a care that slowly softened the fear in their hearts. What started as comfort soon turned into something deeper. Their words faded, their hesitation disappeared, and the emotions they’d been holding back for too long finally found a way to speak without needing to be explained.
That night, Max stayed with both Alice and Lenavira, and their closeness deepened into something more intimate.

It wasn’t driven by impulse alone. It was a quiet, intimate promise between three people who understood the road ahead might separate them for a long time. Beneath the gentle glow of the room’s formations, they gave each other warmth, trust, and a closeness that made the coming danger feel a little less cruel.

For that one night, Max didn’t train. He didn’t think about the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. He didn’t think about Varok, the Devil Race, the Seven Monarchs, or the path beyond the Seven Divine Veins. He stayed with Alice and Lenavira until the weight in their hearts slowly eased, until their fear didn’t feel so sharp anymore, and until the coming separation became something they could face together.

Outside the room, the Voidwalker Clan stayed quiet beneath the ancient sky of the Five Sacred Clan domain. Inside, Max held the two women close, letting the silence settle around them like a fragile peace.
For one night, before stepping into a battlefield where even geniuses from five universes could die, he let himself remember what he was fighting for.
When the night deepened, the room finally settled into a peaceful silence.

chapters.title: Chapter 2028: Michael!
paragraphs: The next day, after spending some time with Freya, Max finally got ready to leave the Four Sacred Clans.

Freya didn’t try to stop him. She knew better than anyone that Max had already made his decision. Instead of trying to talk him out of it, she warned him about several things he needed to keep in mind inside the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.

She told him not to trust anyone too easily, not to underestimate geniuses from the other four universes, not to assume every trial followed fair rules, and not to reveal all his abilities unless he had no other choice.

She also reminded him that in a place like the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, opportunities often came with hidden prices, and sometimes the most beautiful inheritance grounds were the ones that swallowed the most corpses.

Max listened quietly. He didn’t treat her warnings as unnecessary worry. Freya had already been to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, and if even she called that place insane, Max had no reason to take it lightly.
After saying goodbye, Max left the Four Sacred Clans and headed back to the Primordial Ancestral Domain. When he arrived, he found the other top geniuses already gathered.

Damian, Ervin, Revona, Rosaline, Rakan, Aurelian, and the others were there, but they weren’t alone. Besides the seven who’d decided to enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, there were also ten young geniuses from the Four Sacred Clans.
Max spotted the strongest descendants of Valerius, Ashbourne, Ravenhart, and Evercrest among them, and their expressions turned complicated the moment they noticed him.
They no longer looked at him with the same hostility as before. Some looked wary. Some looked curious. Some clearly still disliked him, but none of them dared provoke him openly.

Besides the Four Sacred Clan geniuses, unfamiliar faces stood scattered through the gathering area too. Some looked calm and detached. Some carried strange auras that didn’t belong to ordinary disciples. Some had eyes too old for their young faces, and some stood silently, as if the whole world around them had nothing to do with them.
The number of young geniuses present had crossed thirty. Max hadn’t expected this many people. But apart from the Four Sacred Clan geniuses, the unfamiliar youths all shared one thing in common.

They were all Primordials. Their bloodline aura felt different from the ten geniuses who’d recently awakened Primordial Bloodline. It ran deeper in some spots, more stable in others, clearly belonging to people who’d been raised with Primordial inheritance from birth. That realization made Max wonder if all of them would be entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage together.
"Max, you finally made it."
Sarvion’s voice came from nearby. Max turned and saw Sarvion walking toward him with his usual calm expression.
"Who are the other geniuses besides the ones from the Four Sacred Clans?" Max asked as they started walking together.
Sarvion glanced at the unfamiliar youths and smiled faintly. "They’re disciples of some great hidden experts."
"Hidden experts?" Max raised his brows slightly.

Sarvion nodded. "Not every powerful being in the Divine Realm belongs openly to a palace, clan, court, kingdom, sanctum, hall, or Primordial faction. Some ancient experts prefer to stay outside the public order. They don’t interfere much, but when something as big as the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage opens up, they naturally send their disciples."

Max looked at the unfamiliar geniuses again. That explained their strange auras. They weren’t ordinary disciples from famous forces. They were heirs trained by old monsters living outside the usual structure of the Divine Realm.

Max didn’t dwell on it too much. Soon he met up with Damian, Rakan, Revona, and the others. Damian gave him a brief nod. Rakan looked more serious than usual, while Revona’s gaze lingered on Max for a moment, as if she could tell something about him had shifted again. Max had no plans to explain anything, so he just greeted them calmly.
Just as he was talking with them, a young voice sounded from behind him.
"You must be Max."

Max turned around. A young man with dark blue hair and a sharp, handsome face stood in front of him. His eyes carried pride, and his aura wasn’t weak. A faint pressure surrounded him, marking him as no ordinary genius, but the arrogance on his face stood out even more than his strength.
"And you are?" Max asked.
The young man lifted his chin slightly. "I’m Michael."
"Good to meet you, Michael," Max said, holding out his hand politely.
But to his surprise, Michael slapped it away. The sound wasn’t loud, but it instantly drew the attention of Damian, Rakan, Revona, and several nearby geniuses.
Max looked at his hand for a brief moment. Then he looked back at Michael.
Michael’s expression stayed sharp. "I’m not here to make friends with you."
Max stayed silent.

Michael continued, "I came here to tell you that you don’t deserve the title of the strongest young genius of our universe. Someone stuck at the Law Manifestation Realm doesn’t deserve a title like that."
The atmosphere around them turned strange.
Damian frowned. Rakan’s expression darkened. Revona looked at Michael with mild interest, like she was trying to figure out if he was brave or just foolish.
Max sighed inwardly. ’Trouble really does find me wherever I go.’
He looked at Michael, then shrugged. "You’re right, buddy."
After saying that, he turned away like the whole thing no longer interested him.

Michael froze. The reaction ran completely opposite of what he’d expected. He’d figured Max would get angry, argue back, release his aura, or challenge him. Instead, Max had just agreed and ignored him.
"A-are you ignoring me?" Michael shouted.
Max turned his head slightly and looked at him from the side. "Did you not hear me? I said you’re right."
Michael stood there, not knowing what to say. His challenge had landed on absolutely nothing.
Before the awkward silence could stretch any further, an old man appeared before them.
"My apologies, young man."
The voice sounded calm and aged, but the moment it came out, the whole area seemed to grow heavier.

Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. The old man had a large rectangular face, a thick white beard covering most of his lower face, and a pair of bright eyes that looked surprisingly lively for his age. He wore golden armor that looked like a formal suit prepared for war, and every part of him gave off an aura that felt both dignified and dangerous.
The moment Max saw him, he understood this old man wasn’t simple. His aura matched the four Primarchs, the leaders of the strongest first-rate forces, and the ancestors of the Four Sacred Clans.

What surprised Max even more was that the old man was human. Not a Primordial. Not from the Four Sacred Clans. Just a normal human who’d somehow reached a level where his presence could stand beside the peak figures of the Divine Realm.
