chapters.title: Chapter 2029: Sovereign Warlock!
paragraphs: Just then, Arvantos appeared too.

"Max, and all you young ones," Arvantos said, looking at Max and the other six geniuses before turning toward the bearded old man. "Let me introduce him to you. This is Sovereign Warlock. I believe you’ve all heard of him."
Sovereign Warlock. The moment that title reached their ears, the expressions of Max and the others changed.

The title of Sovereign wasn’t something anyone could just claim. In the Divine Realm, only experts who’d reached the Divine God Realm were qualified to carry it. Those beings stood at a height most cultivators couldn’t even imagine, and each one represented the absolute peak of a path.
Max was already connected to one such figure. Dragonheart, the sword in his possession, had come from the Sword Sovereign. And now another Sovereign stood right in front of him.
Sovereign Warlock looked at their reactions and laughed lightly. "Don’t look so shocked, kids. I’m just an old man."
Then his gaze shifted to Max. "I apologize for my disciple’s behavior," he said. "Michael’s a bit too arrogant for his own good."

Michael’s face changed immediately. "Master!" He looked both embarrassed and unwilling to accept it. After all, he’d just declared Max unworthy of the title of strongest genius, and now his own master was apologizing to Max in front of everyone.
Sovereign Warlock turned toward him and knocked him on the head with his fist.
"What, kid?" the old man said. "Have you not gotten more and more arrogant lately? How many times have I told you not to be arrogant, to stay humble, and to never underestimate anyone?"
Michael lowered his head and answered with a serious face. "I understand, Master."
Sovereign Warlock sighed and shook his head. "You always say you understand, but look at how many problems you keep causing me."
Michael didn’t dare say anything else.

Max watched the whole exchange quietly. The old man’s tone sounded casual, but Max could tell Sovereign Warlock had complete control over the situation. He’d shown up at exactly the right moment, apologized before the conflict could escalate, and scolded his disciple without stripping Michael of all his dignity. That kind of effortless control only came from someone with real strength and experience.
Arvantos smiled faintly. "Michael will also be entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."

Max glanced at Michael. Michael looked back at him with a complicated expression. The hostility hadn’t disappeared, but after getting scolded by his master in front of everyone, he no longer dared act too recklessly.
Sovereign Warlock looked at Max with interest. "I heard what happened during the meeting with the devils."
Max stayed calm. "News travels fast."

"At our level, important news travels before people even finish cleaning up the battlefield," Sovereign Warlock said with a light laugh. "A 1st level Law Manifestation Realm cultivator killed a 5th level Law Manifestation Realm devil in one move, survived the Pearl of Abyss, and then still had the nerve to provoke Varok. How could I not be curious?"

Several nearby geniuses looked toward Max again. Michael’s expression stiffened slightly. Clearly, he’d heard the title of strongest genius, but he hadn’t fully understood what Max had done to earn it.
Sovereign Warlock glanced at Michael from the corner of his eye. "This is exactly why I told you not to judge people by realm alone."
Michael clenched his fists but didn’t argue back.
Max smiled lightly. "It wasn’t as impressive as the rumors make it sound."
Sovereign Warlock laughed again. "Modesty suits you better than arrogance, but fake modesty gets annoying too. You killed him because you were strong enough. That much’s clear."

Arvantos looked toward the gathered geniuses and spoke, pulling everyone’s attention back to the main matter. "You’ve all gathered here because the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage will open soon. Some of you come from the Primordial Race. Some come from the Four Sacred Clans. Some are disciples of hidden experts. Some are among the ten who recently awakened Primordial Bloodline."
His voice turned solemn.

"But once you enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, none of those identities will protect you. The geniuses of the Devil Universe, Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe won’t care about your background unless it gives them a reason to kill you faster."
The atmosphere turned serious again.

Arvantos continued, "Once the gate opens, each of you walks your own path. Whether you find opportunity or death will come down to your strength, judgment, and luck. I won’t repeat this again. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage isn’t some protected trial arranged by your elders. It’s not a competition where someone steps in when you’re about to die. It’s a battlefield, a graveyard, a treasury, and a road left behind by existences far older than the current order of the five universes. Anyone who enters must accept that everything they own can be taken from them."

No one said a word. Even the arrogant young geniuses who’d come from hidden experts and ancient clans went quieter under those words. They were proud, but they weren’t foolish. If Arvantos was speaking this seriously, the danger of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage had to go far beyond ordinary imagination.

Arvantos raised his gaze toward the distant sky of the Primordial Ancestral Domain. "The entrance to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t sit in any ordinary region of the Divine Realm. It lies at a forbidden point in space, far beyond the controlled star regions of most forces. Even Divine King Realm cultivators aren’t allowed to approach that place without permission, and ordinary Divine Lord Realm cultivators would die before they ever reached the outer boundary."
Several expressions changed. A forbidden point in space. Those words alone were enough to make the gathered geniuses understand that the journey itself wouldn’t be simple.

Arvantos continued, "That place sits too close to the Wall of Eternity. The laws there run unstable, space stretches thin, time doesn’t always flow evenly, and the boundary pressure can crush weaker bodies into dust. There are no cities nearby. No forces, no clans, no trade routes, and no safe domains. It’s a place that exists outside the normal map of our universe."
His gaze returned to them. "It’ll take us one day to get there."

The moment that title reached their ears, the expressions of Max and the others changed.
The title of Sovereign wasn’t something anyone could just claim.
In the Divine Realm, only experts who’d reached the Divine God Realm were qualified to carry it.
Those beings stood at a height most cultivators couldn’t even imagine, and each one represented the absolute peak of a path.
Max was already connected to one such figure.
Dragonheart, the sword in his possession, had come from the Sword Sovereign.
And now another Sovereign stood right in front of him.
Sovereign Warlock looked at their reactions and laughed lightly.
"Don’t look so shocked, kids.
I’m just an old man."
Then his gaze shifted to Max.
"I apologize for my disciple’s behavior," he said.
"Michael’s a bit too arrogant for his own good."
Michael’s face changed immediately.
"Master!" He looked both embarrassed and unwilling to accept it.
After all, he’d just declared Max unworthy of the title of strongest genius, and now his own master was apologizing to Max in front of everyone.
Sovereign Warlock turned toward him and knocked him on the head with his fist.
"What, kid?" the old man said.
"Have you not gotten more and more arrogant lately?
How many times have I told you not to be arrogant, to stay humble, and to never underestimate anyone?"
Michael lowered his head and answered with a serious face.
"I understand, Master."
Sovereign Warlock sighed and shook his head.
"You always say you understand, but look at how many problems you keep causing me."
Michael didn’t dare say anything else.
Max watched the whole exchange quietly.
The old man’s tone sounded casual, but Max could tell Sovereign Warlock had complete control over the situation.
He’d shown up at exactly the right moment, apologized before the conflict could escalate, and scolded his disciple without stripping Michael of all his dignity.
That kind of effortless control only came from someone with real strength and experience.
Arvantos smiled faintly.
"Michael will also be entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
Max glanced at Michael.
Michael looked back at him with a complicated expression.
The hostility hadn’t disappeared, but after getting scolded by his master in front of everyone, he no longer dared act too recklessly.
Sovereign Warlock looked at Max with interest.
"I heard what happened during the meeting with the devils."
Max stayed calm.
"News travels fast."
"At our level, important news travels before people even finish cleaning up the battlefield," Sovereign Warlock said with a light laugh.
"A 1st level Law Manifestation Realm cultivator killed a 5th level Law Manifestation Realm devil in one move, survived the Pearl of Abyss, and then still had the nerve to provoke Varok.
How could I not be curious?"
Several nearby geniuses looked toward Max again.
Michael’s expression stiffened slightly.
Clearly, he’d heard the title of strongest genius, but he hadn’t fully understood what Max had done to earn it.
Sovereign Warlock glanced at Michael from the corner of his eye.
"This is exactly why I told you not to judge people by realm alone."
Michael clenched his fists but didn’t argue back.
Max smiled lightly.
"It wasn’t as impressive as the rumors make it sound."
Sovereign Warlock laughed again.
"Modesty suits you better than arrogance, but fake modesty gets annoying too.
You killed him because you were strong enough.
That much’s clear."
Arvantos looked toward the gathered geniuses and spoke, pulling everyone’s attention back to the main matter.
"You’ve all gathered here because the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage will open soon.
Some of you come from the Primordial Race.
Some come from the Four Sacred Clans.
Some are disciples of hidden experts.
Some are among the ten who recently awakened Primordial Bloodline."
His voice turned solemn.
"But once you enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, none of those identities will protect you.
The geniuses of the Devil Universe, Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe won’t care about your background unless it gives them a reason to kill you faster."
The atmosphere turned serious again.
Arvantos continued, "Once the gate opens, each of you walks your own path.
Whether you find opportunity or death will come down to your strength, judgment, and luck.
I won’t repeat this again.
The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage isn’t some protected trial arranged by your elders.
It’s not a competition where someone steps in when you’re about to die.
It’s a battlefield, a graveyard, a treasury, and a road left behind by existences far older than the current order of the five universes.
Anyone who enters must accept that everything they own can be taken from them."
No one said a word.
Even the arrogant young geniuses who’d come from hidden experts and ancient clans went quieter under those words.
They were proud, but they weren’t foolish.
If Arvantos was speaking this seriously, the danger of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage had to go far beyond ordinary imagination.
Arvantos raised his gaze toward the distant sky of the Primordial Ancestral Domain.
"The entrance to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t sit in any ordinary region of the Divine Realm.
It lies at a forbidden point in space, far beyond the controlled star regions of most forces.
Even Divine King Realm cultivators aren’t allowed to approach that place without permission, and ordinary Divine Lord Realm cultivators would die before they ever reached the outer boundary."
Several expressions changed.
A forbidden point in space.
Those words alone were enough to make the gathered geniuses understand that the journey itself wouldn’t be simple.
Arvantos continued, "That place sits too close to the Wall of Eternity.
The laws there run unstable, space stretches thin, time doesn’t always flow evenly, and the boundary pressure can crush weaker bodies into dust.
There are no cities nearby.
No forces, no clans, no trade routes, and no safe domains.
It’s a place that exists outside the normal map of our universe."
His gaze returned to them.
"It’ll take us one day to get there."

chapters.title: Chapter 2030: Wall of Eternity!
paragraphs: The moment he finished speaking, Arvantos waved his hand. The space above the gathering area trembled. A vast shadow slowly appeared in the sky. At first it looked like a golden cloud descending from the heavens, but as the light faded, everyone saw an enormous flying boat hovering above them.

The boat stretched hundreds of meters long, built from ancient bronze-gold metal and dark divine wood that seemed to have soaked up starlight for countless years. Its body was covered in Primordial runes, each one giving off a faint glow that made the surrounding space ripple gently.

The front of the boat was shaped like the head of an ancient beast, neither dragon nor phoenix, but something older and heavier. Its eyes were made of two rotating golden crystals, and its open mouth held a formation circle that looked capable of tearing through space.
Along the sides of the boat, layered defensive barriers flowed like transparent waves, giving off an aura that made even the more reckless geniuses instinctively hold themselves back.

Max looked at the flying boat with interest. He could sense spatial law, defensive law, speed formations, concealment patterns, and something deeper hidden beneath all of it. This wasn’t just a means of transportation. It was a war vessel, a moving fortress crafted by the Primordial Race.
Arvantos looked at everyone. "Board."

No one hesitated. One by one, the young geniuses flew toward the boat and landed on its wide deck. Max stepped onto the vessel too, and the moment his feet touched the surface, he felt a steady power flowing beneath him. The entire boat felt alive, as if every plank, rune, and formation connected to one central will.

Damian stood near the edge of the deck with his arms folded. Revona looked toward the distant stars with a calm expression. Rakan stayed silent, while Michael stood some distance away with his master, Sovereign Warlock, who looked far more relaxed than anyone else present.

After everyone boarded, Arvantos appeared at the front of the flying boat. He didn’t give another long speech. He only raised his hand. The runes across the boat lit up all at once. A low hum spread through the air, and the entire vessel trembled lightly before rising higher into the sky.

The Primordial Ancestral Domain slowly shrank beneath them. Floating mountains, golden rivers, ancient palaces, and towering statues grew smaller and smaller until the entire sacred domain looked like a golden painting beneath the clouds.
Then the flying boat shot upward. The world below disappeared. The boat pierced through the sky and entered the starry void.

Countless stars appeared around them. The Divine Realm stretched vast beyond measure. Star regions spread in every direction, and distant continents, floating worlds, and law rivers glimmered in the endless darkness.
The flying boat moved with terrifying speed, yet the deck stayed steady. Its barriers blocked the pressure of space, the cold of the void, and the turbulent flow of laws outside.

Max stood near the railing and looked into the distance. This wasn’t his first time seeing the vastness of the universe, but the feeling hit different now. In a few days, he’d be entering a place connected not just to this universe, but to all five.

A full day passed as the flying boat traveled through the starry void. During that time, almost no one spoke much. Some geniuses sat cross-legged and settled their minds. Some stood silently staring into space. Some checked their weapons, pills, treasures, and protective talismans. Though they were all proud, none of them dared treat the upcoming pilgrimage lightly.

Max used the time to calm his mind too. This time, he didn’t enter the Dimension of Time. Instead, he quietly stood on the deck and watched the strange changes in space as the boat moved farther and farther from the familiar regions of the Divine Realm.
The laws around them gradually grew thinner, but at the same time heavier. Space no longer felt like a stable ocean. It felt like cracked glass stretched across endless darkness.

After one day, the flying boat finally slowed down. The stars around them had changed. This region of space looked unlike anywhere Max had seen before. No nearby worlds. No continents. No floating cities. No law rivers flowing through the void.
The entire area sat empty, but the emptiness itself felt wrong. Far ahead, the darkness seemed to curve inward, as if the universe had hit a point where it no longer wanted to continue.

The flying boat stopped in front of that strange region. Everyone on the deck stood up. Max looked forward, and his eyes narrowed. At first, he saw nothing. Then, as his perception spread outward, he felt it.

A wall. Not a wall made of stone, metal, or formation power, but a boundary so vast and profound his mind could barely hold onto it. It stretched beyond sight in every direction. It had no clear shape, yet it was undeniably there. Space ended at that point, and something older than space stood beyond it.
The Wall of Eternity.
Max had heard about it plenty of times by now, but hearing about it and standing in front of it were two entirely different things.

The boundary gave him the feeling that it wasn’t just separating lands or star regions. It was separating realities. It was the membrane keeping universes from crashing into each other, the line dividing different cosmic orders, different laws, different origins, and different destinies.
Even from the safety of the flying boat, Max felt a heavy pressure pressing against his body. His five Divine Veins stirred faintly. His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline grew more active too.
Arvantos stood at the front of the vessel, looking toward the invisible boundary ahead.
"This is the place," he said.
Everyone turned toward him.
Arvantos continued, "This point in space is one of the forbidden edges of our universe. The Wall of Eternity sits right here."
His voice stayed calm, but everyone could hear the seriousness underneath it.
"But this side of the Wall is different from the side the devils pierced. It’s not connected to the Devil Universe, the Spirit Universe, the Angel Universe, or the Dragon Universe."
Max’s gaze sharpened.
Arvantos raised his hand and pointed toward the distorted darkness ahead. "This side connects to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
The deck fell completely silent. The young geniuses stared forward with solemn expressions.

Arvantos continued, "The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t belong to any single universe. It exists in a strange region where the boundaries of the five universes overlap without truly merging. To reach it, each universe has its own separate entrance point. This is ours."
The space ahead began to ripple faintly, as if responding to his words.

"Remember this," Arvantos said. "Once the entrance opens, you’ll no longer be standing under the protection of the Primordial Race, the Four Sacred Clans, your masters, your families, or me. You’ll be entering a place where ancient laws decide the rules, and where every race sends the ones they believe can survive."
He turned and looked at the gathered geniuses. "This is your last moment to get ready."
No one stepped back. No one spoke of retreat.
The flying boat floated silently before the Wall of Eternity, and the strange darkness ahead slowly began to pulse, as if something ancient on the other side had just woken up.

chapters.title: Chapter 2031: Into the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage!
paragraphs: Max and the other geniuses waited patiently for the entrance to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage to open.

The flying boat stayed suspended before the forbidden edge of space, unmoving and silent. Around them, the starry void stretched in every direction, but this region didn’t feel like ordinary space. It was too still. Too cold. Too heavy.

There were no distant worlds, no drifting continents, no shining law rivers, and no signs of life anywhere nearby. Only the vast darkness ahead kept pulsing faintly, as if something hidden behind the Wall of Eternity was breathing.

No one spoke much. Even Michael, who’d been arrogant not long ago, stood quietly beside Sovereign Warlock with a serious expression. The young geniuses from the Primordial Race, the Four Sacred Clans, and the hidden experts all watched the distorted space ahead with different looks in their eyes.
Some looked excited. Some looked nervous. Some tried to stay calm, but their tightened fists and sharpened breathing gave away their real feelings.

Max stood near the front of the deck, his gaze fixed on the invisible boundary ahead. The pressure coming from the Wall of Eternity was hard to describe. It didn’t just press against the body. It pressed against perception, bloodline, soul, and law comprehension all at once. Max could feel his Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stirring faintly.
A low sound suddenly spread through the void. It wasn’t thunder. It wasn’t the roar of a beast. It sounded more like an ancient door turning after countless years of silence.
Everyone on the flying boat went alert at once.
The darkness ahead began to twist. At first the change was faint. A thin silver-gold line appeared in the empty space before them, stretching vertically across the void.

Then the line widened slowly, and layers of ancient symbols surfaced around it. Some symbols glowed gold. Some glowed silver. Some looked black. Some carried colors Max had never seen before, colors that seemed to exist somewhere between law and light.
The Wall of Eternity trembled faintly. A crack opened in the boundary. Beyond that crack, Max saw a road.

It wasn’t a normal road. It looked like countless broken stars had fused together into a vast path stretching into endless mist. Ancient ruins floated in the distance. Rivers of light flowed backward through the sky.

Fragments of shattered palaces drifted like dead moons. Enormous bones stretched across the horizon, and somewhere far deeper, Max sensed a power so ancient that even his soul went quiet in front of it.
The entrance to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage had opened.

A heavy aura rushed out from the crack and swept over the flying boat. Several young geniuses immediately changed expressions. Some took half a step back. Some released their bloodline aura on instinct. Some had to circulate their cultivation just to steady themselves.
This was only the aura leaking out from the entrance, yet it already carried the feel of an ancient battlefield soaked in countless eras of death, glory, and forgotten ambition.
Arvantos stood at the front of the flying boat, his robes unmoving despite the violent flow of power from the entrance. He turned around and looked at everyone.
"This is the entrance to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
His voice stayed calm, but every word reached all the geniuses clearly.

"Once you pass through it, you’ll no longer be under my protection. The Primordial Race won’t be able to watch over you. The Four Sacred Clans won’t be able to interfere. Your masters, elders, teachers, and families won’t be able to save you when danger comes."
The geniuses’ expressions turned more solemn.

Arvantos continued, "Inside that place, your identity only matters if you have the strength to defend it. Don’t think your background will scare the geniuses of other universes. The Devil Race will kill you the moment they see weakness."
His gaze swept slowly across all of them. No one dared take his warning lightly.

Arvantos’s expression turned even more serious. "The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage splits into countless regions, and not all of you will land in the same place after entering. Some of you might get separated immediately. Some of you might meet again after days, months, or even years, depending on how the internal space behaves. Time, distance, and direction aren’t always reliable there. If you find companions you can trust, value them. If you find enemies you can’t kill, survive first and settle the debt later."
Max’s eyes moved slightly. That meant they might not be able to rely on each other once they got in.

Arvantos continued, "You’re all geniuses of our universe. Some of you carry the blood of Primordials. Some carry the inheritance of the Four Sacred Clans. Some were trained by hidden experts. Some have walked paths even I can’t fully see. But none of that matters if you die at the first step."
His voice dropped. "So live."
Those two words came out simple, but they carried more weight than any grand speech.

"Take what you can take. Fight when you have to fight. Retreat when you have to retreat. Learn, endure, and come back stronger than you are today. The war with the devils has already cast its shadow over our universe, and the future won’t wait for slow growth."

Arvantos looked at them one last time. "When you come back from the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, I hope to see fewer children standing in front of me and more blades sharp enough to cut into the coming storm."
The flying boat fell into complete silence.
Then Sovereign Warlock laughed lightly, breaking the heaviness for a moment. "You heard him, brats. Go in alive, come back alive, and try not to embarrass your masters too badly."
Some of the tension eased, just slightly.

Arvantos raised his hand. A bridge of golden light stretched out from the flying boat toward the opened entrance. It crossed the empty void and connected directly to the star-forged road beyond the crack in the Wall of Eternity.

The first group of Primordial geniuses stepped forward. Without hesitation, they walked across the bridge and entered the entrance. Their figures got swallowed by the silver-gold light and disappeared into the mist beyond.
After them, the disciples of the hidden experts started moving. Some looked calm. Some looked excited. Some carried silent killing intent in their eyes.
The geniuses of the Four Sacred Clans went next. Several of them glanced at Max before crossing the bridge, but none of them said anything.

chapters.title: Chapter 2032: A very different Place!
paragraphs: Then it was Max and the others’ turn.

Damian walked forward first, his expression cold and steady. Revona followed with a faint smile, though her eyes carried the depth of someone stepping toward an old memory. Ervin took a deep breath and entered after her.
Rakan, Rosaline, Aurelian, and the others moved one by one, each carrying their own thoughts and ambitions.
Michael walked past Max and paused for a brief moment. He looked like he wanted to say something, but in the end he just snorted and stepped onto the bridge.

Max ignored him. His gaze stayed fixed on the entrance. Beyond that light waited the strongest young geniuses of five universes. Beyond that light waited danger, trials, ruins, enemies, inheritances, and maybe the path to the Eternal Body. It was a place where many geniuses would rise and many more would end up buried.
Max stepped forward. He didn’t look back. With calm eyes, he walked into the entrance of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
The silver-gold light swallowed his figure. A moment later, the starry void outside the Wall of Eternity settled back into quiet.

On the other side of the entrance, Max found himself standing on pale yellow land. The moment his feet touched the ground, the silver-gold light behind him disappeared, and the strange pressure of the Wall of Eternity vanished as if it had never existed. Max didn’t move right away. He stood where he was and quietly took in his surroundings.

The land beneath him stretched wide and dry, glowing faintly with a dull yellow sheen. It didn’t look like ordinary soil. Every grain of dust seemed to carry a trace of ancient energy, and when the wind swept across the ground, the pale sand moved like thin waves across the surface of a silent sea.
No mountains stood nearby, no forests, no rivers, no buildings. As far as Max could see, the land stretched endlessly in every direction.
The sky above him looked unusually blue. It wasn’t the gentle blue of an ordinary world. It ran too deep, too clean, too vast, as if someone had washed away every trace of impurity from the heavens.

Even stranger, both a sun and a moon hung in that sky at the same time. The sun burned with a soft golden light, while the moon gave off a faint silver glow despite the brightness around it. Their light mixed together without either one drowning out the other, filling the world with a strange balance of warmth and cold.
Max took a slow breath. The natural energy here entered his body almost on its own. His expression shifted slightly.
"What a refreshing feeling," he muttered.

It felt like he’d arrived in an entirely different kind of world. The energy here didn’t match the Divine Realm or the Primordial Ancestral Domain. It felt more ancient, more active, and more natural.
It didn’t feel neatly arranged by formations or controlled by powerful forces. Instead, it felt wild and pure, like energy that had flowed freely since the beginning of time.
His Tier 4 Primordial Bloodline stirred faintly. The five Divine Veins inside his body responded too.
Max stood there for a while, letting his senses spread outward. After looking around for some time, he confirmed one thing.

He was in the middle of nowhere. No obvious road, no city, no camp, and no sign of the other geniuses who’d entered with him. It seemed Arvantos had been right. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage didn’t send everyone to the same place. Each person had to begin their journey alone, at least for now.
"I need to find civilization first," Max muttered to himself.
Both Freya and Arvantos had warned him about this before he entered. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was vast, strange, and filled with places that could kill even geniuses if they wandered blindly.

Finding a civilization, a settlement, or at least a gathering point was the safest first move. There, he could learn about the region, understand the local rules, and gather information about trials, marks, danger zones, and opportunities.
Max looked around again. No obvious landmarks stood out.

After a short moment, he activated his Dimensional Sovereign Body. His perception shifted. The world around him changed. Space no longer felt like just empty distance. It became layered, folded, and filled with faint traces left behind by movement.
The wind, the ground, and even the path of energy through the air grew clearer in his senses. Soon he noticed something.

Footprints. They were faint and almost completely covered by pale dust, but they were there. Someone or something had passed through this area not too long ago. The traces moved in one direction, and although Max couldn’t immediately tell whether they belonged to humans, beasts, or another race, they were still the only clue he had.
He decided to follow them. Max moved forward calmly, his senses spread around him.
But he’d only taken a few steps when the ground ahead trembled. A low growl echoed across the pale yellow land.
Max stopped.

From the dust in front of him, a huge beast slowly walked out and blocked his path. It was a wolf-like creature, though calling it a wolf didn’t really do it justice. Its body was massive, nearly five times bigger than Max, and its fur was dark gray with streaks of crimson running through it like dried blood.

It had six powerful legs, each ending in claws sharp enough to tear through stone. Most terrifying of all, it had six heads, and each head stared at Max with a different expression of hunger, cruelty, madness, and animal instinct.
Its aura surged outward.
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "3rd level Divine Lord Realm."

The beast wasn’t some hidden guardian, and it didn’t seem to be a rare creature protecting an inheritance. It was just a random beast he’d run into shortly after entering this place, yet it already carried the strength of the 3rd level Divine Lord Realm.
Max frowned. "Even a random beast here sits at the 3rd level of the Divine Lord Realm. My cultivation really is too low for the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
He wasn’t afraid. But he wasn’t careless either. In the Divine Realm, his strength already counted as terrifying for someone at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm.

He could fight across realms, kill enemies above his level, and shock even top experts with his foundation. But the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage clearly worked differently. This was a place where the basic standard of danger sat much higher.

chapters.title: Chapter 2033: A Bronze Mark!
paragraphs: The six-headed wolf didn’t give him more time to think. All six of its heads roared at once. The sound shook the air, and a violent wave of killing intent rushed toward Max. In the next instant, the beast lunged forward with terrifying speed.
Its six legs pushed against the ground at the same time, cracking the pale yellow land beneath it as its huge body turned into a gray-crimson blur.

Max’s eyes stayed calm. He activated his Voidwalker Bloodline. In an instant, ten blue void rings appeared around his two arms. The rings rotated once around his wrists and forearms before flying out together.
They crossed the space between Max and the beast in a flash, circling the six-headed wolf before it could reach him. The beast was still mid-leap when the rings locked into place around it.
Space folded inward. A spherical seal formed instantly.

The six-headed wolf froze in the air less than a few feet from Max’s face. Its claws were still stretched forward, its jaws were still open, and its killing intent was still surging, but its body could no longer move.
The ten void rings rotated around the spherical seal, releasing layers of blue light that pressed down on its body, aura, bloodline, and Divine Lord Realm power.
Max studied the seal carefully. His brows furrowed slightly.
"I can feel the void rings straining to hold the seal."

The ten void rings were still holding, but the pressure showed. The six-headed wolf’s cultivation ran far above Max’s own realm, and although the Ten Void Sealing Art was powerful, the gap in cultivation couldn’t be completely ignored.
The beast’s Divine Lord Realm energy kept pushing against the seal from inside, causing faint ripples to appear across the blue sphere.
"Is it because I’m sealing something far above my cultivation realm?" Max muttered.

That seemed like the most likely reason. Against someone closer to his own level, the void rings could suppress almost effortlessly. But against a Divine Lord Realm beast, even a random one, the burden grew much heavier.
This was valuable information. It meant that inside the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, he couldn’t rely on the Ten Void Sealing Art as carelessly as before against enemies far above his realm.
Still, the seal held enough.

Max raised one hand. Black flames rose from his palm. The flames looked dark, heavy, and devouring. Unlike the Primordial Flames, which refined and purified, these black flames existed to consume, corrode, and destroy.
Max flicked his fingers, and a thin stream of black fire entered the spherical seal formed by the ten void rings.

The moment the flames touched the trapped beast, they spread across its body. The six-headed wolf roared violently. Its Divine Lord Realm energy erupted, and the blue sealing sphere trembled more intensely.

But the void rings held firm. The black flames burrowed into the beast’s flesh, devoured its blood, consumed its energy, and burned through its life force. Within a few breaths, the massive creature that had lunged at Max with such ferocity got reduced to nothing but ashes inside the sealed space.
The ten void rings slowly returned to Max’s arms. The ashes scattered into the wind.

Max stood in place and sensed the change inside his body. A small portion of energy had gotten absorbed through the devouring nature of his flames, but the increase wasn’t much. His body felt slightly strengthened, and his energy grew a bit denser, but it fell far short of causing any major change.
"Only a small increase in strength," Max said with a wry smile. He shook his head. "Even devouring a 3rd level Divine Lord Realm beast isn’t enough to make me break through."

He felt a little disappointed, but not surprised. His foundation ran too strong. His body, bloodline, soul, Pseudo Cosmic Paths, Divine Veins, and several inheritances had pushed his base far beyond ordinary cultivators.

Because of that, ordinary energy gains no longer moved him forward easily. If he wanted to break through, he’d need far greater resources, deeper opportunities, or battles that forced his foundation to transform.
Just then, Max felt an itch on his right wrist. He lowered his gaze.
A faint bronze glow appeared on his skin. The glow slowly gathered into a mark. It formed a circular shape, and inside the circle sat the image of a sword pointing downward.

The mark looked simple at first, but when Max focused on it, he could feel a strange law hidden inside it. It wasn’t just a symbol. It was a record, a recognition, and maybe even a form of currency within the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
Max stared at the bronze mark for a moment. Then he smiled faintly.
"Is this the mark Big Sis told me about?"

Freya hadn’t explained the marks in much detail, but she’d told him one thing very clearly. Marks meant everything in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Arvantos had also hinted at their importance before sending them in.

Marks could decide access, status, opportunities, rankings, exchanges, and even survival in certain places. Some trials required them. Some cities recognized them. Some inheritances demanded them. Some enemies hunted others precisely because of them.
Max lifted his wrist and looked at the bronze circle with the sword inside it.
"I need to know more about these marks," Max muttered as he kept staring at the bronze symbol on his wrist.

The mark didn’t feel ordinary. It wasn’t just something left behind after killing a beast. It had entered his skin without resistance, attached itself to his aura, and settled into his body as if the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage itself had acknowledged his kill.

The more Max sensed it, the more he realized the mark connected to some deeper rule of this place. It wasn’t an external reward handed out by a person, sect, or formation. It was part of the structure of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage itself.
That made him even more curious.

Both Freya and Arvantos had mentioned marks before he entered, but neither of them had explained the details clearly. Freya had only told him marks were extremely important, while Arvantos had merely hinted that opportunities, status, and survival could depend on them.
Neither of them had gone further, and Max didn’t believe that was because they’d forgotten or wanted him kept in the dark.
There had to be a reason.

chapters.title: Chapter 2034: Getting Robbed?
paragraphs: "Restrictions," Max murmured.

That was the only explanation that made sense. If even someone as powerful as Arvantos, one of the four Primarchs of the Primordial Race, couldn’t freely explain the internal rules of this place, then the restrictions around the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage ran far more terrifying than Max had first assumed.
These rules weren’t something the current five universes had created. They were ancient, hidden, and strong enough to bind even the peak figures standing at the top of the Divine Realm.
This thought made Max’s eyes deepen. "This place really is special."

He lowered his wrist and kept following the faint traces he’d found earlier. The pale yellow land stretched endlessly around him. Dust moved with the wind, the blue sky stayed impossibly clear, and the sun and moon kept hanging together above the world like two silent watchers.
The deeper Max walked, the more he sensed that this land only looked empty on the surface. Beneath the silence, traces of danger sat everywhere.
The ground carried old blood aura in some places. The wind occasionally brought faint killing intent from far away. Somewhere beneath the pale soil, broken laws seemed to sleep in fragments.
Max kept walking for some time before his footsteps suddenly stopped. His gaze shifted slightly toward a cluster of large boulders ahead.
The boulders looked ordinary at first. They sat half-buried in the pale soil, weathered by wind, covered with dry cracks.

But Max’s perception ran far sharper than most cultivators at his realm. With the Dimensional Sovereign Body active, space itself revealed small irregularities to him. Behind one of those boulders, the flow of space was slightly distorted.
There were people hiding there.
Max’s expression stayed calm. "You three can come out now," he said.
His voice wasn’t loud, but it carried clearly across the empty land.
Nothing happened. The wind kept blowing. The boulders stayed still.
Max waited for two breaths, then sneered faintly. Black flames rose from his palm. He flicked his fingers, and a ball of devouring fire shot toward the largest boulder.

Before the black flames could touch it, three figures stepped out from behind the rocks. They stood tall and muscular, with dark gray skin, crimson lines crawling across their bodies, and sharp horns growing from their foreheads.

Their eyes glowed deep red, and their smiles carried a cruel hunger Max had already seen too many times from devils. Each of them wore dark armor made from some unknown beast hide and black metal, and all three carried weapons stained with old blood.
Devils.
Max looked at them silently.
The three devils didn’t seem surprised they’d been discovered. If anything, they looked amused.
"Hehe, this Primordial sensed us somehow," one of the devils said, glancing at the other two with a sneer.
Another devil laughed and licked his lips. "Good. Saves us the trouble of waiting. We finally caught ourselves a Primordial newbie."

The third devil looked Max up and down, his gaze lingering on Max’s wrist. When he saw the bronze mark there, his smile widened. "He’s already got a mark too. Not bad. Looks like this little Primordial killed something right after spawning."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. Spawning. So this area really was a place where newcomers appeared after entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.

The first devil cracked his neck and stepped forward. "You’re unlucky, kid. This is one of the better newbie landing zones, and we’ve been guarding this area for a while now. Every time the entrance opens, a few fresh geniuses show up around here. Some carry treasures. Some carry marks. Some carry storage rings packed with treasures from their clans."
The second devil laughed. "Primordials are usually rich. Their bloodlines are useful too, even if they’re a pain to extract. Maybe this one’s worth more than the last angel brat we killed."
The third devil stared at Max with greed in his eyes. "Hand over your storage ring, your weapons, your mark, and whatever treasures you’re carrying. Cooperate, and maybe we’ll let you die quickly."
The three of them laughed together.

Max didn’t laugh. He sensed their auras clearly. All three devils sat at the 2nd level of the Divine Lord Realm. Out in the Divine Realm, that cultivation would’ve been more than enough to crush most people at his level.

Even inside the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, they clearly weren’t weak among those who preyed on newly arrived geniuses. Their choice to hide near a landing zone was deliberate too. They weren’t here to explore trials or fight powerful enemies. They were here to ambush people who entered alone before they understood the rules of this place.
Max’s gaze turned colder. "You guard this area to rob and kill newcomers?"
The first devil grinned. "You say that like it’s a bad thing."
The second devil added, "In the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the weak exist to feed the strong."
The third devil raised his weapon. "And today, you’re the weak one."
Max sighed softly. "I see."
The three devils were still smiling when Max moved. There was no warning. No exchange of threats. Max had no interest in listening to them talk any longer.

Dragonheart appeared in his hand, and in the same instant, the aura around him changed completely. The pale yellow land seemed to lose its warmth. The wind went silent. Even the killing intent of the three devils froze for a brief moment, as if something had cut the emotions right out of the air itself.
The Emotion Severing Path erupted. But this time, Max didn’t use just a trace of it. He used its full power. His eyes turned calm to the point of coldness.
The first devil’s smile vanished. "What is this?"
He tried to retreat, but it was already too late.
Max stepped forward and swung Dragonheart once. The sword light wasn’t dazzling. It didn’t explode with thunder, flames, or overwhelming radiance. It came out quiet, pale, and terrifyingly clean.
Wherever it passed, killing intent disappeared. Fear disappeared. Anger disappeared. Even the devil’s instinctive urge to resist seemed to vanish for a single instant.
That single instant decided life and death. The sword light crossed the first devil’s neck. His head flew into the air.

Their eyes glowed deep red, and their smiles carried a cruel hunger Max had already seen too many times from devils.
Each of them wore dark armor made from some unknown beast hide and black metal, and all three carried weapons stained with old blood.
Devils.
Max looked at them silently.
The three devils didn’t seem surprised they’d been discovered.
If anything, they looked amused.
"Hehe, this Primordial sensed us somehow," one of the devils said, glancing at the other two with a sneer.
Another devil laughed and licked his lips.
"Good.
Saves us the trouble of waiting.
We finally caught ourselves a Primordial newbie."
The third devil looked Max up and down, his gaze lingering on Max’s wrist.
When he saw the bronze mark there, his smile widened.
"He’s already got a mark too.
Not bad.
Looks like this little Primordial killed something right after spawning."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.
Spawning.
So this area really was a place where newcomers appeared after entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
The first devil cracked his neck and stepped forward.
"You’re unlucky, kid.
This is one of the better newbie landing zones, and we’ve been guarding this area for a while now.
Every time the entrance opens, a few fresh geniuses show up around here.
Some carry treasures.
Some carry marks.
Some carry storage rings packed with treasures from their clans."
The second devil laughed.
"Primordials are usually rich.
Their bloodlines are useful too, even if they’re a pain to extract.
Maybe this one’s worth more than the last angel brat we killed."
The third devil stared at Max with greed in his eyes.
"Hand over your storage ring, your weapons, your mark, and whatever treasures you’re carrying.
Cooperate, and maybe we’ll let you die quickly."
The three of them laughed together.
Max didn’t laugh.
He sensed their auras clearly.
All three devils sat at the 2nd level of the Divine Lord Realm.
Out in the Divine Realm, that cultivation would’ve been more than enough to crush most people at his level.
Even inside the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, they clearly weren’t weak among those who preyed on newly arrived geniuses.
Their choice to hide near a landing zone was deliberate too.
They weren’t here to explore trials or fight powerful enemies.
They were here to ambush people who entered alone before they understood the rules of this place.
Max’s gaze turned colder.
"You guard this area to rob and kill newcomers?"
The first devil grinned.
"You say that like it’s a bad thing."
The second devil added, "In the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the weak exist to feed the strong."
The third devil raised his weapon.
"And today, you’re the weak one."
Max sighed softly.
"I see."
The three devils were still smiling when Max moved.
There was no warning.
No exchange of threats.
Max had no interest in listening to them talk any longer.
Dragonheart appeared in his hand, and in the same instant, the aura around him changed completely.
The pale yellow land seemed to lose its warmth.
The wind went silent.
Even the killing intent of the three devils froze for a brief moment, as if something had cut the emotions right out of the air itself.
The Emotion Severing Path erupted.
But this time, Max didn’t use just a trace of it.
He used its full power.
His eyes turned calm to the point of coldness.
The first devil’s smile vanished.
"What is this?"
He tried to retreat, but it was already too late.
Max stepped forward and swung Dragonheart once.
The sword light wasn’t dazzling.
It didn’t explode with thunder, flames, or overwhelming radiance.
It came out quiet, pale, and terrifyingly clean.
Wherever it passed, killing intent disappeared.
Fear disappeared.
Anger disappeared.
Even the devil’s instinctive urge to resist seemed to vanish for a single instant.
That single instant decided life and death.
The sword light crossed the first devil’s neck.
His head flew into the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 2035: Five Types of Marks!
paragraphs: Before the body even hit the ground, Max had already appeared beside the second devil. The second devil roared and tried to activate his devil bloodline. Crimson tattoos lit up across his skin, and dark energy surged from his body like burning smoke.
But the moment the Emotion Severing Path came down on him, his roar weakened. His rage faded. His battle intent got sliced apart before it could fully form.

Max’s sword pierced through his chest. The power of the Emotion Severing Path flowed through the blade and spread through the devil’s body. The second devil froze. His eyes widened. Then the light in them dimmed as his soul, emotions, and life force all got severed together.
Two devils died almost instantly.

The third devil stood frozen in place. His weapon was still half-raised, but his body no longer dared move. Everything had happened too fast. One moment, the three of them were laughing about robbing a newly arrived Primordial.
The next moment, two of them were dead, and the young man they’d called weak stood right in front of him with a sword in hand.
The third devil’s face turned pale. Only now did he truly understand. This Primordial wasn’t prey. He was a monster.

Max appeared in front of him and placed Dragonheart against his throat. The cold edge of the sword touched the devil’s skin, and the lingering power of the Emotion Severing Path made his entire body tremble.
It wasn’t ordinary fear. It felt like something deep inside him was slowly getting stripped away, as if his courage, arrogance, and will to resist were being peeled from his soul layer by layer.
Max looked at him calmly. "Where’s the nearest city?"
The devil’s throat moved slightly. He wanted to speak, but his voice didn’t come out right away.
Max pressed the blade a little closer. A thin line of blood appeared on the devil’s neck.
"Answer," Max said. "And think carefully before you do."
The third devil swallowed hard.
Max’s eyes stayed cold. "If you lie to me, you won’t die like the other two."
The devil’s pupils contracted.
Max continued in the same calm voice, "They died fast. You won’t."
The devil’s body trembled harder. The two corpses beside him were still falling apart under the lingering power of Max’s sword. One had lost his head before he could even understand what happened.

The other had been pierced through the chest, his life erased so cleanly that even his devil energy couldn’t erupt properly. Compared to them, the third devil suddenly felt like death might have been mercy.
"I’ll talk," he said quickly, his voice hoarse. "I’ll talk. Don’t kill me."
Max didn’t move the sword away. "Nearest city."

The devil took a shaky breath and pointed toward the direction the faint footprints had been leading. "Keep going that way. There’s a city called Bloodstone City. It’s the nearest gathering place in this region. If you move at full speed, you can reach it in half a day. If you walk normally, it’ll take longer."
Max stared at him.

The devil quickly added, "I’m not lying. I swear I’m not lying. Everyone who spawns in this outer region tries to reach Bloodstone City first. It’s not safe, but it’s still better than wandering outside. There are traders there, information brokers, mark exchange halls, and people who know where the nearby trials are."
Max’s eyes moved slightly. Bloodstone City. Mark exchange halls. Information brokers. That was exactly the kind of place he needed.
He looked at the devil again. "What are marks used for?"
The devil hesitated for a brief moment. Max’s sword pressed slightly deeper. The hesitation vanished immediately.

"Everything," the devil said hurriedly. "Marks get used for everything. You need them to enter trials, buy information, exchange resources, rent cultivation rooms, enter some cities, and open certain inheritance grounds. They also decide your ranking and status in some places. Without marks, you’re nothing in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
Max’s gaze deepened. Freya had been right. Marks truly were everything here.

The devil continued, afraid that silence would anger Max. "There are five types of marks in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. The first is the Bronze Mark. Every newcomer gets one when they enter, which is why it’s also called the beginner’s mark. The second is the Gold Mark. Above that sits the Sacred Mark. The fourth is the Divine Mark, and the last one is the Godslayer Mark."
Max glanced at the bronze sword mark on his wrist. "Only five?" he asked.

The devil nodded quickly. "Only five recognized grades. The gap between them is enormous. A Bronze Mark sits at the lowest, while a Godslayer Mark stands at the absolute peak. Most participants spend countless years struggling to advance even one grade. Plenty die before they can get a Gold Mark, and only a tiny number ever reach the Divine or Godslayer level."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "How does someone get the higher marks?"
The devil’s expression turned solemn. "You can’t get them directly. You have to build up enough marks of the lower grade first."
"Explain."

"To become eligible for a Gold Mark, you need to collect one thousand Bronze Marks," the devil said. "Once you’ve gathered one thousand Bronze Marks, the rules of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage let you condense them into a single Gold Mark."
Max’s gaze sharpened. "One thousand Bronze Marks for one Gold Mark?"

"Yes," the devil replied. "And the same rule applies at every level. After collecting one thousand Gold Marks, you become eligible to condense them into a Sacred Mark. Then you need to collect one thousand Sacred Marks to become eligible for a Divine Mark. Finally, after collecting one thousand Divine Marks, you can condense them into the highest grade, the Godslayer Mark."

Max stayed silent. The numbers were staggering. One thousand Bronze Marks for one Gold Mark. One thousand Gold Marks for one Sacred Mark. One thousand Sacred Marks for one Divine Mark. And one thousand Divine Marks for a single Godslayer Mark. The progression wasn’t just difficult. It was practically monstrous.

chapters.title: Chapter 2036: Uses of Marks!
paragraphs: The devil kept explaining, terrified Max might think he was hiding something. "The marks don’t just disappear for no reason. When you meet the requirement, the Pilgrimage recognizes your accumulation and gives you the choice to advance. But once you condense the lower marks into a higher one, the lower marks get consumed. You can’t use the same marks twice."
"What happens if someone collects enough but refuses to advance?" Max asked.

"They can keep accumulating," the devil answered. "Some people wait because lower-grade marks can get used directly for certain exchanges and transactions. But the higher your mark grade, the greater your authority, and the more valuable your status becomes. A Gold Mark holder gets treated very differently from someone who only carries Bronze Marks."
Max looked down at his wrist again. The bronze symbol seemed to glow faintly beneath his skin.
"So every newcomer starts with one Bronze Mark," he said.
"Yes."
"And killing beasts gives more Bronze Marks?"

"Usually," the devil replied. "The number depends on the strength of the beast and the rules of the region. Some beasts give one Bronze Mark. Stronger ones might give several. Certain trials can reward dozens or even hundreds. Killing other participants can also give marks, but the amount depends on the victim’s accumulated marks and the rules governing the area."
Max’s eyes turned cold. "So killing someone lets you take their marks?"

The devil nodded nervously. "Sometimes. Not every region allows it, but plenty do. That’s why people are so careful about revealing their mark count. A powerful participant carrying a large number of marks turns into a walking treasure vault."

Max understood immediately. The three devils hadn’t just wanted his storage ring and treasures. They’d also noticed he already carried a Bronze Mark. If he’d accumulated more, they would’ve tried to seize those too.

The devil continued, "There are also missions, inheritances, ancient ruins, and special trials that reward marks. Some opportunities can grant more marks than months of killing beasts. But the more valuable the reward, the more dangerous the trial."
"What about the Godslayer Mark?" Max asked. "Has anyone ever obtained one?"
The devil’s face changed. Fear and reverence appeared in his eyes.

"I don’t know," he admitted. "There are rumors that a few ancient existences once obtained Godslayer Marks, but nobody knows if those stories are even true. In the current era, I’ve never heard of anyone openly holding one. Even Divine Mark holders are rare enough to become legends in most regions."

Max’s expression stayed calm, but his mind was already working. The mark system was clearly more than a simple reward mechanism. It was a hierarchy built into the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, one that measured achievement, authority, and maybe even destiny.
If the highest mark truly required one thousand Divine Marks, obtaining a Godslayer Mark would demand an unimaginable accumulation of lower-grade marks.
The devil looked at Max carefully. "Do you understand now?"
Max raised his eyes. "Not completely."
The devil’s face went pale.
Max continued, "You said marks can be used for exchanges and entry fees. If I spend a Bronze Mark, does that reduce the number I need for advancement?"

"Yes," the devil answered quickly. "Any mark you spend gets removed from your total. If you want to condense one thousand Bronze Marks into a Gold Mark, you need to still hold one thousand Bronze Marks at that moment. Marks used for transactions can’t get counted again."
Max nodded slowly. That meant he’d need to choose carefully between immediate benefits and long-term advancement.

The devil added, "But some cities and factions offer conversion services. They might let you exchange treasures for marks or marks for resources. The exchange rates usually run terrible, though. The stronger the mark, the more valuable it gets. A Gold Mark is worth far more than one thousand Bronze Marks in ordinary transactions, even though it takes one thousand Bronze Marks to condense one."
Max’s eyes flashed. "So the system pushes people to advance, but also tempts them to spend their marks before they can."

"That’s exactly how it works," the devil said bitterly. "The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage hands out opportunities, but it also forces people to make choices. Those who spend everything just to survive might stay at the bottom forever. Those who save everything might die before they ever get to use it."

Max fell silent. The rules ran cruel, but they weren’t chaotic. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage had built a clear path. Bronze. Gold. Sacred. Divine. Godslayer. Each step required an accumulation of one thousand marks from the level before it. The higher one climbed, the harder the journey got, but the rewards and authority grew accordingly too.

Freya had said marks were extremely important. Now Max understood why. They weren’t just currency. They were proof of achievement, a key to opportunities, a symbol of status, and maybe the only way to reach the deepest secrets of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
Max looked back at the devil. "Is there anything else I should know about marks?"
The devil hesitated. Max’s sword pressed slightly deeper. The hesitation disappeared immediately.

"There’s one more thing," the devil said hurriedly. "Marks are bound to the soul. They can’t normally get stolen through ordinary means. If someone kills a participant in a region where mark transfer is allowed, the rules of the Pilgrimage decide how many marks can transfer. But if the victim has hidden or sealed their marks, the killer might not get everything."
Max nodded. "And the mark on my wrist?"

"That’s your personal mark," the devil replied. "It records your current accumulation and grade. As you get more Bronze Marks, the symbol will gradually change. Once you reach one thousand Bronze Marks, it’ll transform into a Gold Mark if you choose to advance."

Max studied the bronze symbol again. A faint light moved across its surface. He could sense it connected to something vast and ancient, something existing beyond his understanding. It wasn’t simply counting his achievements. It was watching them.
Maybe the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was watching every participant. Maybe it was judging them. Or maybe it was just waiting to see who could climb high enough to reach the end.
Max pulled his gaze away from the mark and looked at the devil. "You’ve told me everything you know?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2037: Outer, Inner and Core!
paragraphs: The devil nodded rapidly. "Yes. I swear. I’ve told you everything."
Max stared at him for a moment. Then he pulled Dragonheart back.
The devil’s expression loosened with relief.
But before that relief could fully settle in, Max’s left hand rose. A blue void ring flashed across the air and entered the devil’s chest.
The devil froze. His eyes widened in terror. "You said..."
"I said you’d end up worse than them if you lied," Max replied calmly. "I never said I’d let you go."

The void ring tightened. The devil’s body collapsed to the ground, his cultivation sealed and his devil energy locked inside him. Max didn’t kill him right away. Instead, black flames rose from his palm and slowly wrapped around the two dead devils first, devouring their bodies, bloodline energy, and remaining devil power.
Then he looked down at the sealed devil. "I still need more information before reaching Bloodstone City."
The devil trembled on the ground.
Max’s expression stayed the same.
He looked down at the sealed devil beneath his feet and spoke in a calm voice. "Talk properly while you lead me to Bloodstone City, and your death will come quick."

The devil’s body trembled. He knew those words weren’t a threat meant to scare him. They were a plain statement. After watching two of his companions die in an instant, he no longer had the nerve to test Max’s patience. He nodded quickly and forced himself to stand, though his legs still felt weak from fear.
"Alright, alright," the devil said fast. "I’ll lead the way. I’ll tell you everything I know."

Max pulled the seal back slightly, leaving just enough power inside the devil’s body to keep him from escaping or using his devil energy recklessly. The devil clearly sensed it too. His face went even paler, but he didn’t dare complain. He turned toward the direction he’d pointed earlier and started leading Max across the pale yellow land.

As they traveled, the devil talked without waiting for Max to ask too many questions. At first his voice shook. But once he realized Max genuinely wanted information and wasn’t planning to kill him right away, he started explaining more carefully.
What he shared turned out useful. Some of it matched what Freya and Arvantos had already hinted at, while some of it gave Max a clearer picture of the place he’d just entered.
According to the devil, the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage split into three major regions.

The first region was the outer layer. This was where most newcomers landed when they entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage for the first time. It stretched vast and chaotic, filled with danger, but compared to the deeper regions, it still counted as the safest part of the pilgrimage.

New participants from all five universes usually got scattered across different areas of the outer layer. Some appeared near cities. Some appeared near wilderness. Some appeared near beast territories, ruined lands, abandoned trial grounds, or places where hunters like the three devils waited for fresh prey.

The outer layer was a place of adaptation. Newcomers learned the rules there. They learned about marks, cities, trials, dangers, factions, and the cruelty of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Those who adjusted quickly could gather marks and resources before pushing forward. Those who stayed naive usually turned into targets for beasts, traps, old participants, or geniuses from rival races.
The second region was the inner layer. The devil’s tone turned noticeably more serious when he brought it up.

The inner layer counted as the main region of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage and also the largest part of the entire place. Most famous trials, ancient ruins, inheritance grounds, bloodline pools, law comprehension zones, body tempering grounds, and mark exchange cities were said to sit there. Almost every genius who entered the pilgrimage dreamed of reaching the inner layer, since that’s where the real opportunities started showing up.

"The outer layer has opportunities too," the devil explained as he walked. "But most of them are small. Enough for weaker participants or newcomers, sure, but not enough for the real monsters. The inner layer’s different. That’s where the geniuses of the five races truly start competing."
Max listened quietly.

The devil continued, "If someone wants to make a name for themselves in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, they have to enter the inner layer. If they can’t even reach that place, then no matter how famous they were outside, people here just see them as ordinary."

The inner layer also drew the most attention from stronger participants because it was dangerous but still reachable. It wasn’t like the outer layer, where a lot of newcomers wandered around with no direction, and it wasn’t like the core layer, where only the most terrifying geniuses could even step inside.
The inner layer was the great battlefield of the pilgrimage, the place where most conflicts between the five races played out and where countless reputations got built or destroyed.
Then there was the third region. The core layer.
When the devil said those words, even his voice dropped instinctively.

The core layer was the most mysterious part of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Legend claimed it was the true center of the entire place, the region holding the deepest secrets and most ancient inheritances.

But unlike the outer and inner layers, the core layer wasn’t a place people could enter just because they wanted to. Only the strongest of the strongest geniuses had any real chance of getting inside.
The devil glanced back at Max nervously and said, "Legend says that since the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage first appeared, fewer than a hundred people have ever entered the core layer."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly. "Fewer than a hundred?"

That number was shockingly low. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage had existed since time immemorial. Nobody knew who’d created it, when it first appeared, or what purpose it truly served. Every time its gates opened, geniuses from all five universes poured in. The Primordial Universe, Devil Universe, Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe all sent their strongest young talents inside.

The number of participants wasn’t small. Each opening pulled in a massive wave of geniuses, and over countless eras, the total number of people who’d entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage should have reached an unimaginable scale. Yet out of all of them, fewer than a hundred had ever reached the core layer.
That made the core layer terrifyingly rare. It also made it unimaginably mysterious.

chapters.title: Chapter 2038: Bloodstone City!
paragraphs: Max’s interest deepened. "What’s inside the core layer?" he asked.
The devil hesitated for a moment, but when he felt the faint pressure of the seal inside his body tighten, he answered quickly.

"I don’t know the details. People like me aren’t qualified to know much about that place. But according to the rumors, the core layer holds the main inheritance left behind by the owner of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage."
Max’s gaze sharpened. The owner of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. That was the first time he’d heard this place might have an owner.

The devil continued, "Some say the owner was a god. Some say he was a godslayer. Some say he killed gods and built this place out of their corpses, laws, weapons, blood, and broken worlds. Others say the pilgrimage itself is a test left behind to find someone worthy of inheriting his path."
The devil swallowed before going on. "But nobody knows the truth. At least, nobody in the outer layer knows. Even in the inner layer, most people only know rumors."
Max’s eyes deepened.

A place beyond the Wall of Eternity. A pilgrimage connected to all five universes. A mark system even Primarchs couldn’t freely explain. An outer layer, an inner layer, and a core layer that fewer than a hundred people had entered since time immemorial. And now, a rumor that the core layer held the main inheritance of the mysterious owner of this entire place.
No matter how Max looked at it, the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage ran far more extraordinary than he’d first imagined.

The devil kept walking as he talked. "The core layer’s also said to be the real testing ground for the geniuses of the five races. The outer layer tests whether you can survive. The inner layer tests whether you can compete. But the core layer tests whether you’re truly qualified to stand above the geniuses of all five universes."
Max stayed silent. Those words carried weight. The core layer wasn’t just the deepest region. It was the place where the strongest geniuses of every race got measured against each other.

Maybe that explained why fewer than a hundred had entered it. Getting into the core layer likely demanded more than strength alone. It might require marks, achievements, talent, comprehension, bloodline, and recognition from the rules of the pilgrimage itself.
The devil glanced back and saw Max’s calm expression. For some reason, that calm scared him more than anger would have.

He quickly continued, "Bloodstone City’s only an outer layer city. It’s not one of the great cities, but it’s still a proper gathering point. You can buy information there, exchange marks, accept tasks, learn about nearby trials, and find out how to reach the stronger regions. Most newcomers who survive the first few days try to head there."
Max nodded slightly.
About an hour later, the silhouette of a city came into view. Seeing that, Max came to a stop, and so did the devil.
"What’s wrong?" the devil asked.
"Wait a minute," Max said, waving his right hand.

The void ring inside the devil flew out of his body, freeing him again, but before the devil could feel relieved, a different void ring entered his body. This time he didn’t feel his energy getting sealed or anything like that, but a strange feeling told him Max had done something worse than before.
"What did you do?" the devil asked, fear in his voice.
"I planted a slave seal on you," Max said calmly. "You’re under my control now. If I want you dead, you’ll die. So watch what you say once we reach Bloodstone City, and follow my lead."
"What?" The devil looked shocked. He hadn’t expected Max to go this far.
"Do you understand or not?" Max asked in an authoritative tone.
"I understand, I understand!" The devil nodded his head fast.
"Good." Max smiled. He hadn’t expected the many techniques and uses hidden inside the Voidwalker Inheritance’s void rings to come in handy like this, but he wasn’t complaining at all.
"Now let’s head into the city," Max said, smiling. "You go ahead and keep some distance from me. It’d look too suspicious if a devil and a Primordial showed up together."
He added, "I’ll call you when I need you. And if you have anything to say to me, just talk to yourself and I will know. Now move."
The devil nodded and flew off toward Bloodstone City.
Max followed after him slowly.
The journey wasn’t long, but it wasn’t peaceful either. Along the way, Max saw traces of many battles scattered across the pale yellow land.

Claw marks were carved deep into the ground, broken weapons lay half-buried beneath the dust, dried blood stains hadn’t faded even under the strange sunlight, and faint remnants of laws still lingered in the air like invisible wounds.

In several spots, Max sensed the aura of beasts far stronger than the six-headed wolf he’d killed earlier, but those beasts kept their distance, probably because the path they were walking was one commonly used by people heading toward the city.
After a while, the outline of Bloodstone City finally appeared in the distance.

At first it looked like a dark red mountain rising from the pale yellow earth. But as they got closer, Max realized it wasn’t a mountain at all. It was a massive city built from crimson stone, black metal, and ancient bones.
Its walls stood tall and thick, and every stone seemed soaked in blood from countless years. Strange symbols were carved across the walls, and several large gates stood open beneath towering arches.
Above the gates, a blood-red crystal floated silently, casting a faint light that swept over everyone who entered.
The devil walking ahead of Max slowed his steps on instinct.

"This is Bloodstone City," he said in a low voice. "It’s one of the outer layer cities. Not the safest place, but open killing inside the city is forbidden unless both sides agree to a duel or the city rules allow it. That’s why a lot of newcomers try to reach this place first."
Max glanced at him. "Forbidden by who?"
The devil swallowed. "By the city rules."
Max’s eyes moved slightly. "And who enforces those rules?"
The devil hesitated for a moment before answering. "The city itself."

Max didn’t ask any further, but his interest deepened. A city that enforced its own rules. That alone told him Bloodstone City wasn’t just a settlement built by cultivators. It was part of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage system, or at least deeply tied to it.
