chapters.title: Chapter 2039: People From All Races!
paragraphs: They approached the gate. The blood-red crystal above the entrance released a beam of light that swept over Max. The bronze mark on his wrist warmed slightly, and then the pressure disappeared.

No one stopped him. No guard questioned him. No fee got demanded. The devil beside him passed through the gate too, though his face stayed pale since the seal Max had placed inside his body was still there.

The moment Max stepped into Bloodstone City, his gaze sharpened. The city turned out far livelier than he expected. Wide streets stretched in several directions, paved with dark red stone that gave off a faint heat.
Tall buildings rose on both sides, some shaped like towers, some like fortresses, some like ancient temples converted into shops, halls, or resting places.

Strange signs floated in the air, glowing in different colors. Some displayed words related to mark exchange. Some advertised information halls. Some belonged to weapon stores, beast material shops, cultivation chambers, healing pavilions, and trial registration halls.
The most striking thing wasn’t the city itself. It was the people. For the first time since entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, Max saw beings from all five races gathered in the same place.
Primordials walked through the streets with calm, proud expressions. Their auras came off stable, deep, and naturally close to the laws around them.

Some had faint golden patterns on their skin. Some carried ancient weapons on their backs. Some moved in groups, while others walked alone with the confidence of people who didn’t fear being challenged.
Devils were around too. Their dark skin, horns, crimson tattoos, and savage auras made them easy to spot. Some stood huge and muscular, while others looked lean and cruel.

Their eyes often carried violence, and plenty of them didn’t bother hiding their hostility toward members of the Primordial Universe. Still, despite their sneers and cold stares, none of them attacked openly.

Then Max saw the Spirit Race for the first time. They took humanoid form, but there was an otherworldly quality to how they looked. Their skin carried faint natural colors, like pale green, soft blue, moon-white, and light gold.

Some had hair that flowed like water, while others had hair resembling leaves, silver grass, or strands of soft light. Their eyes glowed clear and luminous, and their bodies seemed to breathe with the energy around them.

Unlike the devils, who gave off oppressive and brutal auras, the Spirit Race gave Max the feeling of living law and natural harmony. Some had small vines coiling around their wrists. Some had faint elemental halos behind them. Some walked barefoot across the stone streets, yet dust never seemed to touch their feet.
Max’s gaze paused on them for a moment. "So those are true spirits in humanoid form," he muttered inwardly.

They were different from elves, different from humans, and different from Primordials. Their existence felt closer to nature itself, as if they’d been born from the breath of the world rather than from flesh alone.

Not far off, Max also spotted members of the Angel Race. Their appearances reminded him strongly of elves. Most stood tall, elegant, and almost impossibly beautiful. Their features looked refined, their skin fair, their hair coming in shades of silver, gold, white, and pale blue. Some had pointed ears, and their eyes carried a calm but distant pride.

Unlike ordinary elves, though, each of them had a golden halo floating above their head. Some halos were simple rings of light, while others were layered with runes, feathers, or sword-like patterns. Their auras came off pure, bright, and filled with a kind of holy order that made the surrounding space feel cleaner wherever they walked.
The sight sent Max’s thoughts drifting. He remembered Planet Orion. He remembered Kazreth. That mysterious being had carried an aura similar to the Angel Race, but far stronger and more oppressive.

Back then, Max had guessed Kazreth might be the leader of the Angel Race, or at least someone standing extremely high in their hierarchy. Now, after seeing these angels in Bloodstone City, that feeling only grew stronger.
The angels here carried real power. But compared to the memory of Kazreth, they felt like sparks before a sun.
Max pulled his gaze away and kept looking around. Soon he spotted members of the Dragon Race. They also took humanoid form, but they looked very different from Max’s own dragon transformation.

Max’s dragon power usually showed up when he activated his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline or transformed parts of his body. These Dragon Race members, though, carried dragon traits naturally even while holding humanoid shape.

Scales covered parts of their bodies like armor. Some had scales across their arms and shoulders. Some had scales running along their necks and faces. Some had long tails, sharp claws, or horns curving backward from their heads.
Their pupils looked narrow and beast-like, and their physical auras felt dense, heavy, and full of overwhelming vitality.

Some of them looked toward Max as he passed. Their gazes lingered on him for a moment, as if sensing the dragon aura hidden inside his body. But since Max didn’t openly reveal his Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, they only looked at him with mild curiosity before turning away.
Max quietly took it all in. He’d expected trouble the moment he entered Bloodstone City.

After all, outside the city, three devils had been guarding a newbie spawning area just to rob and kill fresh arrivals. He’d figured a city packed with geniuses from all five races would be even more chaotic. He’d expected sneers, provocations, challenges, and maybe even immediate attacks.
But to his surprise, Bloodstone City felt fairly peaceful. Not friendly. Not gentle. But peaceful in its own cold way.

Everyone seemed caught up in their own business. Some hurried toward mark exchange halls. Some gathered near information boards. Some entered weapon shops or healing pavilions. Some sat in open courtyards negotiating trades.

Some stood outside large halls, forming temporary teams for nearby trials. The air carried tension, but it was controlled tension, like blades kept inside sheaths. Everyone here might be dangerous, but nobody drew their weapon without a reason.

He’d expected sneers, provocations, challenges, and maybe even immediate attacks.
But to his surprise, Bloodstone City felt fairly peaceful.
Not friendly.
Not gentle.
But peaceful in its own cold way.
Everyone seemed caught up in their own business.
Some hurried toward mark exchange halls.
Some gathered near information boards.
Some entered weapon shops or healing pavilions.
Some sat in open courtyards negotiating trades.
Some stood outside large halls, forming temporary teams for nearby trials.
The air carried tension, but it was controlled tension, like blades kept inside sheaths.
Everyone here might be dangerous, but nobody drew their weapon without a reason.

chapters.title: Chapter 2040: Being an Anomaly!
paragraphs: The devil beside Max whispered, "Open killing’s forbidden here. That’s why the city looks calm. Outside the walls, it’s different."
Max gave him a brief glance. "I can tell."
As Max walked deeper into the street, plenty of people noticed him. The Primordials reacted first. Several of them looked at Max and immediately sensed his cultivation realm.

When they realized he was only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm, strange expressions crossed their faces. Some looked surprised. Some frowned slightly. Some seemed puzzled about how someone at his level had even entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.

But once they sensed the Primordial aura in his body, most of them didn’t show any contempt. Instead, they nodded to him. It wasn’t a warm greeting, but it counted as recognition. Maybe they assumed he had some unusual background.

Maybe they figured anyone who could enter this place despite such low cultivation couldn’t be completely ordinary. Or maybe it was simply because he carried Primordial Bloodline, and in a city where all five races gathered, people from the same universe naturally kept up at least a surface-level courtesy toward each other.
The devils reacted very differently. Plenty of them sneered when they saw Max.
"A Law Manifestation Realm Primordial?"
"He came here to die?"
"Maybe some old monster threw him in for tempering. If he leaves the city, he won’t last long."
Their voices weren’t loud, but Max heard them clearly. He ignored them. If he reacted to every sneer, he’d waste too much time.

Besides, the three devils outside the city had sat at the 2nd level of the Divine Lord Realm, and two of them were already dead. If the devils here wanted to underestimate him because of his cultivation, that was their problem.
Max’s calm reaction made some of the nearby Primordials glance at him again. A few of them looked slightly impressed.

The devil leading Max grew more nervous the deeper they went into the city. He clearly didn’t want to be seen walking with a Primordial, especially with a hidden seal still controlling his body. But Max didn’t care about his discomfort.
"Where’s the information hall?" Max asked.

The devil discretely pointed toward a tall building ahead. "That one. The black tower with the bronze mark symbol above the entrance. Most newcomers head there first to buy basic information about the outer layer, nearby trials, mark rules, and routes toward the inner layer."

Max followed his gaze. A tall black tower stood at the end of the street. Above its entrance floated a large bronze circle with a sword in the middle, the same shape as the mark on Max’s wrist. Plenty of participants were entering and leaving the tower, most of them wearing serious expressions.
However, before Max could enter the information hall, several Primordials stepped into his path.

They didn’t look hostile, but their movements came off firm. There were three of them, each carrying a stable Primordial aura that felt far more natural than the newly awakened bloodline aura Max had seen among the ten geniuses chosen from the Cosmic Ascension Conference.
Their expressions stayed calm, their gazes lingering on Max’s face, cultivation, and wrist mark for a brief moment before one of them spoke.
"Follow us."
After saying that, the Primordial turned and walked toward a quieter street without waiting for Max’s reply.

Max frowned slightly. He didn’t like being ordered around, especially in a place like Bloodstone City, where every race had its own agenda and every friendly face might hide another motive. But these people were Primordials, and their behavior didn’t carry obvious malice.
Since he’d just arrived in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage and still knew very little about this place, it seemed better to see what they wanted before making any judgment.
Max glanced at the sealed devil beside him. "You go ahead and wait for me at the information hall."

The devil’s expression shifted slightly, but he quickly lowered his head. He didn’t dare ask whether this meant he could escape. The seal inside his body was still there, and Max could crush him the moment he tried anything foolish.
"I understand," the devil said quickly.
Max then followed the Primordials.

They led him away from the busy main street and into another part of Bloodstone City. The surroundings changed gradually. The crowded shops, loud exchanges, and mixed auras of the five races grew less dense.

The streets here were wider and cleaner, and the buildings carried fewer chaotic signs. Instead, most of them were built with a solemn, ancient style, as if they belonged not to merchants or wandering participants, but to factions that had occupied this city for a long time.

Soon, Max arrived in front of a large mansion-like building. The mansion was built from pale gold stone and dark red crystal, standing out clearly against the blood-colored structures surrounding it in Bloodstone City.

Its entrance was guarded by two tall Primordials, and above the gate floated a circular emblem giving off a calm golden glow. The symbol wasn’t exactly the same as the bronze mark on Max’s wrist, but it carried the same ancient feeling of recognition and authority.

Many Primordials could be seen entering and leaving the mansion. To Max’s surprise, there were also humans among them. Some of those humans wore battle robes, some carried swords, and some had auras clearly not inferior to the Primordials walking beside them.

This immediately told Max the building wasn’t purely a base of the Primordial Race. It was more likely the headquarters of their universe in Bloodstone City, a place where participants from the Primordial Universe could gather, exchange information, and get basic protection.
Max’s eyes moved slightly. ’So every race has a base here.’

That made sense. Bloodstone City might stay peaceful under the city rules, but the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage itself was still a place where the five races competed fiercely. In a place like this, each race naturally needed a foothold, especially in the outer layer where newcomers kept showing up constantly.

chapters.title: Chapter 2041: Anna!
paragraphs: The Primordials led him through the entrance. The moment Max entered the mansion, a female Primordial walked toward him with a polite smile.

She looked young, though Max knew age could be deceiving in a place like this. Her hair was pale gold, her eyes clear and bright, and faint primordial patterns flowed across her skin like thin streams of light.
Her aura felt gentle, but not weak. Compared to the cold tension outside, she gave off a steadier and more welcoming presence.
"Hello," she said. "You must be new to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. My name is Anna."
Max nodded slightly. "I am new. Arrived not long ago."
Anna looked at him carefully. "And your name?"
"Max Voidwalker."
The moment he said his name, Anna’s brows moved slightly.
"Max Voidwalker."

She seemed to find the surname strange, or maybe familiar in a way she couldn’t immediately place. But she didn’t ask about it. After only a brief pause, her gaze shifted to his cultivation, and her expression turned more concerned.
"How were you allowed to enter the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage with this level of cultivation?"
Max shrugged slightly. He truly didn’t know how to answer that.

Anna sighed and pressed her fingers against her forehead, like she’d suddenly gotten a headache. "How did the elders, even the Primarchs, agree to send someone at the Law Manifestation Realm into this place?"
Max stayed silent.
Anna looked at him for another moment, then shook her head. "Anyway, since you’re already here, there are a few things you need to know."

Her tone turned more serious. "Bloodstone City is only one of many cities in the outer layer. Every major outer-layer city has bases belonging to the five races, so you’ll find people from the Primordial Universe, Devil Universe, Spirit Universe, Angel Universe, and Dragon Universe scattered throughout the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Some cities are more balanced. Some are dominated by one race. Some are technically neutral, but everyone knows which faction actually holds the most influence there."
Max listened quietly.
Anna pointed toward his wrist. "I’m guessing you already know something about the marks?"
Max glanced at the bronze symbol on his skin. "I’ve heard some information."
"That’s good," Anna said. "At least you’re not completely blind."
Then her expression turned stern. "But do you understand how dangerous this place is for someone like you?"
Max looked at her without answering.

Anna continued, "You’re at the Law Manifestation Realm. Out in the wider world, that might already be enough to make countless cultivators admire you, especially with high talent. But in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, this cultivation is dangerously low. The outer layer is packed with Divine Lord Realm geniuses. A lot of them have been here for years, and some have survived countless battles, trials, ambushes, and beast territories."

Her voice grew heavier. "The inner layer is even worse. That place is full of Divine King Realm geniuses. The strongest among them are monsters who can fight across realms, crush ordinary Divine Kings, and compete for opportunities people in the outer layer can only dream about."
Max’s eyes narrowed slightly.

Anna looked at him directly. "With your current cultivation, almost everyone who sees you will assume you’re easy prey. Devils will target you. Dragon Race members might challenge you. Angel Race cultivators might dismiss you outright. Even people from our own universe might wonder if you’re carrying some special treasure that let you in despite being so weak in cultivation."
She sighed again. "Honestly, I’m surprised you made it from the spawning area to Bloodstone City in one piece."
Max ignored that last part, but Anna’s words gave him a much clearer picture of the overall power level in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
The outer layer was dominated by Divine Lord Realm geniuses. The inner layer was dominated by Divine King Realm geniuses. And he was only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm.

No wonder so many people had looked at him strangely when he entered Bloodstone City. From their perspective, his presence here was abnormal. Even among top geniuses, entering this place at his realm had to be extremely rare.
After a moment, Max asked, "How long have you been here?"
Anna smiled faintly. "Around three years, I think."
"Three years?" Max’s eyes showed a trace of surprise. "And you still haven’t entered the inner layer?"
Anna stared at him for a moment. Then she laughed softly, not mockingly, but like his question was something only a true newcomer would ask.
"You really think entering the inner layer is that easy?"
Max didn’t answer.

Anna shook her head and said, "I won’t get into every detail right now, but you should understand one thing. Out of every thousand participants in the outer layer, maybe only ten have a real shot at entering the inner layer."
Max’s expression finally changed. "Only ten out of a thousand?"

Anna nodded. "That’s already a generous estimate. Plenty of people spend years here and still fail to meet the conditions. Some die trying. Some give up and stay in the outer layer, using their marks just for survival and cultivation resources. Some keep taking on trials until their foundations collapse or their luck runs out."

Max’s gaze deepened. Only around one percent had a real chance. That number reshaped his understanding of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage all over again. He’d already known the inner layer wouldn’t be easy to enter, but he hadn’t expected the gap to run this severe.

The outer layer wasn’t simply a beginner region everyone eventually moved past. It was a filtering ground. It swallowed the weak, trapped the ordinary, and let only a tiny number of truly capable geniuses pass through.
Anna looked at him seriously. "That’s why I said you need to be careful. Surviving the outer layer’s already hard. Leaving it is much harder."
Max stayed silent for a moment. Then he looked toward the deeper part of the mansion. "I understand."
His voice came out calm, but his eyes had sharpened.
The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was far more dangerous than he’d expected.
Max thought for a moment before asking, "Has anyone else from my batch arrived in this city?"
Anna looked at him. "You mean the new Primordials who entered with you?"
Max nodded. "Yes."
"There are two," Anna replied. "One’s from the Sword God Palace. His name’s Damian. The other’s Miss Revona."
Max’s eyes moved slightly. Damian and Revona had also landed near Bloodstone City.

"As for the rest," Anna continued, "they must’ve shown up near other cities in the outer layer. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage doesn’t send everyone to the same place. Even people who enter through the same entrance can end up scattered across different regions."

chapters.title: Chapter 2042: Anna’s Plan!
paragraphs: Max nodded with understanding. That matched what he’d already guessed. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was too vast, and the entry process seemed to follow its own rules. It was already lucky that Damian and Revona had ended up in the same city as him.
He glanced around the mansion and asked, "So this place is the base for Primordials and humans from our universe?"

Anna nodded. "Yes. More precisely, this is the Bloodstone City base for participants from the Primordial Universe. Primordials, humans, and a few other races connected to our side can come here for help. If you need information, temporary lodging, basic supplies, introductions, or guidance, you can come here. As long as the request isn’t too outrageous, most people here will be willing to help."
"I see," Max said.
At least now he had a proper foothold in Bloodstone City. That beat wandering around blindly and relying on a terrified devil for every scrap of information.
After thinking it over, Max turned toward the entrance. "Then I’ll go to the information hall of Bloodstone City now."
He’d barely taken a step when Anna suddenly reached out from behind, grabbed his collar, and pulled him back.
Max nearly stumbled.
"Where the hell are you going?" Anna asked, her earlier polite smile gone in an instant.
Max turned his head and looked at her with a wry smile. "To the information hall."
"I heard you the first time," Anna said, her expression turning solemn. "But do you understand what’ll happen if you go there openly?"
Max didn’t answer right away.

Anna pointed at him and continued, "You’re only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm. The moment you step into the information hall, plenty of people will notice you. That place isn’t like this base. Participants from all five races go there. Information brokers, scouts, hunters, faction members, and people looking for easy prey all keep their eyes on newcomers. Once word gets out that a Law Manifestation Realm Primordial has entered Bloodstone City, your existence will spread fast."
Her tone grew heavier. "And when that happens, you’ll be as good as dead."
Max looked at her calmly. "I have to go there, Anna."
Anna frowned. "Why?"

"I’m new here," Max replied. "I need to understand the situation in Bloodstone City, the outer layer, the nearby trials, the mark system, and the route toward the inner layer. I heard the information hall’s the best place for newcomers to learn the basics."
"That’s true," Anna admitted.

She let go of his collar, but her expression stayed tense. She looked at Max for a moment, then fell into thought. Her brows furrowed slightly, and her fingers tapped against her arm, as if she were quickly weighing a few options. A few breaths later, her eyes lit up.
Then she clapped her hands once. "I think I’ve got a plan."
Max raised a brow. "A plan?"
Anna pointed at him with a serious face. "You. Stay here."
Max blinked.

"Don’t move," Anna continued. "Don’t wander outside. Don’t go to the information hall on your own. Don’t let some devil, dragon, angel, spirit, or even a bored Primordial drag you into trouble. I’ll be right back."
Max raised both hands slightly. "I’m not going anywhere."
"Good," Anna said.
Without another word, she turned and vanished deeper into the mansion.
Max watched her leave, then shook his head with a faint smile. ’Wonder what kind of plan she’s got.’
Since Anna had clearly told him to wait, Max didn’t try to leave. Instead, he started wandering slowly through the main hall of the mansion.

The interior turned out much bigger than it looked from outside. The hall stretched wide and bright, with pillars made of pale gold stone supporting a high ceiling engraved with faint primordial runes.

Several counters lined the sides, where participants talked with attendants about missions, marks, injuries, lodging, and information. A few groups sat around stone tables, quietly going over maps and routes. Others stood near floating screens displaying notices about nearby trials, dangerous zones, recent deaths, and faction movements.
Max took it all in carefully. Most of the people inside were Primordials, but there were also quite a few humans. Unlike the nervous newcomers outside, the participants here looked more experienced.
Their auras stayed stable, and their eyes carried the caution of people who’d survived the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage long enough to understand its cruelty.
Max silently checked their cultivation levels. The result wasn’t surprising, but it still gave him something to think about.

Most of the participants here sat at the 8th, 9th, or 10th level of the Divine Lord Realm. A smaller number sat at the middle levels of the Divine Lord Realm. As for those at the early levels, Max only spotted a few.
Law Manifestation Realm cultivators were almost nonexistent.
That alone explained Anna’s reaction. In this place, his cultivation realm wasn’t merely low. It was abnormal.

Even Anna herself had reached the 10th level of the Divine Lord Realm. Her aura had felt gentle when she greeted him, but thinking it over now, she was actually one of the stronger participants in this base. If she’d still stayed in the outer layer after three years at that cultivation, entering the inner layer clearly ran far harder than he’d imagined.
’Looks like all of them have spent a good number of years in the outer layer,’ Max thought.

That was the only reasonable explanation. These people hadn’t entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage yesterday. They’d survived, fought, cultivated, gathered marks, and slowly pushed themselves toward the peak of the Divine Lord Realm. Yet even then, most of them hadn’t made it into the inner layer.
The outer layer wasn’t a beginner area in any simple sense. It was a cruel filter. Only those strong enough, cautious enough, and lucky enough could even dream of moving forward.

As Max kept observing the hall, several Primordials and humans noticed him too. Their reactions all played out nearly the same way. First, they sensed the Primordial aura on him. Then they sensed his cultivation.

After that, their expressions turned strange. Some looked confused. Some frowned. Some whispered to their companions. A few nodded politely once they realized he belonged to their side, but even they couldn’t hide the doubt in their eyes. Clearly, they were all wondering the same thing.
How had someone at the Law Manifestation Realm gotten into the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage?
Max ignored their stares. He’d already gotten used to this kind of reaction. In the Divine Realm, people had underestimated him because of his age, background, realm, or lack of reputation.
Here, they’d underestimate him because his cultivation sat far below the common standard of the outer layer. That was fine. Sometimes being underestimated worked out better than being feared.
Still, Anna was right about one thing. If too many people learned about him too fast, trouble would come.

That matched what he’d already guessed.
The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was too vast, and the entry process seemed to follow its own rules.
It was already lucky that Damian and Revona had ended up in the same city as him.
He glanced around the mansion and asked, "So this place is the base for Primordials and humans from our universe?"
Anna nodded.
"Yes.
More precisely, this is the Bloodstone City base for participants from the Primordial Universe.
Primordials, humans, and a few other races connected to our side can come here for help.
If you need information, temporary lodging, basic supplies, introductions, or guidance, you can come here.
As long as the request isn’t too outrageous, most people here will be willing to help."
"I see," Max said.
At least now he had a proper foothold in Bloodstone City.
That beat wandering around blindly and relying on a terrified devil for every scrap of information.
After thinking it over, Max turned toward the entrance.
"Then I’ll go to the information hall of Bloodstone City now."
He’d barely taken a step when Anna suddenly reached out from behind, grabbed his collar, and pulled him back.
Max nearly stumbled.
"Where the hell are you going?" Anna asked, her earlier polite smile gone in an instant.
Max turned his head and looked at her with a wry smile.
"To the information hall."
"I heard you the first time," Anna said, her expression turning solemn.
"But do you understand what’ll happen if you go there openly?"
Max didn’t answer right away.
Anna pointed at him and continued, "You’re only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm.
The moment you step into the information hall, plenty of people will notice you.
That place isn’t like this base.
Participants from all five races go there.
Information brokers, scouts, hunters, faction members, and people looking for easy prey all keep their eyes on newcomers.
Once word gets out that a Law Manifestation Realm Primordial has entered Bloodstone City, your existence will spread fast."
Her tone grew heavier.
"And when that happens, you’ll be as good as dead."
Max looked at her calmly.
"I have to go there, Anna."
Anna frowned.
"Why?"
"I’m new here," Max replied.
"I need to understand the situation in Bloodstone City, the outer layer, the nearby trials, the mark system, and the route toward the inner layer.
I heard the information hall’s the best place for newcomers to learn the basics."
"That’s true," Anna admitted.
She let go of his collar, but her expression stayed tense.
She looked at Max for a moment, then fell into thought.
Her brows furrowed slightly, and her fingers tapped against her arm, as if she were quickly weighing a few options.
A few breaths later, her eyes lit up.
Then she clapped her hands once.
"I think I’ve got a plan."
Max raised a brow.
"A plan?"
Anna pointed at him with a serious face.
"You.
Stay here."
Max blinked.
"Don’t move," Anna continued.
"Don’t wander outside.
Don’t go to the information hall on your own.
Don’t let some devil, dragon, angel, spirit, or even a bored Primordial drag you into trouble.
I’ll be right back."
Max raised both hands slightly.
"I’m not going anywhere."
"Good," Anna said.
Without another word, she turned and vanished deeper into the mansion.
Max watched her leave, then shook his head with a faint smile. ’Wonder what kind of plan she’s got.’
Since Anna had clearly told him to wait, Max didn’t try to leave.
Instead, he started wandering slowly through the main hall of the mansion.
The interior turned out much bigger than it looked from outside.
The hall stretched wide and bright, with pillars made of pale gold stone supporting a high ceiling engraved with faint primordial runes.
Several counters lined the sides, where participants talked with attendants about missions, marks, injuries, lodging, and information.
A few groups sat around stone tables, quietly going over maps and routes.
Others stood near floating screens displaying notices about nearby trials, dangerous zones, recent deaths, and faction movements.
Max took it all in carefully.
Most of the people inside were Primordials, but there were also quite a few humans.
Unlike the nervous newcomers outside, the participants here looked more experienced.
Their auras stayed stable, and their eyes carried the caution of people who’d survived the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage long enough to understand its cruelty.
Max silently checked their cultivation levels.
The result wasn’t surprising, but it still gave him something to think about.
Most of the participants here sat at the 8th, 9th, or 10th level of the Divine Lord Realm.
A smaller number sat at the middle levels of the Divine Lord Realm.
As for those at the early levels, Max only spotted a few.
Law Manifestation Realm cultivators were almost nonexistent.
That alone explained Anna’s reaction.
In this place, his cultivation realm wasn’t merely low.
It was abnormal.
Even Anna herself had reached the 10th level of the Divine Lord Realm.
Her aura had felt gentle when she greeted him, but thinking it over now, she was actually one of the stronger participants in this base.
If she’d still stayed in the outer layer after three years at that cultivation, entering the inner layer clearly ran far harder than he’d imagined.
’Looks like all of them have spent a good number of years in the outer layer,’ Max thought.
That was the only reasonable explanation.
These people hadn’t entered the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage yesterday.
They’d survived, fought, cultivated, gathered marks, and slowly pushed themselves toward the peak of the Divine Lord Realm.
Yet even then, most of them hadn’t made it into the inner layer.
The outer layer wasn’t a beginner area in any simple sense.
It was a cruel filter.
Only those strong enough, cautious enough, and lucky enough could even dream of moving forward.
As Max kept observing the hall, several Primordials and humans noticed him too.
Their reactions all played out nearly the same way.
First, they sensed the Primordial aura on him.
Then they sensed his cultivation.
After that, their expressions turned strange.
Some looked confused.
Some frowned.
Some whispered to their companions.
A few nodded politely once they realized he belonged to their side, but even they couldn’t hide the doubt in their eyes.
Clearly, they were all wondering the same thing.
How had someone at the Law Manifestation Realm gotten into the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage?
Max ignored their stares.
He’d already gotten used to this kind of reaction.
In the Divine Realm, people had underestimated him because of his age, background, realm, or lack of reputation.
Here, they’d underestimate him because his cultivation sat far below the common standard of the outer layer.
That was fine.
Sometimes being underestimated worked out better than being feared.
Still, Anna was right about one thing.
If too many people learned about him too fast, trouble would come.

chapters.title: Chapter 2043: Daniel!
paragraphs: As Max kept observing the mansion, Anna finally returned. This time, she wasn’t alone. Two familiar figures walked beside her.
Damian and Revona.
The moment Damian saw Max, a faint smile crossed his face. "Max, you’re here too."
His expression made it clear he’d thought only he and Revona had made it to Bloodstone City. Seeing Max here was a pleasant surprise.
Max smiled lightly too. "Damian, Revona. Looks like the three of us are the only ones from our batch who landed near Bloodstone City."

Revona nodded. "That’s probably the case. Bloodstone City isn’t far from one of the nearby spawning points. Anyone who appeared around that region should’ve reached the city by now, if they survived the journey. Since we haven’t heard anything about the others, they most likely landed near different cities in the outer layer."
Damian nodded along. "That makes sense. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage is way too big to gather everyone in one place."

Max wasn’t surprised by any of this. Arvantos had already warned them they might get separated after entering, but running into two familiar faces this soon still felt reassuring. In a place like this, even a familiar rival beat complete strangers.
Anna clapped her hands lightly, pulling their attention back to her. "Now, let’s head to the Information Hall."

She looked at Max with a half-serious, half-helpless expression. "Since you insist on going, you should at least go with people you know. Damian and Miss Revona haven’t visited the Information Hall either, so the three of you can go together."
Max had no objection. "Then let’s go," he said.
Anna nodded, but instead of leaving right away, she looked around the mansion like she was searching for someone. "We’re still missing one more person. Let’s wait for him."
Max raised a brow. "Who?"
Damian and Revona looked curious too.
"Daniel," Anna said lightly.

Max stayed calm, since the name meant nothing to him. But Damian and Revona reacted differently. Their eyes moved slightly, and they exchanged faint looks of surprise. Max had just arrived in Bloodstone City and knew almost nothing about the important figures here, but Damian and Revona had already spent some time deeper inside the mansion. Because of that, they’d already heard a fair bit about Daniel.

Daniel counted as one of the three strongest Primordials currently stationed in Bloodstone City. He’d defeated many geniuses from the other four races and built up a powerful reputation in the outer layer.

There was even a rumor that he’d once fought two top geniuses from the Angel Race and Dragon Race at the same time without losing. Whether that rumor was fully true or not, the fact that people still talked about it said a lot about how formidable he was.

But what really made Daniel famous was his spot on the Bloodstone City Rankings. He sat at seventh. That meant he counted as one of the strongest young experts in the entire city, not just among Primordials but across all five races gathered here.
Damian and Revona couldn’t quite figure out how Anna had managed to call someone like him over just to walk three newcomers to the Information Hall.

Just as they were wondering about it, another Primordial walked toward them. He stood tall, around six feet, with a lean but powerful build. His hair was dark red, and his eyes carried a relaxed confidence that didn’t feel forced. Unlike a lot of geniuses who deliberately let their aura show to prove strength, Daniel’s presence stayed restrained.
That restraint made him feel even more dangerous, like the power inside him had been tempered through years of real battles.
"Hey, Anna," Daniel said casually. His gaze moved across Max, Damian, and Revona. "These the three newbies?"
Anna nodded with a smile. "Yeah. I’m taking them to the Information Hall, so I figured I’d bring you along."
Daniel stared at her for a moment. For a rare instant, his expression went speechless. "No need for me to tag along if you’re the one taking them there," he said helplessly.
Anna pointed at Max without hesitation. "Look at him."
Daniel followed her finger and looked at Max.

Anna continued seriously, "He’s only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm, and yet he walked into Bloodstone City openly. Now he wants to walk into the Information Hall, where people from all five races gather to buy and sell news. If some arrogant fools from the other races notice him, they might start something just to test him."
Max looked at Anna with a faintly helpless expression.
She ignored him and kept going. "That’s why I want you with us. You’ll act as a deterrent."
Daniel smiled wryly. Others might not know it, but he knew Anna wasn’t weak either. With her around, ordinary troublemakers would already think twice. Still, he understood her concern.

A Law Manifestation Realm newcomer walking into the Information Hall would definitely draw attention. Even with open killing forbidden inside the city, provocation, schemes, challenges, and targeted information leaks were still very much on the table.
Since he wasn’t busy, Daniel didn’t refuse. "Fine," he said with a light smile. "Let’s go."
Anna nodded, satisfied.
With that, the group left the mansion and headed toward the Information Hall. As they walked, Anna introduced Daniel to the three of them and introduced Max, Damian, and Revona to Daniel in return.
Daniel didn’t act arrogant despite his ranking. He greeted Damian and Revona politely, and when his gaze landed on Max, curiosity showed in his eyes, but no contempt.
"So you’re the Law Manifestation Realm newcomer everyone’s about to start talking about," Daniel said with a faint smile.
Max glanced at him. "That doesn’t sound like a good thing."

"It’s not," Daniel replied honestly. "But it’s not necessarily bad either. In the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, attention can bring danger, but it can also bring opportunities. The real question is whether you’ve got the strength to control what kind of attention sticks around you."
Max nodded slightly. That answer felt practical.

The group soon reached the black tower Max had spotted earlier. The Information Hall stood at the end of the wide street, taller than most surrounding buildings and far more crowded. Its walls were made of dark stone that seemed to soak up light, and countless glowing inscriptions moved across its surface like living words.

Above the entrance floated a large bronze symbol shaped like a circle with a sword at its center, almost identical to the mark on Max’s wrist. Around that symbol, smaller lights flickered constantly, each one carrying fragments of information, announcements, rankings, warnings, and transaction notices.

chapters.title: Chapter 2044: Infor for Newbies!
paragraphs: Participants from all five races moved in and out of the hall. Primordials walked in with calm expressions. Devils strode out sneering at something they’d just heard. Spirit Race members gathered near the entrance, quietly exchanging information through glowing leaves of energy.

Angels stood in small groups, their golden halos casting gentle light over their elegant figures. Dragon Race geniuses leaned against the stone pillars outside, their scaled arms folded across their chests as they watched the crowd with beast-like patience.

The moment Max approached with Anna, Daniel, Damian, and Revona, several gazes turned toward them. Some recognized Anna. More recognized Daniel. Because Daniel stood there, the gazes landing on Max didn’t linger too recklessly.
A few devils noticed his cultivation and flashed mocking smiles, but after spotting Daniel walking beside him, they quickly looked away. Even the curious ones didn’t step forward to provoke him.
Anna glanced at Max. "See? This is why I brought him."
Max smiled faintly and said nothing.
They entered the Information Hall together. The moment they stepped inside, Max felt like he’d entered a completely different world.
The interior stretched vast, far larger than the tower looked from outside. It had clearly been expanded through spatial formations.

Floors rose in layers above them, connected by floating stairways and circular platforms drifting through the air. Countless information screens hovered everywhere, displaying maps, city notices, mark exchange rates, trial locations, beast warnings, faction disputes, recent deaths, ranking changes, and basic guides for newcomers.

The hall was noisy but organized. Voices filled the air from every direction. Some people were buying maps. Some were arguing with information brokers. Some were checking the rankings. Some were digging through trial records.

Some gathered around large floating boards discussing newly discovered ruins and dangerous zones. Despite the crowd, the atmosphere stayed controlled, like the rules of Bloodstone City reached deep into this place too.
Max looked around carefully. This was exactly what he needed.

Anna noticed his expression and started explaining. "The Information Hall’s one of the most important places for newcomers. Almost every proper city in the outer layer has one. Some run bigger than this, some smaller, and some get controlled more heavily by certain races, but their function stays mostly the same."

She pointed toward the floating screens. "Here, you can learn the basic rules of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. You can buy maps of nearby regions, gather information about trial grounds, learn which beast territories to avoid, check mark-related rules, see rankings, purchase news about the inner layer, and even hire guides or join temporary teams."
Damian looked toward one of the screens showing a map of the surrounding region. "So this place holds everything a newcomer needs to avoid dying blindly."
Anna nodded. "Exactly. Though the free information only covers the basics. Anything valuable requires marks."
Revona smiled faintly. "Naturally."

Anna continued, "Information’s one of the most expensive things in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage. Good information can save your life, lead you to an opportunity, or help you dodge a trap. Bad information can kill you faster than an enemy’s blade."
Max’s gaze moved across the hall. He spotted one counter marked Basic Newcomer Knowledge. Another was marked Outer Layer Maps. Farther off, a larger platform displayed Bloodstone City Rankings.
A separate area seemed to sell information about nearby ruins, while another section was surrounded by participants scanning team recruitment notices.

Anna said, "Since all three of you are new, you should grab the basic information package first. It covers the outer layer, city rules, mark usage, common dangers, and how to dodge the most obvious traps. After that, you can decide what specific information you want to buy."

Daniel added calmly, "Don’t spend your marks carelessly. Newcomers usually waste their first marks on stuff that sounds impressive but ends up useless. Buy what helps you survive first. Opportunities come later."
Max glanced at him and nodded.
The devil he’d captured had already told him a lot, but compared to the scale of information inside this hall, that devil’s knowledge was clearly limited.
If Max wanted to properly understand the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, especially the path to the inner layer, the core layer, and anything tied to the Eternal Body, he needed more reliable sources.

As they moved deeper into the Information Hall, more gazes fell on Max. This time, he could feel the curiosity more clearly. A Law Manifestation Realm cultivator entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was just too unusual.

Even with Daniel beside him, people couldn’t help but stare. Some Primordials frowned in confusion. Several devils sneered from a distance. A few angels glanced at him with cold indifference, while one or two Dragon Race geniuses looked like they were trying to sense whether his weak realm hid something unusual underneath.
Max ignored all of it, keeping his eyes calm as he looked toward the information counters ahead.
Most of the basic information displayed inside the Information Hall had already been explained to Max by the devil he’d captured earlier. Even so, Max didn’t skip over it.

The devil had been terrified while speaking, and fear usually made people more honest, but Max wasn’t careless enough to take everything at face value without checking. This was the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, a place where information could mean the difference between life and death.
If the devil had hidden something, twisted something, or deliberately left out an important detail, Max needed to know before it caused him trouble later.

So he carefully read through the newcomer information package. The outer layer. The inner layer. The core layer. The five grades of marks. Bloodstone City’s basic rules. The common dangers outside the city. The role of Information Halls, exchange halls, trial grounds, and race bases.

After a few minutes, Max confirmed that most of what the devil had told him checked out. No obvious lies, at least not in what he’d already shared. Bloodstone City really was one of the outer layer cities.
Open killing inside the city really was restricted by the city’s own rules. Marks really did serve as the main currency, status symbol, and proof of achievement in the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
The outer layer really was filled mostly with Divine Lord Realm participants, while the inner layer really was dominated by Divine King Realm geniuses.

chapters.title: Chapter 2045: Ascension Seals!
paragraphs: Max’s expression stayed calm as he kept reading. Then his eyes suddenly stopped. One title caught his attention.
Ascension Seals.
Max narrowed his eyes slightly. This was the first time he’d seen that term since entering the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.

The devil had explained marks in great detail, and had talked about Bloodstone City, the outer layer, the inner layer, and the core layer, but he’d never once mentioned Ascension Seals. Whether that came from ignorance or a deliberate dodge, Max couldn’t say yet.
Curious, Max opened the information entry and started reading. A few minutes later, he finally understood why entering the inner layer was so hard.

To enter the inner layer, a participant needed something called an Ascension Seal. Only one Ascension Seal was required. At first glance, that sounded simple. But the real difficulty lay in getting one.

Ascension Seals ranked among the rarest things in the outer layer. Unlike marks, you couldn’t earn them by killing beasts, completing ordinary tasks, robbing other participants, or exchanging resources in cities.
They never showed up randomly in shops, and no one could buy them through normal mark transactions. Even powerful factions in the outer layer couldn’t produce them on demand.
There was only one known way to get an Ascension Seal.
The Ascension Trial.
Every few years, the Ascension Trial would descend somewhere in the outer layer. Its location was never fixed, and once it appeared, word of it would spread through the cities like wildfire.

Nearly every powerful genius in the outer layer would rush toward it, because the Ascension Trial was the only recognized path to obtain an Ascension Seal and earn the right to step into the inner layer.
Max kept reading, and his expression finally shifted slightly. Every time the Ascension Trial descended, it carried only ten Ascension Seals.
Ten. That number sounded almost absurdly small.

Max slowly leaned back and looked at the glowing information screen in front of him. The outer layer stretched enormous. It held many cities like Bloodstone City, countless wilderness regions, beast territories, ruins, trial grounds, and race bases.
Every time the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage opened, geniuses from all five universes poured in. Some stayed for years. Some stayed for decades. Some never managed to leave the outer layer at all.
If Max’s math was right, the number of participants in the outer layer could easily surpass one or two million. Yet every few years, only ten Ascension Seals showed up.
No wonder Anna had said that out of every thousand people, maybe only ten had a real shot at entering the inner layer. Honestly, even that estimate might have been generous.

The Ascension Trial wasn’t merely a trial. It was a bloodbath. When only ten seals appeared in front of countless geniuses who’d spent years struggling in the outer layer, the competition couldn’t stay peaceful.

Every genius who wanted to advance would fight for them. Every race would send its strongest outer layer participants. Every hidden expert’s disciple, every Primordial, every devil, every angel, every dragon, and every spirit confident enough would gather around the trial.
Those ten seals weren’t opportunities handed out to the talented. They were prizes that had to be ripped away from a battlefield.
Max’s gaze deepened. Now he understood why so many participants stayed stuck in the outer layer despite already reaching the 8th, 9th, or even 10th level of the Divine Lord Realm.

Their cultivation might be strong enough to survive here, but survival alone wasn’t enough to enter the inner layer. They needed an Ascension Seal, and getting one meant beating countless opponents who were just as desperate, just as prepared, and often far more experienced.
The difficulty was terrifying.

For most participants, the outer layer wasn’t a temporary stop before the real pilgrimage began. It was a cage. A massive cage filled with marks, trials, beasts, cities, and endless competition, where only a tiny number of people could ever break through the ceiling and move forward.

To Max, the outer layer was starting to feel less like a simple starting region and more like an enormous filter. It was a place built to throw countless geniuses from all five universes into danger, pressure, competition, and uncertainty.

Those who lacked strength would die. Those who lacked caution would get hunted down. Those who lacked persistence would stay trapped here for years. Only a very small number, those strong enough to seize Ascension Seals away from countless rivals, would ever get to step into the inner layer.
The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage wasn’t guiding geniuses forward gently. It was forcing them to prove they deserved to move forward at all.
After reading about the Ascension Seals, Max shifted his attention to another section of the information screen.
Bloodstone City Rankings.

The ranking only recorded the top one hundred geniuses in Bloodstone City. Beside each name sat the race or faction they belonged to, which made the list more than just a measure of individual strength. It also revealed the balance of power within the city.
Max’s gaze moved down the names slowly. Soon he spotted Daniel’s. Daniel sat at seventh, and beside his name was written one word.
Primordial.
Max wasn’t surprised. Damian and Revona had already reacted strongly when Anna mentioned Daniel, and now Max understood why.

Ranking seventh in a city where geniuses from all five universes gathered was no small feat. It meant Daniel wasn’t just strong among Primordials. He was one of the strongest figures in Bloodstone City overall.
Max kept reading.

First place belonged to Greyon of the Dragon Race. Second place belonged to Hemilin of the Angel Race. Third place belonged to Raymond of the Primordial Race. Fourth place belonged to Drevor of the Devil Race. Fifth place belonged to Shreya of the Spirit Race.
Looking at the top five, Max got a clearer picture of the power structure in Bloodstone City. Each of the five great races had at least one terrifying genius near the peak of the rankings.

The Dragon Race held first, the Angel Race held second, the Primordial Race held third, the Devil Race held fourth, and the Spirit Race held fifth. Just from that lineup alone, it was clear no single race completely dominated Bloodstone City.
The balance here ran delicate. Every race had powerful representatives. Every race carried enough strength to keep the others cautious.

Max’s eyes moved further down the list. As expected, the five great races took up many of the higher spots. Primordials, devils, angels, dragons, and spirits kept appearing throughout the ranking, proving they were the main powers of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage.
Their bloodlines, inheritances, bodies, souls, and foundations gave them an edge most other races couldn’t easily match.

But they weren’t the only ones on the list. Max also spotted humans. He saw elves. He saw demons. He saw names belonging to other lesser races he’d never even heard of before. Some ranked low, but a few had climbed surprisingly high. That made Max’s eyes sharpen slightly.

The five great races dominated, sure, but the so-called lesser races weren’t without their own monsters. Any genius who could force their way onto the Bloodstone City Rankings while competing against the five great races couldn’t be ordinary.
That realization made Max take the list a lot more seriously. The Bloodstone City Rankings weren’t just some display of fame.

They were a warning. Every name on that list belonged to someone who’d survived the outer layer, built up enough strength, beaten enough opponents, and earned enough recognition to be feared or respected in Bloodstone City.
Some of them were enemies. Some might turn into temporary allies. Some would stay neutral unless there was something in it for them. But none of them deserved to be underestimated.

chapters.title: Chapter 2046: Battle Space!
paragraphs: "Did you understand everything?"
Anna’s voice came from behind just as Max finished looking through the Bloodstone City Rankings.
Max turned around and saw her walking toward him with Daniel, Damian, and Revona nearby. He nodded calmly. "Almost."
Anna grinned, like she’d already expected that answer. "So do you get now why I said entering the inner layer is so hard?"

Max glanced back at the information screen for a moment before nodding. "I knew it wouldn’t be easy, but I honestly didn’t expect the difficulty to run this high. Guess I underestimated the outer layer."

"You’re not the first newcomer to think that way," Anna said. "Most people assume the outer layer’s just a starting region, but after they stick around for a while, they realize this place alone is enough to trap countless geniuses."
"You two talking about Ascension Seals?" Damian asked as he walked over.
Anna nodded. "Yeah."
Damian’s expression turned solemn. "I read about them too." He looked at Max and continued in a heavier tone. "From the looks of it, we might end up stuck in the outer layer for a couple of years."

Max nodded lightly, though his thoughts ran differently. He had no intention of settling down here like most people. The Godslayer’s Pilgrimage was dangerous, and the outer layer clearly held plenty of opportunities, but wasting years here wasn’t something he could accept.

They only had five hundred years before the final war with the devils, and next to a threat that size, even five hundred years didn’t stretch far. If he wanted the Eternal Body, if he wanted to uncover the deeper secrets of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, and if he wanted to grow strong enough to shape the coming battlefield, he needed to reach the inner layer as fast as possible.
After that, he needed to get into the core layer too.
Staying in the outer layer for years just because everyone else considered it normal would be foolish.

A moment later, Revona came back too. Unlike Damian, she wore a bright smile, a faint excitement showing in her eyes. Before anyone could ask where she’d gone, she raised her wrist toward Max and Damian.
"Look what I got."
The bronze mark on her wrist glowed faintly. Inside the glow, a number showed clearly.
Three hundred and twenty-five.
Damian’s eyes shifted slightly. "Did you get those from the Battle Space?"
Revona nodded, clearly satisfied. "Yeah. Didn’t expect the Battle Space to allow mark betting, but it does. Fought a few matches, and the other side underestimated me badly."

Anna smiled hearing that. "The Battle Space is one of the most popular spots in every outer layer city. It’s also the only area inside the cities where people can fight freely without breaking city rules."
Max looked at her.

Anna explained patiently, "The Battle Space gets built through extremely powerful virtual runes and spatial formations. When someone enters, their real body stays safe, while their consciousness and battle projection show up inside the arena. Because of that, even if you kill your opponent inside the Battle Space, or your opponent kills you, neither side actually dies."
Damian’s interest sharpened. "So it lets people fight without holding back."

"Exactly," Anna said. "That’s why so many geniuses use it to test their strength, drill their techniques, and challenge opponents from other races. Outside the city, one mistake can cost you your life. Inside the Battle Space, a mistake only costs you the marks you wagered."
Revona smiled. "That’s what makes it useful."

Anna nodded. "There’s another important point too. The Battle Spaces across all the outer layer cities are connected. If you enter the Battle Space in Bloodstone City, you might run into someone from a completely different city. You’re not limited to opponents in this city alone."
Max’s eyes moved slightly. "So the Battle Space connects the whole outer layer?"

"Only the outer layer," Anna corrected. "The inner layer runs its own system, and the outer layer Battle Space can’t connect to it. But among outer layer cities, yeah, the Battle Spaces link up. That’s part of why rankings and reputations spread so fast. If someone performs too well inside the Battle Space, people from a bunch of cities might hear about it."

Max nodded slowly. He’d already read a brief description of the Battle Space in the information package, but he hadn’t paid it much attention at first. He’d seen plenty of illusion worlds, virtual arenas, and projection spaces before, so the concept itself didn’t surprise him. What genuinely interested him was the mark betting.

In the Battle Space, people couldn’t fight casually with nothing on the line. They had to bet marks. That single rule made every battle mean something. Win, and you gained marks without risking your life.
Lose, and you paid the price. For ordinary participants, that made the Battle Space a place of both opportunity and danger. For Max, it might turn out even more useful than he’d first thought.

His cultivation realm sat only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm. To almost everyone in the outer layer, that realm made him look weak. Honestly, it made him look like the easiest prey in the city.
Max could already picture what would happen if he walked into the Battle Space openly. Devils, dragons, angels, spirits, and maybe even some Primordials would come forward to challenge him.
To them, Max would look like free marks. But to Max, they’d be the same thing.
’It’s a good way to earn marks,’ Max thought calmly. A faint light passed through his eyes.

The Battle Space could turn into a perfect hunting ground for him. His true strength couldn’t be measured by his cultivation realm alone, and that made him extremely dangerous in a place where opponents judged people purely by numbers.
If others wanted to underestimate him, he’d let them. If they wanted to challenge him, he’d accept. If they wanted to hand him marks with their own hands, he had no reason to say no.
Anna noticed the look in his eyes and immediately narrowed her own. "Max, why do I suddenly get the feeling you’re thinking of something troublesome?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2047: Bregor
paragraphs: Max looked at her with an innocent expression. "I’m just thinking the Battle Space sounds useful."
Daniel, who’d been listening quietly nearby, suddenly smiled. "It is useful. But only if you know what you’re doing."

Anna’s expression turned serious again. "Don’t rush into it blindly. The Battle Space might not kill you, but it can expose you. If you show too much of your strength there, people outside will start paying attention."

Max understood exactly what she meant. The Battle Space protected life, but it didn’t protect secrets. Every technique he used, every power he revealed, every victory he earned could turn into information other people would buy, sell, and study.
In a place like the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, showing strength carelessly could get just as dangerous as showing weakness.
Still, the opportunity was real.
Just then, Daniel walked back toward them, his gaze moving across Max, Damian, Revona, and Anna before he spoke. "They done?"
Anna nodded. "I think they’ve got the basics now."
"Good," Daniel said. "Then it’s time to move."
"Move?"
A cold sneer suddenly came from behind them.
Max and the others turned around at the same time.

A group of Dragon Race geniuses had shown up, blocking the path leading out of the Information Hall. There were several of them, all in humanoid form, though their dragon traits were impossible to miss. Scales covered their arms, necks, and parts of their faces like natural armor.

Some had curved horns rising from their heads, while others had long tails swaying behind them with a slow, dangerous rhythm. Their eyes were sharp and vertical, carrying the natural arrogance of ancient beasts who believed their bodies alone could suppress most opponents.

The one standing at the front gave off a particularly oppressive presence. His body stood tall and broad, dark bronze scales covering one side of his neck before spreading down toward his shoulder. His pupils were golden, his arms crossed over his chest, and his expression carried a lazy arrogance that made it obvious he wasn’t here for friendly conversation.
"Daniel," the Dragon Race genius said, his gaze sweeping across Max, Damian, and Revona. "These the three Primordial newcomers who came in this time?"
Daniel’s expression stayed calm. "What about them, Bregor?"
’Bregor?’ Max’s eyes narrowed slightly at the name. He’d seen that name not long ago on the Bloodstone City Rankings. Bregor sat ranked eighth. Only one spot below Daniel.

That meant the dragon standing in front of them was one of the strongest figures in Bloodstone City. No wonder he’d dared to block Daniel’s group inside the Information Hall so openly. Even without attacking directly, his presence alone was enough to draw a crowd.
Some nearby participants slowed their steps. A few devils stopped watching the information screens and turned around with amused expressions.

Several angels glanced over with faint interest, while some Spirit Race members quietly stepped aside, clearly unwilling to get involved but curious enough to watch. In a place like Bloodstone City, a confrontation between the seventh and eighth ranked geniuses was enough to draw attention even without a fight breaking out.
Bregor smiled, showing sharp teeth. "Nothing much. Was just thinking that since both our races got newcomers this time, why not make things a little interesting?"
Daniel looked at him silently.

Bregor gestured toward the four Dragon Race newcomers behind him. "How about we bet some marks on whose newcomers are better? Just your Primordial Race and my Dragon Race. Newcomers against newcomers. Should be fair enough."

Daniel didn’t answer right away. His gaze moved toward the four Dragon Race newcomers. All four sat at the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm. Their cultivation clearly ran much higher than Max’s, and their dragon bloodline gave them naturally powerful bodies.
Against ordinary geniuses, any one of them would be extremely hard to deal with. But Damian and Revona weren’t ordinary either, and Max was an even stranger case.
After a moment, Daniel nodded. "Sure."
Anna looked at him, a little surprised.
Daniel continued calmly, "But our Primordial side only has three newcomers here, so we don’t need four battles. We’ll do three matches. Whichever side wins two takes the bet."
Bregor’s smile widened. "Daniel, no wonder even some members of the Dragon Race respect you. You really do have nerve."
Daniel’s expression didn’t change. "Bregor, we both know a small number of marks won’t help or hurt either of us much. If I win, it’s a bit of extra gain. If I lose, it won’t touch me."
"You really are strange," Bregor said, shaking his head with a grin. "Most people would at least pretend to care."
"I only care when the amount’s actually worth caring about," Daniel replied.
Bregor laughed. "Fine. Since you’re so relaxed about it, let’s make it three hundred Gold Marks."

The moment those words landed, several people nearby reacted. Three hundred Gold Marks wasn’t a small amount. Even for top-ranked geniuses, that wasn’t something most people would toss around casually for entertainment.

It was enough to buy valuable information, powerful resources, high-grade cultivation rooms, and access to plenty of special places in the outer layer. For newcomers, the value felt even more terrifying.
Anna’s brows furrowed slightly. Damian and Revona turned serious too.
Daniel, though, just looked at Bregor calmly.

Bregor continued, "If my Dragon Race newcomers win two out of three matches, I get three hundred Gold Marks from you. If your Primordial newcomers win two out of three, you get three hundred Gold Marks from me."
"Fine by me," Daniel said with a faint smile.
Bregor’s eyes flashed with satisfaction.
Daniel then turned to Anna, Max, Damian, and Revona. His gaze stayed calm, but a faint hint of interest showed through. "So, how about it? You three willing to take the challenge?"
Before Damian or Revona could speak, Max smiled. "Sure," Max said calmly. "It’ll be an easy win on my side."
For a moment, the air around them seemed to go quiet.
Anna stared at him.
Daniel looked at him in silence too.
Even Damian’s lips twitched slightly, while Revona blinked, like she was wondering if Max had actually just said that in front of Bregor and the Dragon Race newcomers.
