If you show too much of your strength there, people outside will start paying attention."
Max understood exactly what she meant.
The Battle Space protected life, but it didn’t protect secrets.
Every technique he used, every power he revealed, every victory he earned could turn into information other people would buy, sell, and study.
In a place like the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, showing strength carelessly could get just as dangerous as showing weakness.
Still, the opportunity was real.
Just then, Daniel walked back toward them, his gaze moving across Max, Damian, Revona, and Anna before he spoke.
"They done?"
Anna nodded.
"I think they’ve got the basics now."
"Good," Daniel said.
"Then it’s time to move."
"Move?"
A cold sneer suddenly came from behind them.
Max and the others turned around at the same time.
A group of Dragon Race geniuses had shown up, blocking the path leading out of the Information Hall.
There were several of them, all in humanoid form, though their dragon traits were impossible to miss.
Scales covered their arms, necks, and parts of their faces like natural armor.
Some had curved horns rising from their heads, while others had long tails swaying behind them with a slow, dangerous rhythm.
Their eyes were sharp and vertical, carrying the natural arrogance of ancient beasts who believed their bodies alone could suppress most opponents.
The one standing at the front gave off a particularly oppressive presence.
His body stood tall and broad, dark bronze scales covering one side of his neck before spreading down toward his shoulder.
His pupils were golden, his arms crossed over his chest, and his expression carried a lazy arrogance that made it obvious he wasn’t here for friendly conversation.
"Daniel," the Dragon Race genius said, his gaze sweeping across Max, Damian, and Revona.
"These the three Primordial newcomers who came in this time?"
Daniel’s expression stayed calm.
"What about them, Bregor?"
’Bregor?’ Max’s eyes narrowed slightly at the name.
He’d seen that name not long ago on the Bloodstone City Rankings.
Bregor sat ranked eighth.
Only one spot below Daniel.
That meant the dragon standing in front of them was one of the strongest figures in Bloodstone City.
No wonder he’d dared to block Daniel’s group inside the Information Hall so openly.
Even without attacking directly, his presence alone was enough to draw a crowd.
Some nearby participants slowed their steps.
A few devils stopped watching the information screens and turned around with amused expressions.
Several angels glanced over with faint interest, while some Spirit Race members quietly stepped aside, clearly unwilling to get involved but curious enough to watch.
In a place like Bloodstone City, a confrontation between the seventh and eighth ranked geniuses was enough to draw attention even without a fight breaking out.
Bregor smiled, showing sharp teeth.
"Nothing much.
Was just thinking that since both our races got newcomers this time, why not make things a little interesting?"
Daniel looked at him silently.
Bregor gestured toward the four Dragon Race newcomers behind him.
"How about we bet some marks on whose newcomers are better?
Just your Primordial Race and my Dragon Race.
Newcomers against newcomers.
Should be fair enough."
Daniel didn’t answer right away.
His gaze moved toward the four Dragon Race newcomers.
All four sat at the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm.
Their cultivation clearly ran much higher than Max’s, and their dragon bloodline gave them naturally powerful bodies.
Against ordinary geniuses, any one of them would be extremely hard to deal with.
But Damian and Revona weren’t ordinary either, and Max was an even stranger case.
After a moment, Daniel nodded.
"Sure."
Anna looked at him, a little surprised.
Daniel continued calmly, "But our Primordial side only has three newcomers here, so we don’t need four battles.
We’ll do three matches.
Whichever side wins two takes the bet."
Bregor’s smile widened.
"Daniel, no wonder even some members of the Dragon Race respect you.
You really do have nerve."
Daniel’s expression didn’t change.
"Bregor, we both know a small number of marks won’t help or hurt either of us much.
If I win, it’s a bit of extra gain.
If I lose, it won’t touch me."
"You really are strange," Bregor said, shaking his head with a grin.
"Most people would at least pretend to care."
"I only care when the amount’s actually worth caring about," Daniel replied.
Bregor laughed.
"Fine.
Since you’re so relaxed about it, let’s make it three hundred Gold Marks."
The moment those words landed, several people nearby reacted.
Three hundred Gold Marks wasn’t a small amount.
Even for top-ranked geniuses, that wasn’t something most people would toss around casually for entertainment.
It was enough to buy valuable information, powerful resources, high-grade cultivation rooms, and access to plenty of special places in the outer layer.
For newcomers, the value felt even more terrifying.
Anna’s brows furrowed slightly.
Damian and Revona turned serious too.
Daniel, though, just looked at Bregor calmly.
Bregor continued, "If my Dragon Race newcomers win two out of three matches, I get three hundred Gold Marks from you.
If your Primordial newcomers win two out of three, you get three hundred Gold Marks from me."
"Fine by me," Daniel said with a faint smile.
Bregor’s eyes flashed with satisfaction.
Daniel then turned to Anna, Max, Damian, and Revona.
His gaze stayed calm, but a faint hint of interest showed through.
"So, how about it?
You three willing to take the challenge?"
Before Damian or Revona could speak, Max smiled.
"Sure," Max said calmly.
"It’ll be an easy win on my side."
For a moment, the air around them seemed to go quiet.
Anna stared at him.
Daniel looked at him in silence too.
Even Damian’s lips twitched slightly, while Revona blinked, like she was wondering if Max had actually just said that in front of Bregor and the Dragon Race newcomers.

chapters.title: Chapter 2048: Anna’s Advice!
paragraphs: Anna finally snapped out of it and turned to Max with a stern look. "What do you mean, easy win?"
Max looked at her innocently. "Exactly what I said."

Anna’s expression turned even more helpless. "All four of them sit at the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm, and you’re only at the 1st level of the Law Manifestation Realm. Where’s this confidence even coming from?"
Max didn’t answer.
Anna pointed at Damian and Revona. "Only Damian and Revona fight first. Let’s hope they win their matches so you don’t even have to fight."
Max smiled wryly. "As you say."

Damian couldn’t help but smile seeing Max’s expression. He wasn’t sure whether Anna genuinely didn’t know Max’s real strength or was just too worried because of the realm gap, but Damian knew well enough that Max couldn’t be judged by cultivation alone.
Still, he didn’t explain anything. In a place like the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, the fewer people who understood Max’s true ability, the better.
Bregor looked at Max with clear amusement in his eyes.

"A Law Manifestation Realm newcomer calling a battle against the Dragon Race an easy win," he said with a low laugh. "Interesting. I knew Primordials were arrogant, but I didn’t know they’d gotten this entertaining."
The Dragon Race newcomers behind him laughed too.
One of them looked at Max with contempt. "If he’s allowed to fight, I want him."
Another dragon grinned. "No, let me take him. I’ve never crushed a Law Manifestation Realm participant in the Battle Space before."
The third dragon shook his head and said mockingly, "Calling it a fight would be generous. It’ll be over before he even understands what happened."
Max listened quietly. His expression didn’t change.
Daniel glanced at him from the corner of his eye, and for some reason, that calmness on Max’s face left him a bit curious.

Most Law Manifestation Realm cultivators would’ve felt humiliated, scared, or angry under that kind of ridicule, especially facing Divine Lord Realm dragons. Max just stood there like he’d overheard a couple of kids arguing over a toy.
That calmness wasn’t simple.
Anna noticed it too, but she still sighed in frustration. "Just don’t cause trouble before we even reach the Battle Space," she said.
Max nodded. "I’ll try."
Anna narrowed her eyes. "That answer doesn’t reassure me at all."
Revona covered a small smile, while Damian looked toward the Dragon Race newcomers with a sharper gaze. Since the challenge had already been accepted, there was no point dodging it now.
They were all new to the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage, but if they backed down right after entering Bloodstone City, their reputations would take a hit before they even got a chance to build one.
Daniel looked back at Bregor. "Bet’s settled. Let’s head to the Battle Space."
Bregor smiled widely. "Good. Hope your newcomers are as confident as that Law Manifestation Realm brat."
Daniel didn’t respond to the jab. He just turned and started walking.

Anna followed beside Max, still wearing the look of someone bracing for a headache. Damian and Revona walked behind them, both more serious than before. Bregor and the Dragon Race group followed with relaxed confidence, their mocking glances occasionally landing on Max, like they’d already decided he was the weak point of the Primordial side.

As they left the Information Hall, more and more people started noticing the movement. A bet between Daniel and Bregor wasn’t a small deal in Bloodstone City. Both of them sat in the top ten of the Bloodstone City Rankings, and their names carried real weight among the geniuses of the outer layer.

Daniel represented the Primordial side, while Bregor stood as one of the strongest Dragon Race figures stationed in the city. If ordinary participants placed a wager in the Battle Space, only a handful of curious people would bother watching.
But when two top-ranked geniuses decided to gamble three hundred Gold Marks on a battle between newcomers, the news spread through Bloodstone City almost instantly.

At first, only the people inside the Information Hall heard about it. Then the news hit the nearby streets. After that, it spread to the mark exchange halls, cultivation chambers, race bases, inns, weapon shops, and trial recruitment areas.
Before long, plenty of people knew Daniel and Bregor had made a bet, and that the Primordial newcomers would fight the Dragon Race newcomers in the Battle Space.

The amount involved made people even more interested. Three hundred Gold Marks wasn’t something ordinary participants could shrug off. Even for high-level Divine Lord Realm geniuses, it counted as a serious sum.

For newcomers, it felt almost unimaginable. A lot of people quickly realized this wasn’t just a casual contest between young participants. This was a public test between two races, and the result would shape how the newest batch of Primordial and Dragon Race geniuses got viewed in Bloodstone City.
By the time Daniel, Anna, Max, Damian, and Revona reached the Battle Space with Bregor and the Dragon Race newcomers, the area was already packed.

The Battle Space building stood enormous, shaped like a circular fortress at the center of a wide plaza, its walls built from black stone and carved with countless silver runes. Those runes pulsed with light, creating a faint barrier that wrapped around the entire structure.

Above the entrance, a massive projection floated in the air, showing ongoing battles between participants from different cities across the outer layer. Every strike, every movement, every win, and every loss showed up clearly for the crowd outside to watch.

People from all five races had gathered. Primordials stood in groups near one side of the plaza, their expressions calm but attentive. Devils watched with cold smiles, clearly hoping to see one side get humiliated.

Spirit Race members floated or stood quietly near the edges, their luminous eyes filled with curiosity. Angels gathered in elegant silence, golden halos glowing above their heads as they watched the arriving groups with unreadable expressions.
Dragon Race participants stood with their arms folded, scales gleaming under the strange light of the city as they looked toward Bregor’s group with open confidence.

chapters.title: Chapter 2049: Arrival of Shreya!
paragraphs: Humans, elves, demons, and several lesser races mixed into the crowd too. Some had come purely for entertainment. Some had come to size up the newcomers’ strength. Some had come because Daniel and Bregor’s names were involved.
And some had come because they understood that information gathered from watching a battle like this could turn useful later.
Max’s gaze swept across the plaza, and he immediately noticed the crowd wasn’t made up only of ordinary participants. Several powerful auras hid among them, restrained but impossible to overlook.
These weren’t newcomers, and they weren’t simple spectators either. Their presence felt stable, deep, and dangerous.

Some stood quietly on balconies overlooking the Battle Space. Some sat in private viewing areas behind translucent formation screens. Some watched from the upper floors of nearby buildings, their eyes fixed on Daniel, Bregor, and the six newcomers about to fight.
Anna noticed Max looking around and lowered her voice. "This bet drew more attention than I expected."

Daniel glanced toward one of the upper balconies and smiled faintly. "Not surprising. Bregor and I both sit in the top ten. Even if we’re not fighting ourselves, people still want to see what kind of newcomers our sides pulled in this time."
Damian’s expression turned more serious. "Those people up there aren’t ordinary."

"They’re not," Daniel said calmly. "Some are high-level figures from the race bases. Some are information brokers. Some are connected to the Bloodstone City Rankings. A few might even represent the stronger factions in the outer layer."

Just as Daniel finished speaking, a soft commotion suddenly spread from the far side of the plaza. The noise wasn’t loud at first, but it moved through the crowd fast, like a ripple crossing still water.

Several Spirit Race members standing near the edge of the Battle Space turned at the same time. The devils who’d been sneering went quieter. Even some Dragon Race geniuses shifted their gazes, and the angels standing beneath their golden halos looked toward the same direction with visible interest.
A woman from the Spirit Race walked into the plaza.

She stood in humanoid form, but her presence instantly set her apart from the ordinary spirits around her. Her long emerald hair flowed behind her like strands of living silk, and faint golden-green light moved across her skin in patterns resembling vines, leaves, and ancient runes.

Her eyes were clear and deep, carrying the calm of an old forest and the sharpness of a blade hidden beneath flowers. Every step she took landed light, yet the natural energy around her seemed to bend toward her willingly, as if the world itself recognized her.
Someone in the crowd drew in a sharp breath.
"Shreya."
"The fifth-ranked genius on the Bloodstone City Rankings actually showed up."
"She rarely watches newcomer battles. Why’s she here?"
The name spread through the plaza almost instantly.

Shreya. Ranked fifth on the Bloodstone City Rankings. A top genius of the Spirit Race. Her arrival shocked a lot of people, since someone at her level wouldn’t usually bother with a small battle between newcomers.

Even with Daniel and Bregor involved, this was still just a wager between their younger members. Yet Shreya had shown up in person, and that alone shifted the mood. The crowd stopped treating the event as simple entertainment. If the fifth-ranked genius had come to watch, this match clearly carried more weight than most people had first assumed.
Bregor’s eyes narrowed slightly when he saw her, but his smile didn’t fade.
Daniel looked toward Shreya too and gave a small nod from a distance.

Shreya returned the nod calmly, then moved to one of the raised viewing platforms beside the Battle Space. She didn’t speak, and she didn’t explain why she’d come. She just stood there, her gaze passing over Daniel, Bregor, Damian, Revona, and finally Max.
For a brief moment, her eyes paused on Max.

Max felt it clearly. Her gaze wasn’t mocking like the devils, and it wasn’t arrogant like the dragons. It came across quiet and searching, like she’d sensed something strange but hadn’t yet figured out what.
Then she looked away.
Anna’s expression turned even more serious. "Even Shreya came. This is getting troublesome."
Max glanced toward the Spirit Race woman. "She’s ranked fifth, right?"
"Yeah," Daniel answered calmly. "Shreya of the Spirit Race. She’s stronger than Bregor and me."

Max’s eyes moved slightly. That one sentence said enough. If Daniel admitted it so openly, Shreya’s strength wasn’t just a matter of ranking. She genuinely stood above both him and Bregor in Bloodstone City.

The crowd grew louder after her arrival. More people stopped to watch. More messages went out. More powerful figures turned their attention toward the Battle Space. What had started as a provocation inside the Information Hall had now turned into one of the most watched events in Bloodstone City that day.

Bregor walked to the front of the Battle Space entrance and looked back at Daniel with a wide grin. "Looks like everyone’s interested. Even Shreya decided to show up. Good. A bigger audience makes the bet more fun."
Daniel’s expression stayed relaxed. "It also makes losing more embarrassing."
Bregor laughed. "Then I hope your newcomers are ready."
"They are," Daniel said.
Above the Battle Space, the floating projection shifted, and a new notice appeared in bright golden letters.
[Primordial Universe Newcomers vs Dragon Race Newcomers.]
[Three battles.]
[Best of three.]
[Wager: Three hundred Gold Marks.]
The moment the notice appeared, the entire plaza stirred again.
Max looked up at the glowing words. A faint smile touched his lips.

To others, this was a dangerous public stage. To him, it was his first real chance to see how the Battle Space worked, earn some marks, and measure the strength of Dragon Race newcomers without risking his life.

If the Dragon Race wanted to use this battle to test the Primordial newcomers, he had no reason to refuse. Let them test. He wanted to know how far the so-called geniuses of the Godslayer’s Pilgrimage could actually go, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 2050: Virgil’s Bet!
paragraphs: As the excitement around the Battle Space kept rising, Daniel and Bregor walked to the registration platform and submitted the names of their three contestants.
The process was simple but solemn. Both of them placed their palms on the dark stone platform, and the bronze marks on their wrists lit up at the same time.

A moment later, several lines of light appeared in the air above the platform, recording the names of the participants, the races they represented, the number of battles, and the wager between the two sides.
Once registration wrapped up, the notice above the Battle Space glowed even brighter, and the crowd outside stirred again.
Daniel returned to Max, Damian, and Revona. His expression stayed calm as he looked at the three of them.
"Revona, you’re up first. Damian, you go second. Max, you fight last."
The three of them nodded.
Max didn’t object, though he quietly figured he might not even need to fight if Revona and Damian did well.
Both of them were geniuses chosen by the Primordial Race, and their strength wasn’t ordinary. If they won the first two battles, the third wouldn’t even matter.
Still, Max didn’t underestimate the Dragon Race. ’The Dragon Race isn’t something anyone should take lightly,’ Max thought.
He knew this better than most. After all, he himself carried the Black Dragon Chaotic Bloodline, and because of that, he understood how terrifying a true dragon body could be.

Even in humanoid form, Dragon Race members had monstrous vitality, overwhelming defenses, explosive strength, and instincts far sharper than ordinary cultivators. If Damian and Revona judged them only by cultivation level, they might take a loss before they even realized what happened.

Anna seemed to share the same worry. She stepped closer to the three of them and lowered her voice. "Listen carefully. Dragon Race members aren’t like ordinary opponents. Their bodies are their biggest advantage. Their scales can block attacks that would injure anyone else, their bloodline gives them powerful recovery, and their physical strength alone can suppress enemies before a technique even gets used."
Revona listened with a serious expression.
Damian focused on her words too.

Anna continued, "Don’t clash with them carelessly in close combat unless you’re confident in your own body. Their defense runs extremely strong, but that doesn’t mean they have no weaknesses. Their movements hit hard but land heavy when they lean on brute force, and a lot of dragons get arrogant because of their natural strength. Make them overextend. Go for the joints, eyes, throat, and anywhere their scales run thinner. If they push their transformation further, don’t just stand there and try to endure it. Keep moving."

Daniel added from the side, "Also keep in mind this is the Battle Space. You won’t actually die inside it, but the pain, pressure, and exhaustion will still feel real. Don’t relax just because it’s virtual. A lot of newcomers lose because they treat it like a game."
Revona smiled faintly. "Understood."
Damian nodded. "I’ll keep that in mind."
Max stayed silent, but his gaze drifted toward the Dragon Race side.
At that moment, one of the Dragon Race newcomers stepped forward. He stood tall and muscular, with dark green scales covering both arms and spreading up the side of his neck.

Two short horns curved from his forehead, and his golden vertical pupils carried a fierce confidence. His aura sat firmly at the 1st level of the Divine Lord Realm, and even among the four Dragon Race newcomers, his presence didn’t come off weak.
He looked toward the Primordial side and spoke loud enough for the crowd around him to hear. "I’m Virgil. I’ll fight first. Who’s my opponent?"
Revona stepped forward with a light smile. Her silver hair moved gently behind her, and her expression stayed composed even under the crowd’s pressure.
"That’d be me," she said. "I’m Revona."
Virgil studied her for a moment before nodding. "Revona, huh? Good."
Then a grin crossed his face. "Since we’re already fighting, how about we make it more interesting?"
Revona raised a brow. "What do you mean?"
"Let’s put a personal bet on our battle," Virgil said.
The crowd around them perked up immediately.
Revona didn’t refuse right away. "How much are you thinking?"
Virgil lifted his wrist, and the bronze mark on it glowed faintly. "Two hundred Bronze Marks."

Revona’s eyes widened slightly. Two hundred Bronze Marks wasn’t a small amount for a newcomer. Even though she’d just earned three hundred and twenty-five Bronze Marks from the Battle Space, risking two hundred of them on a single fight still counted as a bold move.
Damian showed a trace of surprise too, and even Max looked at Virgil with a bit more interest.
This dragon carried real confidence. Or maybe he was just arrogant.
Revona looked at him for a few breaths. Then she smiled.
"Fine," she said. "Don’t regret it later."
Virgil’s grin widened. "That should be my line."

The registration platform responded to their agreement right away. Two beams of bronze light dropped from the air and connected to the marks on their wrists. The numbers on both marks flickered briefly before the Battle Space itself recorded the wager.
A new line appeared on the floating notice above the arena.
[First Battle: Revona of the Primordial Universe against Virgil of the Dragon Race.]
[Personal Wager: Two hundred Bronze Marks.]

The crowd grew even louder. Some Primordials looked at Revona with hope. The Dragon Race members wore confident expressions, clearly believing Virgil’s win was already locked in. Devils sneered, ready to enjoy the show, while angels and spirits watched with quiet interest.
On the raised platform, Shreya’s luminous eyes shifted toward Revona and Virgil too, like she wanted to see if these newcomers were worth remembering.
Then the runes around the Battle Space began to shine. A circular formation opened beneath Revona’s feet. At almost the same moment, another formation appeared beneath Virgil.
Revona turned her head slightly and glanced once at Max and Damian, her smile still calm. "I’ll be back after I win."
Damian nodded. "Be careful."
Max looked at her and said, "Don’t underestimate his body."
"I know," Revona replied.
Virgil laughed from the other side. "You’ve still got time to worry about yourself."
